“Dr. Waldron,” the lady sitting across from me said. “I have been struggling a lot lately.”

“Tell me what’s going on,” I said.

“I don’t know how to explain it,” she hesitated… “I just feel tired most of the time. I can’t concentrate anymore, and I just don’t enjoy most of the things that I used to enjoy. I’m getting through my days, but that’s about it. Do you think I have a thyroid problem or am low in some mineral or vitamin?”

“That could be,” I told her. “We can certainly check those things, but I think something else is going on here.”

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

I am a family doctor and probably thirty percent of the people who come to my office to see me have symptoms of depression. This doesn’t mean that they are on medication for it or feel that they need special help, but it does say that these symptoms are widespread in our world.

Even in Christian circles, surveys indicate that about 15 percent of Christians self-report having been diagnosed with depression at some point in their life. This is 25 percent lower than in society as a whole, but it is still higher than we would like to believe.

In the very beginning, God created the world and Adam and Eve. And God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good… –Genesis 1:31. Before the Fall, everything was perfect.

I don’t think we know entirely what this meant. Obviously, there were no physical diseases or maladies to afflict either the humans or the flora and fauna of Eden. More than that, Adam and Eve didn’t suffer from anxiety or depression. Their hormones didn’t get out of balance, they didn’t get stressed out (even if there could have been stress in a perfect garden), and they wouldn’t have gotten upset or angry at any point.

Everything changed with Adam and Eve sinning. We see this in the tension between them after they ate the fruit with Adam blaming Eve, and Eve blaming the snake. And the man said, The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat. And the LORD God said unto the woman, What is this that thou hast done? And the woman said, The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat –Genesis 3:12-13.

Feeding a family suddenly became hard work. Viruses and bacteria became pathogenic and at some point, in the first families, people would have begun to struggle with emotional and mental health challenges.

Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee. And unto Adam he said, Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life; Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field; In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return –Genesis 3:16-19.

I would like to explore what depression is as defined by the medical world, some of the sources of it, and then discuss how we can deal with it, both in our own lives and in the lives of our friends and family.

Diagnosing Depression

As mentioned earlier, many people have some symptoms of depression. They may feel more fatigued, cry easily, or have other symptoms that aren’t usual for them. Most of them do not actually have true clinical depression.

Most people do not have all of these symptoms, but when they are continually present without dissipating for two weeks or more, especially if they are strong enough to hinder normal day-to-day responsibilities or the ability to get proper rest, then it is time to do something.

It is important to remember that there is a large or broad continuum regarding depression. Some people have mild discouragement, some have deep feelings of sadness, and some have enough depression that they are at risk to cause harm to themselves or others.

Causes of Depression

There are different examples of people in the Bible who seem to have exhibited symptoms consistent with depression. Two of them stand out to me.

First is Naomi. We know that she went with her husband and her two sons to Moab because of a famine that was affecting southern Israel. She spent ten years in this foreign land and during that time, her husband and both of her sons died.

The book of Ruth tells us that when she returned to Bethlehem, she said to the people, …Call me not Naomi [pleasant], call me Mara [bitter]: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me. I went out full, and the LORD hath brought me home again empty: why then call ye me Naomi, seeing the LORD hath testified against me, and the Almighty hath afflicted me? –Ruth 1:20-21.

There is no way to interview Naomi and find out all the things that she was feeling, but this seems to be more than simple grief. She had lost all the things that were of value to her, and to her it seemed that even God had turned against her.

As we read the story of Ruth, we see that things did improve for her throughout the book—mostly through the ministry of her daughter-in-law, Ruth, but also, through God gradually restoring things of value back into her life, and through others encouraging her in the Lord’s goodness. And the women said unto Naomi, Blessed be the LORD, which hath not left thee this day without a kinsman, that his name may be famous in Israel. And he shall be unto thee a restorer of thy life, and a nourisher of thine old age: for thy daughter in law, which loveth thee, which is better to thee than seven sons, hath born him. And Naomi took the child, and laid it in her bosom, and became nurse unto it –Ruth 4:14-16.

Another one that comes to mind is the Prophet Jeremiah. Jeremiah was called when he was a young man, and he had a very long career speaking God’s Word to a group of kings and other people who simply weren’t interested in what he had to say.

Jeremiah’s life was constantly under threat. At one time, he was thrown into a dungeon full of mud and was only rescued at the last minute. Jerusalem was besieged three different times before the Babylonians razed it. Through his decades of ministry, Jeremiah told the people what God was asking of them, and the people constantly ignored it.

Perhaps it is no wonder that Jeremiah is known today as the weeping prophet. He said, Cursed be the day wherein I was born: let not the day wherein my mother bare me be blessed. Cursed be the man who brought tidings to my father, saying, A man child is born unto thee; making him very glad. And let that man be as the cities which the LORD overthrew, and repented not: and let him hear the cry in the morning, and the shouting at noontide … Wherefore came I forth out of the womb to see labour and sorrow, that my days should be consumed with shame? –Jeremiah 20:14-18.

It is important to note that in both of these examples from the Bible, sin is not revealed to be the issue (or the reason) that pushed these people into depression. For Naomi it was probably a mixture of isolation from her homeland and loss of people she loved dearly. For Jeremiah, it was the constant stress of trying to serve God in a nation that didn’t care about God.

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

Depression is always multi-factorial. That is to say, there are usually a mixture of internal and external factors that break a person down.

There are genetic and hormonal components that come into play here. There is no doubt that some individuals and some families are more prone to depression than others. It is thought by many doctors and researchers that changes in genes which transport the chemical, Serotonin, through the brain can make some people more susceptible to depression than others.

These differences in genetic makeup can help us understand why some people require very little stress to bring them down, while others seem very resilient. Since we can’t change our genetic makeup, there is no sense gloating if we have a more upbeat personality than someone else. And, if we recognize that we have a greater tendency towards depression, we don’t need to feel discouraged by this fact. If God created us in such a way that we tend towards being moody instead of being naturally upbeat, we need to use wisdom in doing what we can to manage as many external factors as we can so as to minimize the risk of debilitating (extreme) depression.

External stressors are often the thing that triggers these sorts of feelings (discouragement). It can be the death of a close friend or family member, or it can be a financial misfortune. It is important to remember that even good events can produce large amounts of stress. Mothers with newborns are often functioning on very little sleep, even while they have large physical changes taking place in their bodies.

Some people may have poor coping skills. Unfortunately, many turn to street drugs or alcohol to try to smother the feelings that they can’t control otherwise.

As a final thing, sin and guilt can trigger depression or make it worse. We can see this present in David and Saul’s lives. (See Psalm chapter 32) This is not to say that all depression is the result of sin—far from it—but sin needs to be dealt with, and repented of, in order to move forward.

Perhaps as a side note, I will mention that in my experience, deeply depressed people often struggle with horrible guilt. They don’t even know what sin they might have committed; they are only certain that God is angry with them, and they must have done something wrong. Fixing the depression will help with the assurance of salvation issues that these people tend to deal with.

This leaves us with the question of how to help someone who is dealing with this sort of thinking.

Listen

Listening is a powerful tool for helping other people. Listen actively and without jumping in to interrupt negative thinking.

You may be able to see that all is not terrible and that there is much positive in the world. The fact that they can’t see these things has more to do with their mindset than with how terrible things really are. A person struggling with depression may know that there are people worse off in the world, but it doesn’t really help them much to point that out to them.

Encourage

Encouragement can simply be saying good things that you see in the life of the person who is struggling. This is something that all of us need more of.

More than this, we need to encourage people to do things that are healthy for themselves. They need to get out of their home, they should try to exercise, and they should make an attempt to eat healthy. We can help them do better in all of these areas. (See Galatians 6:2)

Pray

…The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much –James 5:16.

These people need someone to pray with them. They need someone to pray for them. Jesus asks us to pray in secret, but it is also really encouraging for someone who is struggling to hear themselves being prayed for. This helps them to know that there are many people who are lifting them up with prayer support.

Be Willing to be the Initiator

People with depression have very low energy levels. Beyond that, they don’t see themselves as having any value. At least such that someone else would want to spend time with them. They aren’t going to call or text, and they certainly won’t set up a lunch meeting or prayer time.

Even though they crave all of these things, it is just really difficult for them to take the first step to reach out to others. It therefore falls to the rest of us to be willing to do those things.

Don’t Jump to Conclusions

We know the story of Job’s friends. They rode up to see Job after disaster fell on him and sat quietly in shock for several days upon seeing the devastation that had happened to him. When they finally began to speak, it was to judge him for the terrible sin they assumed he had committed.

It isn’t wrong to ask about sin, but there are plenty of times where depression isn’t sin-related. Focusing in on sin prematurely, or if it is assumed, will simply drive wedges that will make it less likely that you can help a person find healing.

What if you are the person struggling with depression? How should you deal with it and what things can help?

Deal With Issues Early

Everyone has moments when they are stressed out and really discouraged. We use terms like “burn-out” and “compassion fatigue” in the medical field when people are heading in the wrong direction. These struggles manifest themselves when we are being irritable with the people around us, when we’re feeling tired most of the time, or when we’re feeling discouraged most of the time. When we see that these symptoms are popping up, it is time to do something to keep things from getting worse.

Maybe a first step is simply knowing our limitations. There are times where we will simply need to say no to work projects or even to church activities because it doesn’t leave us sufficient time to rest. Certain times of the year could be worse—many people struggle more during the winter months because of less sunlight.

Cutting back in whatever areas we can is important when we see that we are on the wrong trajectory.

Don’t Do Comparisons

Everyone is different. Identifying people who seem to “have it altogether” when you are struggling doesn’t help you and it probably will make you feel worse.

Struggling with discouragement does not mean that you aren’t a Christian or that God is done with you. It means that you are human living in a fallen world. You don’t want to continue to live with a depressed spirit, but neither should you believe that you are the only one who has dealt with this. (See 2 Corinthians 10:12)

Exercise

Cardiovascular exercise is really important to boost the chemicals in the brain that are associated with depression. It doesn’t really matter what type of exercise you do. What does matter, is that it increases your heart rate 25 to 30 percent above your baseline heart rate.

Exercise is something that is hard to do, even when you aren’t dealing with depression. It is particularly hard when you are fatigued and feeling down.

Spend Time with Encouragers

People need community. When we are dealing with depressive feelings, we really need other people around to lift us up, to pray with us, and to give us encouragement. None of us is better from spending extended times alone. (See Proverbs 27:17)

Deal with Sin

Sin can make prayer feel ineffective. That isn’t to say that simply confessing sin will suddenly make someone’s depression lift, but it is an important part of reaching healing. Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed… –James 5:16.

Be Willing to Take Medication

Not everyone needs medication. The hope is that if you do the right (helpful) things (some of which are listed above), you can keep things from getting bad enough that you would need medical help. But there are plenty of situations where someone simply needs to start on some medication in order to aid them in a number of ways: to sleep, to rest a weary mind that will not stop, to dull the emotional pain, etc.

People with severe enough depression may be a risk to themselves. They may even be completely unable to respond to counseling or any of the other non-medical treatments for these feelings. These people really need to start on medication with the goal to transition off of those medications down the road when they are thinking clearly enough to continue on the right path.

Unfortunately, the benefits of these medications seem to be short-lived. Long-term use of antidepressant medications really does not seem to improve quality of life for many patients. A recent study looked at patients who took antidepressant medications and compared them to those who did not and found similar levels of health-related quality of life in the two groups. In other words, when comparing two groups of depressed patients, with the one group taking medication and the other group not, after a period of time (approximately 6 months) there were no longer any observable differences in their depression levels. So, while these medications may help to stabilize a person who has severe depression, after a period of time the actual medical “help” of the medication starts to diminish. Hopefully, by this time, the person will be stable enough that a safe taper can be taken towards weaning off the medication.

With this in mind, it is very important to do things other than medication to attempt to improve the situation.

Continue, Even When You Feel Better

Many times, when someone has a medical issue, they will consciously change their diet and lifestyle to improve their situation. The problem is that when the symptoms get better, the tendency is to fall back into old eating and behavioral patterns.

If you have dealt with depression in the past, it is important that you continue a path of healthy choices. Exercise regularly, eat healthy meals, manage your stress level (as much as you can), don’t over-schedule, and make a conscious effort to meet regularly with godly friends for times of prayer and support.

Periodically take an inventory of how you are doing. If you are struggling, figure out what you are going to change to make things better.

Depression is very common in our society and in our churches. We can have victory over it alone, but with God’s help and with the support of Christian brothers and sisters, we can move forward.

You may not be gloriously happy all of the time, but by God’s grace, you will have the joy of the Lord in your heart, even on the most stressful days.

“Dr. Waldron,” sê die dame wat my teenoor sit. “Ek sukkel baie deesdae.”

“Vertel my wat aan die gang is,” sê ek.

“Ek weet nie hoe om dit te verduidelik nie,” huiwer sy… “Ek voel bloot meestal moeg. Ek kan nie meer konsentreer nie, en ek geniet nie meer die meeste van die dinge wat ek voorheen geniet het nie. Ek kom deur my dae, maar dit is omtrent dit. Dink u ek het ’nborsiekte of is ek laag in ’n mineraal of vitamien?”

“Dit kan so wees,” sê ek vir haar. “Ons kan daardie dinge beslis toets, maar ek dink daar gebeur iets anders hier.”

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

Ek is ’n gesinsdokter en waarskynlik dertig persent van die mense wat na my kantoor kom, het simptome van depressie. Dit beteken nie dat hulle medikasie daarvoor gebruik of voel dat hulle spesiale hulp nodig het nie, maar dit sê wel dat hierdie simptome wydverspreid in ons wêreld voorkom.

Selfs in Christelike kringe dui opnames daarop dat omtrent 15 persent van Christene self rapporteer dat hulle op ’n stadium in hul lewe gediagnoseer is met depressie. Dit is 25 persent laer as in die samelewing in die geheel, maar dit is steeds hoër as wat ons sou wou glo.

In die heel begin het God die wêreld en Adam en Eva geskep. And God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good… –Genesis 1:31. Voor die val was alles volmaak.

Ek dink nie ons verstaan heeltemal wat dit ingehou het nie. Duidelik was daar geen fisiese siektes of kwale wat mens of die plante- en diereryk van Eden getref het nie. Meer as dit, het Adam en Eva nie aan angs of depressie gely nie. Hul hormone het nie uit balans geraak nie, hulle het nie gestres geraak nie (al sou daar spanning in ’n volmaakte tuin kon wees), en hulle sou nie op enige tyd ontsteld of kwaad geraak het nie.

Alles het verander toe Adam en Eva gesondig het. Ons sien dit in die spanning tussen hulle nadat hulle die vrug geëet het, met Adam wat Eva blameer, en Eva wat die slang blameer. And the man said, The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat. And the LORD God said unto the woman, What is this that thou hast done? And the woman said, The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat –Genesis 3:12-13.

Om ’n gesin te voed het skielik moeilik geword. Virusse en bakterieë het patogenies geword en op ’n stadium, in die eerste families, sou mense begin het om met emosionele en geestesgesondheidsuitdagings te worstel.

Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee. And unto Adam he said, Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life; Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field; In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return –Genesis 3:16-19.

Ek wil ondersoek wat depressie is soos dit deur die mediese wêreld gedefinieer word, ’n paar van die bronne daarvan noem, en dan bespreek hoe ons daarmee kan omgaan, beide in ons eie lewens en in die lewens van ons vriende en familie.

Diagnoseer van Depressie

Soos vroeër vermeld, het baie mense ’n paar simptome van depressie. Hulle mag meer moeg voel, maklik huil, of ander simptome hê wat nie tipies vir hulle is nie. Die meeste van hulle het nie eintlik ware kliniese depressie nie.

Die meeste mense het nie al hierdie simptome nie, maar wanneer dit aaneenlopend teenwoordig is sonder om te verdwyn vir twee weke of langer, veral as dit sterk genoeg is om normale daaglikse pligte of die vermoë om behoorlik te rus te belemmer, dan is dit tyd om iets te doen.

Dit is belangrik om te onthou dat daar ’n groot of breë kontinuum rakende depressie is. Sommige mense het ’n ligte moedeloosheid, sommige ervaar diep gevoelens van hartseer, en sommige het genoeg depressie dat hulle ’n risiko is om hulself of ander skade te berokken.

Oorsake van Depressie

Daar is verskillende voorbeelde van mense in die Bybel wat simptome getoon het wat ooreenstem met depressie. Twee van hulle val vir my op.

Die eerste is Naomi. Ons weet dat sy saam met haar man en haar twee seuns na Moab gegaan het weens ’n honger wat suidelike Israel getref het. Sy het tien jaar in hierdie vreemde land deurgebring en in daardie tyd het haar man en albei haar seuns gesterf.

Die boek Ruth vertel ons dat toe sy na Betlehem teruggekeer het, het sy vir die mense gesê, …Call me not Naomi [pleasant], call me Mara [bitter]: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me. I went out full, and the LORD hath brought me home again empty: why then call ye me Naomi, seeing the LORD hath testified against me, and the Almighty hath afflicted me? –Ruth 1:20-21.

Daar is geen manier om Naomi te ondervra en uit te vind alles wat sy gevoel het nie, maar dit lyk na meer as eenvoudige rou. Sy het alles verloor wat vir haar waardevol was, en vir haar het dit gelyk of selfs God teen haar gedraai het.

Soos ons die verhaal van Ruth lees, sien ons dat dinge in die loop van die boek vir haar verbeter het—meestal deur die bediening van haar schoondogter, Ruth, maar ook deurdat God geleidelik weer dinge van waarde in haar lewe herstel het, en deur ander wat haar bemoedig het in die Here se goedheid. And the women said unto Naomi, Blessed be the LORD, which hath not left thee this day without a kinsman, that his name may be famous in Israel. And he shall be unto thee a restorer of thy life, and a nourisher of thine old age: for thy daughter in law, which loveth thee, which is better to thee than seven sons, hath born him. And Naomi took the child, and laid it in her bosom, and became nurse unto it –Ruth 4:14-16.

’n Ander wat by my opkom is die profeet Jeremia. Jeremia is geroep toe hy ’n jong man was, en hy het ’n baie lang bediening gehad waarin hy God se Woord aan ’n groep konings en ander mense verkondig het wat eenvoudig nie geïnteresseerd was in wat hy te sê gehad het nie.

Jeremia se lewe was konstant onder bedreiging. Op een tydstip is hy in ’n tronk vol modder gegooi en net op die laaste oomblik gered. Jerusalem is drie keer beleër voordat die Babiloniërs dit platgevee het. Deur sy dekades van bediening het Jeremia die mense vertel wat God van hulle verwag het, en die mense het dit voortdurend geïgnoreer.

Dit is dalk geen wonder dat Jeremia vandag as die weende profeet bekend staan nie. Hy het gesê, Cursed be the day wherein I was born: let not the day wherein my mother bare me be blessed. Cursed be the man who brought tidings to my father, saying, A man child is born unto thee; making him very glad. And let that man be as the cities which the LORD overthrew, and repented not: and let him hear the cry in the morning, and the shouting at noontide … Wherefore came I forth out of the womb to see labour and sorrow, that my days should be consumed with shame? –Jeremiah 20:14-18.

Dit is belangrik om te let dat in albei hierdie voorbeelde uit die Bybel, sonde nie as die kwessie (of die rede) wat hierdie mense in depressie gedryf het, openbaar word nie. Vir Naomi was dit waarskynlik ’n mengsel van isolasie van haar vaderland en die verlies van mense vir wie sy baie lief was. Vir Jeremia was dit die konstante spanning van probeer om God te dien in ’n nasie wat nie om God gegee het nie.

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

Depressie is altyd multifaktoreel. Dit beteken menselik dat daar gewoonlik ’n mengsel van interne en eksterne faktore is wat ’n persoon afbreek.

Daar is genetiese en hormonale komponente wat hier in werking tree. Daar is geen twyfel dat sekere individue en sekere families meer geneig is tot depressie as ander nie. Baie dokters en navorsers meen dat veranderinge in gene wat die chemikalie Serotonien (Serotonin) deur die brein vervoer, sommige mense meer vatbaar vir depressie kan maak as ander.

Hierdie verskille in genetiese samestelling kan ons help verstaan waarom sommige mense baie min spanning nodig het om hulle neer te bring, terwyl ander baie veerkragtig blyk te wees. Aangesien ons nie ons genetiese samestelling kan verander nie, maak dit geen sin om te spog as ons ’n meer opgewekte persoonlikheid het as iemand anders nie. En, as ons erken dat ons ’n groter neiging tot depressie het, hoef ons nie moedeloos te raak oor daardie feit nie. As God ons so geskep het dat ons geneig is om buierig te wees eerder as natuurlik opgewek te wees, moet ons wysheid gebruik om soveel eksterne faktore as moontlik te bestuur om die risiko van verlammande (ekstreem) depressie te minimaliseer.

Eksterne strewers is dikwels die ding wat hierdie soort gevoelens (moedeloosheid) trigger. Dit kan die dood van ’n noue vriend of familielid wees, of dit kan ’n finansiële teëslag wees. Dit is belangrik om te onthou dat selfs goeie gebeure groot hoeveelhede spanning kan produseer. Moeders met pasgebore babas funksioneer dikwels op baie min slaap, selfs terwyl baie fisiese veranderings in hul liggame plaasvind.

Sommige mense mag swak hanteringsvaardighede hê. Ongelukkig wend baie mense hom/haar tot straatdwelms of alkohol om te probeer om die gevoelens te verstik wat hulle andersins nie kan beheer nie.

As ’n finale punt kan sonde en skuld depressie trigger of dit slegter maak. Ons kan dit in Dawid en Saul se lewens sien. (Sien Psalm hoofstuk 32) Dit beteken nie dat alle depressie die gevolg van sonde is nie—lank van nie—maar sonde moet aangespreek en bekeer word om vorentoe te kan beweeg.

Lykende as ’n synoot sal ek noem dat uit my ervaring diep depressiewe mense dikwels met verskriklike skuld sukkel. Hulle weet nie eens watter sonde hulle moontlik gepleeg het nie; hulle is net seker dat God vir hulle kwaad is, en hulle moes iets verkeerd gedoen het. Die herstel van die depressie sal help met die versekering van redding-kwessies wat hierdie mense geneig is om mee te worstel.

Dit laat ons met die vraag hoe om iemand te help wat met hierdie soort denke te doen het.

Luister

Luister is ’n kragtige hulpmiddel om ander mense te help. Luister aktief en sonder om in te spring en negatiewe denke te onderbreek.

Jy mag kan sien dat dit nie alles verskriklik is nie en dat daar baie positiewe in die wêreld is. Die feit dat hulle hierdie dinge nie kan sien nie het meer te doen met hul gemoedstoestand as met hoe verskriklik dinge regtig is. ’n Persoon wat met depressie sukkel, mag weet dat daar mense is wat slegter daaraan toe is in die wêreld, maar dit help hulle nie regtig veel om dit aan hulle uit te wys nie.

Bemoedig

Bemoediging kan eenvoudig wees deur goeie dinge te sê wat jy in die lewe van die persoon wat sukkel, sien. Dit is iets waarna ons almal meer verlang.

Meer as dit, moet ons mense aanmoedig om dinge te doen wat gesond vir hulle is. Hulle moet uit hulle huis uitkom, hulle moet probeer oefen, en hulle moet ’n poging aanwend om gesond te eet. Ons kan hulle help om in al hierdie areas beter te doen. (Sien Galasiërs 6:2)

Bid

…The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much –James 5:16.

Hierdie mense benodig iemand wat saam met hulle sal bid. Hulle benodig iemand wat vir hulle sal bid. Jesus vra ons om in die geheim te bid, maar dit is ook regtig bemoedigend vir iemand wat sukkel om hulleself gebid te hoor word. Dit help hulle om te weet dat daar baie mense is wat hulle ondersteun met gebed.

Wees Bereid om die Inisiator te Wees

Mense met depressie het baie lae energievlakke. Verder sien hulle hulself nie as waardevol nie. Ten minste nie as iemand anders sou wou spandeer tyd saam met hulle nie. Hulle gaan nie bel of boodskappe stuur nie, en hulle gaan beslis nie ’n middagete-afspraak of gebedstyd reël nie.

Alhoewel hulle na al hierdie dinge hunker, is dit net regtig moeilik vir hulle om die eerste stap te neem om ander te nader. Dit val dus op die res van ons om bereid te wees om daardie dinge te doen.

Moenie na Gevolgtrekkings Spring nie

Ons ken die verhaal van Job se vriende. Hulle is opgery na Job toe nadat rampspoed hom getref het en het vir verskeie dae stil gesit in skok toe hulle die verwoesting sien wat hom aangedoen is. Toe hulle uiteindelik begin praat, was dit om hom te oordeel vir die verskriklike sonde wat hulle aanvaar het hy gepleeg het.

Dit is nie verkeerd om na sonde te vra nie, maar daar is baie tye waar depressie nie sondeverwant is nie. Om te veel vroeg op sonde te fokus, of dit aan te neem, sal net wiggies dryf wat dit minder waarskynlik maak dat jy ’n persoon kan help om genesing te vind.

Wat as jy die persoon is wat met depressie sukkel? Hoe moet jy daarmee omgaan en watter dinge kan help?

Hantering van Probleme Vroeg

Almal het oomblikke wanneer hulle gestres en regtig moedeloos is. Ons gebruik terme soos “uitbranding” en “medelye-moegheid” in die mediese veld wanneer mense in die verkeerde rigting beweeg. Hierdie stryd manifesteer wanneer ons prikkelbaar is met die mense rondom ons, wanneer ons die meeste van die tyd moeg voel, of wanneer ons meeste van die tyd moedeloos voel. Wanneer ons sien dat hierdie simptome opduik, is dit tyd om iets te doen om te keer dat dit erger word.

Miskien is ’n eerste stap eenvoudig om ons beperkte vermoëns te ken. Daar is tye waar ons eenvoudig nee sal moet sê vir werksprojekte of selfs kerkaktiwiteite omdat dit nie genoeg tyd vir rus laat nie. Sekere tye van die jaar kan slegter wees—baie mense sukkel meer gedurende die wintermaande as gevolg van minder sonlig.

Terugskroef in watter areas ookal moontlik is belangrik wanneer ons sien dat ons op die verkeerde trajek is.

Moenie Vergelykings Aanwend nie

Almal is anders. Om mense te identifiseer wat blykbaar “alles bymekaar het” wanneer jy sukkel, help jou nie en dit sal jou waarskynlik slegter laat voel nie.

Om met moedeloosheid te worstel beteken nie dat jy nie ’n Christen is nie of dat God klaar met jou is nie. Dit beteken dat jy mens is wat in ’n gevallen wêreld leef. Jy wil nie aanhou leef met ’n depressiewe gees nie, maar jy moet ook nie glo dat jy die enigste een is wat hiermee te doen gehad het nie. (Sien 2 Korintiërs 10:12)

Oefen

Farmosessionele oefening is regtig belangrik om die chemikalieë in die brein te verhoog wat met depressie geassosieer word. Dit maak regtig nie saak watter tipe oefening jy doen nie. Wat saak maak, is dat dit jou hartklop 25 tot 30 persent bo jou basislynhartklop verhoog.

Oefening is iets wat moeilik is om te doen, selfs wanneer jy nie met depressie te doen het nie. Dit is veral moeilik wanneer jy moeg en neerslagtig voel.

Spandeer Tyd met Bemoedigingsbronne

Mense het gemeenskap nodig. Wanneer ons met depressiewe gevoelens worstel, het ons regtig ander mense nodig om ons op te lig, om saam met ons te bid, en om ons aan te moedig. Niemand verbeter deur lang tye alleen deur te bring nie. (Sien Spreuke 27:17)

Hantering van Sonde

Sonde kan gebed doeltreffend laat voel asof dit ondoeltreffend is. Dit beteken nie dat eenvoudige belydenis van sonde skielik iemand se depressie sal ophef nie, maar dit is ’n belangrike deel van om genesing te bereik. Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed… –James 5:16.

Wees Bereid om Medikasie te Neem

Nie almal het medikasie nodig nie. Die hoop is dat as jy die regte (behulpame) dinge doen (sommige hiervan is hierbo gelys), kan jy verhoed dat dinge sleg genoeg raak dat jy mediese hulp nodig het. Maar daar is baie situasies waar iemand eenvoudig op medikasie moet begin om hulle in ’n aantal maniere te help: om te slaap, om ’n moeg gemoed wat nie stilhou nie te laat rus, om die emosionele pyn af te demp, ensovoorts.

Mense met genoegsampige ernstige depressie kan ’n risiko vir hulself wees. Hulle mag selfs heeltemal onvermoë wees om op berading of enige van die ander nie-mediese behandelings vir hierdie gevoelens te reageer. Hierdie mense moet regtig op medikasie begin met die doel om later af te bou van daardie medikasie wanneer hulle helder genoeg dink om op die regte pad voort te gaan.

Ongelukkig blyk die voordele van hierdie medikasie kortstondig te wees. Langtermyngebruik van antidepressiewe medikasie blyk nie regtig die lewenskwaliteit van baie pasiënte te verbeter nie. ’n Onlangse studie het pasiënte wat antidepressante geneem het vergelyk met dié wat dit nie gedoen het nie en het soortgelyke vlakke van gesondheidsverwante lewenskwaliteit in die twee groepe gevind. Met ander woorde, wanneer twee groepe depressiewe pasiënte vergelyk is—een groep wat medikasie neem en die ander wat nie—na ’n tydperk (ongeveer 6 maande) was daar geen waarneembare verskille meer in hul depressievlakke nie. Dus, alhoewel hierdie medikasie kan help om ’n persoon met ernstige depressie te stabiliseer, begin die werklike mediese “hulp” van die medikasie na ’n tyd verminder. Hopelik sal die persoon teen daardie tyd genoegsaam stabiel wees dat ’n veilige afbouing gedoen kan word om van die medikasie af te kom.

Met dit in gedagte is dit baie belangrik om dinge anders as medikasie te doen om die situasie te probeer verbeter.

Gaan Aan, Selfs Wanneer Jy Beter Voel

Baie kere, wanneer iemand ’n mediese probleem het, sal hulle bewustelik hul dieet en leefstyl verander om hul situasie te verbeter. Die probleem is dat wanneer die simptome beter word, die neiging is om terug te val in ou eet- en gedragsgewoontes.

As jy in die verlede met depressie te doen gehad het, is dit belangrik dat jy ’n pad van gesonde keuses bly volg. Oefen gereeld, eet gesonde maaltye, bestuur jou stresvlak (so veel as wat jy kan), moenie te veel skeduleer nie, en doen ’n bewuste poging om gereeld met godvrugtige vriende te ontmoet vir tye van gebed en ondersteuning.

Neem periodiek ’n inventarisasie van hoe dit met jou gaan. As jy sukkel, bepaal wat jy gaan verander om dinge beter te maak.

Depressie is baie algemeen in ons samelewing en in ons kerke. Ons kan alleenoorwinning hê daaroor, maar met God se hulp en met die ondersteuning van Christelike broers en susters kan ons vorentoe beweeg.

Jy mag nie deurgaans glorieryk gelukkig wees nie, maar deur God se genade sal jy die blydskap van die Here in jou hart hê, selfs op die mees stresvolle dae.

The angel of the LORD encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them –Psalm 34:7.

“Tell us a story, Grandma,” begged two eager children as they crowded around her rocking chair.

“My, my, you children like to hear stories, don’t you?” replied Grandma, with a twinkle in her eye. “All right, I’ll tell you about a time when I was about eight years old, and my sister Lori was nine.

We lived on an old farm, back a short lane along a dirt road. One morning, Mother called us in from our play and said she was out of sugar. She asked us to walk to Mrs. Brightbill to see if she had any sugar to spare. You see, we didn’t have telephones when I was a little girl, so she couldn’t call the neighbor and ask her. Neighbors often shared back and forth because we didn’t go shopping at the store very often either. So, mother gave us a container, and we started out on our long walk as Mother called after us and reminded us not to loiter along the way.”

“How far was it to the Brightbills?” asked Sharon.

“Oh, it was about half a mile to our closest neighbor, the Rhine’s place, and then about another quarter of a mile to the Brightbills,” replied Grandma.

“Oh, that’s far. Mother won’t let us walk on the road at all,” added Micah.

“I’m sure you are right,” agreed Grandma. “And I hope you never walk on the road without your parents’ permission. But things were much different when I was a little girl. We also walked every day to school, which was quite a bit further than the Brightbill farm. So, the little errand we were doing on this morning for Mother seemed like fun. There was only one problem though. The Rhine family had an old man living in their summer house. His name was Pierce, and he had a very fierce dog; at least he acted very fierce! He was kept behind a high wire fence connected to an old shed.

Every day when we walked to school, that dog frightened us terribly with his fierce barking and growling. But Mother always reminded us to pray and remember the Bible verse which says: What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee –Psalm 56:3. Still, we hurried by as fast as our legs could take us.

Lori and I started out happily on our errand for Mother. We skipped along, watching the dust swirl beneath our feet on that warm summer morning. Everything seemed unusually quiet and still as we passed through the gully, over the rippling creek, and up the steep hill right before Neighbor Rhine’s place. There before us was the old shed, and on the other side was the high fence which kept in Pierce’s mean dog. My heart began to thump rapidly. ‘Maybe that bad dog hadn’t seen us yet,’ I thought gratefully as I whispered once more to myself, ‘I will trust and not be afraid.’

Suddenly, the air was shattered by the ferocious barking of that mean dog as he sprang around the corner of the old shed! Lori and I froze in our tracks! As that angry dog raced toward us, Lori screamed. The next moment, I realized she had fallen down and was sitting in the middle of the dirt road, with her hands behind her on the hard packed gravel, feet and legs in the air, kicking and kicking, spinning around and around as that angry dog circled her, jumping in at her and nipping at her feet and legs! I was so scared. I just stood frozen to the spot. I don’t remember if I screamed, or if I prayed. But suddenly there was a shout! It was Pierce, with a whip in his hand. He came running around the shed and out on the road. He whipped and whipped that dog and finally got him away from Lori and back inside the fence where he belonged, as Lori and I stood there, trembling, and crying with relief.”

“Wow!” exclaimed Sharon. “That was really scary, wasn’t it?”

“Did Pierce need to get rid of his dog?” asked Micah.

“Yes, Sharon, it was very scary,” answered Grandma. “And no, Micah, Pierce did not get rid of his dog. We children needed to keep trusting the good Lord to keep us safe every day.”

“I don’t remember what happened after Pierce got the dog away that day, or if we ever got Mother’s sugar, but I will never forget what happened that day.

It was a miracle that Lori and I were not injured. There is a verse in Psalms which says: Save me from the lion’s mouth… –Psalm 22:21. How thankful we were to be delivered from the dog’s mouth! I like to think that the Lord’s angel had his sword drawn in front of that dog’s mouth every time he leaped at my dear sister.”

여호와의 천사는 그를 경외하는 자를 둘러 진 치시고 그들을 건지시느니라 — 시편 34:7.

“이야기 하나 해 줘, 할머니.” 두 아이가 흔들의자에 모여들며 간절히 부탁했다.

“어머나, 너희들 이야기 듣는 걸 참 좋아하구나?” 할머니가 눈을 반짝이며 대답했다. “자, 내가 여덟 살쯤 되고 내 여동생 로리가 아홉 살이었을 때 얘기를 해 주마.

우리는 흙길 옆의 짧은 차도 안쪽 오래된 농장에서 살았단다. 어느 날 아침, 엄마가 우리를 놀던 데서 불러 오시더니 설탕이 없다고 하셨어. 엄마는 우리가 브라이트빌 부인 댁에 가서 설탕을 좀 얻을 수 있는지 물어보러 가라고 하셨어. 내가 어릴 때는 전화기가 없어서 이웃에게 전화를 걸어 물어볼 수가 없었단다. 이웃들은 서로 드나들며 서로 나눠 쓰곤 했지. 우리도 가게에 자주 가지 않았으니까. 그래서 엄마는 용기를 하나 주시고 우리가 길게 걸어가게 되었지. 엄마는 가는 길에 빈둥거리지 말라고 뒤에서 일러 주셨단다.”

“브라이트빌 집까지 얼마나 멀었어?” 샤론이 물었다.

“오, 우리 집에서 가장 가까운 이웃인 라인네 집까지는 대략 반 마일쯤, 그리고 브라이트빌 집까지는 그보다 더 가서 대략 4분의 1마일쯤 더 되었단다.” 할머니가 대답했다.

“오, 그건 멀다. 엄마는 우리를 절대 길 위로 못 걷게 해.” 미카가 덧붙였다.

“네 말이 맞구나,” 할머니가 동의하셨다. “그리고 엄마 허락 없이 절대 길 위를 걷지 않길 바란다. 하지만 내가 어릴 때는 사정이 많이 달랐단다. 우리는 매일 학교까지도 걸어 다녔는데, 학교는 브라이트빌 농장보다 훨씬 더 멀었지. 그래서 그날 아침에 엄마 심부름은 오히려 재미있는 일이었단다. 단 한 가지 문제가 있었는데, 라인네 집에는 여름 별장에 살던 늙은 남자가 한 사람 있었단다. 그의 이름은 피어스였고, 아주 사나운 개를 키웠지. 적어도 행동은 매우 사나워 보였단다! 그 개는 오랜 외양간에 연결된 높은 철조망 울타리 안에 갇혀 있었어.

우리가 학교에 걸어갈 때마다 그 개는 사납게 짖고 으르렁대서 우리를 몹시 겁주곤 했지. 하지만 엄마는 항상 기도하고 시편의 다음 구절을 기억하라고 일러 주셨다: 내가 두려울 때에 주를 의뢰하리이다 — 시편 56:3. 그럼에도 우리는 다리가 닿는 대로 빨리 달려 지나가곤 했단다.

로리와 나는 엄마 심부름을 즐겁게 떠났단다. 우리는 그 따뜻한 여름 아침에 발밑에 이는 먼지를 보며 깡충깡충 뛰었지. 우리 앞길은 유달리 고요하고 잠잠한 듯했어. 계곡을 지나고 잔물결 치는 시내를 건너고 라인네 집 바로 전의 가파른 언덕을 올라갔지. 바로 거기에 오래된 외양간이 있었고, 그 맞은편에 피어스의 사나운 개가 갇혀 있던 높은 울타리가 있었단다. 내 심장은 급히 뛰기 시작했어. ‘아마도 그 나쁜 개가 아직 우리를 보지 못했을 거야’ 하고 난 감사히 속으로 생각하며 또 한 번 속으로 중얼거렸지. ‘나는 의지하고 두려워하지 않으리라.’

갑자기 그 사나운 개가 외양간 모퉁이로 뛰어나오며 맹렬히 짖어 대더구나! 로리와 나는 발이 얼어붙은 듯 꼼짝하지 못했지! 그 화난 개가 우리를 향해 달려오자 로리가 비명을 질렀다. 다음 순간, 그녀는 넘어져서 흙길 한가운데 앉아 있었어. 단단히 다져진 자갈 위에 손을 뒤로 짚고 발과 다리를 허공에 올린 채 발차기를 하고 빙글빙글 도는 상황이었단다. 그 성난 개는 그녀를 빙빙 돌며 다가와 발과 다리를 물기 시작했어! 난 너무 무서웠다. 그냥 제자리에 얼어붙어 서 있었지. 내가 비명을 질렀는지, 기도했는지도 기억나지 않는다. 그런데 갑자기 누군가 소리를 질렀다! 피어스였어. 채찍을 든 채 달려나오며 외양간을 돌아 길로 나왔단다. 그는 개를 채찍으로 때리며 쫓아내서 마침내 로리에게서 떨어지게 하고 개가 있어야 할 울타리 안으로 다시 밀어 넣었어. 우리 둘은 떨면서도 안도에 울음을 터뜨렸단다.”

“와!” 샤론이 감탄했다. “정말 무서웠겠네?”

“피어스가 자기 개를 없애야 했어?” 미카가 물었다.

“그렇구나, 샤론, 아주 무서운 일이었단다.” 할머니가 대답하셨다. “그리고 아니란다, 미카, 피어스는 그 개를 없애지 않았단다. 우리 아이들은 날마다 우리를 지켜 주시는 선하신 주님을 계속 의지해야 했단다.”

“피어스가 그날 개를 떼어낸 뒤에 무슨 일이 있었는지, 우리가 엄마 설탕을 얻어 왔는지 나는 기억나지 않지만, 그날 있었던 일은 결코 잊을 수가 없단다.

로리와 내가 다치지 않은 것은 기적이었단다. 시편에 이런 구절이 있지: 내가 사자(사나운 입)로부터 나를 건지소서… — 시편 22:21. 우리는 개의 입에서 구원받은 것을 얼마나 감사했는지 몰라! 나는 그 사나운 개가 내 사랑하는 여동생에게 달려들 때마다 주의 천사가 그 개의 입앞에 검을 들고 서 있었던 것이라고 생각하곤 한단다.”

The angel of the LORD encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them –Psalm 34:7.

“Tell us a story, Grandma,” begged two eager children as they crowded around her rocking chair.

“My, my, you children like to hear stories, don’t you?” replied Grandma, with a twinkle in her eye. “All right, I’ll tell you about a time when I was about eight years old, and my sister Lori was nine.

We lived on an old farm, back a short lane along a dirt road. One morning, Mother called us in from our play and said she was out of sugar. She asked us to walk to Mrs. Brightbill to see if she had any sugar to spare. You see, we didn’t have telephones when I was a little girl, so she couldn’t call the neighbor and ask her. Neighbors often shared back and forth because we didn’t go shopping at the store very often either. So, mother gave us a container, and we started out on our long walk as Mother called after us and reminded us not to loiter along the way.”

“How far was it to the Brightbills?” asked Sharon.

“Oh, it was about half a mile to our closest neighbor, the Rhine’s place, and then about another quarter of a mile to the Brightbills,” replied Grandma.

“Oh, that’s far. Mother won’t let us walk on the road at all,” added Micah.

“I’m sure you are right,” agreed Grandma. “And I hope you never walk on the road without your parents’ permission. But things were much different when I was a little girl. We also walked every day to school, which was quite a bit further than the Brightbill farm. So, the little errand we were doing on this morning for Mother seemed like fun. There was only one problem though. The Rhine family had an old man living in their summer house. His name was Pierce, and he had a very fierce dog; at least he acted very fierce! He was kept behind a high wire fence connected to an old shed.

Every day when we walked to school, that dog frightened us terribly with his fierce barking and growling. But Mother always reminded us to pray and remember the Bible verse which says: What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee –Psalm 56:3. Still, we hurried by as fast as our legs could take us.

Lori and I started out happily on our errand for Mother. We skipped along, watching the dust swirl beneath our feet on that warm summer morning. Everything seemed unusually quiet and still as we passed through the gully, over the rippling creek, and up the steep hill right before Neighbor Rhine’s place. There before us was the old shed, and on the other side was the high fence which kept in Pierce’s mean dog. My heart began to thump rapidly. ‘Maybe that bad dog hadn’t seen us yet,’ I thought gratefully as I whispered once more to myself, ‘I will trust and not be afraid.’

Suddenly, the air was shattered by the ferocious barking of that mean dog as he sprang around the corner of the old shed! Lori and I froze in our tracks! As that angry dog raced toward us, Lori screamed. The next moment, I realized she had fallen down and was sitting in the middle of the dirt road, with her hands behind her on the hard packed gravel, feet and legs in the air, kicking and kicking, spinning around and around as that angry dog circled her, jumping in at her and nipping at her feet and legs! I was so scared. I just stood frozen to the spot. I don’t remember if I screamed, or if I prayed. But suddenly there was a shout! It was Pierce, with a whip in his hand. He came running around the shed and out on the road. He whipped and whipped that dog and finally got him away from Lori and back inside the fence where he belonged, as Lori and I stood there, trembling, and crying with relief.”

“Wow!” exclaimed Sharon. “That was really scary, wasn’t it?”

“Did Pierce need to get rid of his dog?” asked Micah.

“Yes, Sharon, it was very scary,” answered Grandma. “And no, Micah, Pierce did not get rid of his dog. We children needed to keep trusting the good Lord to keep us safe every day.”

“I don’t remember what happened after Pierce got the dog away that day, or if we ever got Mother’s sugar, but I will never forget what happened that day.

It was a miracle that Lori and I were not injured. There is a verse in Psalms which says: Save me from the lion’s mouth… –Psalm 22:21. How thankful we were to be delivered from the dog’s mouth! I like to think that the Lord’s angel had his sword drawn in front of that dog’s mouth every time he leaped at my dear sister.”

مَلَكُ الرَّبِّ يَحُطُّ حَوْلَ مُرْتَعِدِيهِ، وَيُنَجِّيهمْ – مزمور 34:7.

«احكِ لنا قصة، يا جدتي»، توسّل طفلان متلهّفان وهما يتجمعان حول كرسيها الهزاز.

«يا إلهي، أنتم الأطفال تحبّون الاستماع إلى القصص، أليس كذلك؟» ردّت الجدة، مع لمعة في عيونها. «حسنًا، سأحدّثكم عن مرة كنتُ فيها في حوالي الثامنة من عمري، وكانت أختي لوري بعمر التاسعة.

كنا نعيش في مزرعة قديمة، بعيدًا على ممر قصير على طريق ترابي. في صباح أحد الأيام نادتنا أمّنا عن لعبنا وقالت إنها نفدت منها السكر. طلبت منا أن نمشي إلى منزل السيدة برايتبيل لنرى إن كان عندها بعض السكر لتعيرنا. أتعرفون، لم يكن لدينا هواتف عندما كنت طفلة صغيرة، فلم تستطع أن تتصل بالجارة وتطلب منها. كان الجيران كثيرًا ما يتقاسمون بعضهم البعض لأننا لم نكن نذهب للتسوّق إلى المتجر كثيرًا أيضًا. لذا أعطتنا أمّنا وعاءً، وبدأنا مشينا الطويلة بينما كانت أمّنا تنادينا من الخلف وتذكّرنا ألا نتأخّر على الطريق.»

«كم كان البُعد إلى بيت عائلة برايتبيل؟» سألت شارون.

«أوه، كان حوالي نصف ميل إلى أقرب جار لنا، منزل عائلة راين، ثم حوالي ربع ميل آخر إلى منزل برايتبيل»، أجابت الجدة.

«أوه، هذا بعيد. أمّي لا تسمح لنا بالمشي على الطريق على الإطلاق»، أضاف ميخا.

«أظن أنك على حق»، وافقت الجدة. «وأدعو ألا تمشوا أبدًا على الطريق دون إذن والديكم. لكن الأمور كانت مختلفة كثيرًا عندما كنت طفلة. كنّا نمشي أيضًا كل يوم إلى المدرسة، والتي كانت أبعد بكثير من مزرعة برايتبيل. لذا، بدا الأمر كقضاء متعة صغيرة في المهمّة التي قمنا بها لصالح أمّنا ذلك الصباح. كان هناك مشكلة واحدة فقط. كان لعائلة راين رجل مسنّ يعيش في بيتهم الصيفي. كان اسمه بيرس، وكان لديه كلب شرس جدًا؛ على الأقل كان يتصرّف بوحشيّة! كان يُحبَس خلف سياج سلكي عالٍ متصل بمستودع قديم.

كل يوم عندما كنا نمشي إلى المدرسة، كان ذلك الكلب يرعبنا بشدة بنباحه وصهيله المرعب. لكن أمّنا كانت تذكّرنا دائمًا أن نصلي ونتذكر آية الكتاب المقدس التي تقول: عِنْدَمَا أَخَافُ، أَتَّكِلُ عَلَيْكَ – مزمور 56:3. ومع ذلك، كنّا نسرع مرورًا بأسرع ما تطيق أقدامنا.

انطلقت أنا ولوري في مهمّتنا لصالح الأمّ بمرح. كنا نقفز فرحين، نراقب الغبار وهو ينعَّم تحت أقدامنا في ذلك الصباح الصيفي الدافئ. بدا كل شيء هادئًا وساكنًا كما مررنا بالخندق، وعبرنا الجدول المتماوج، وصعدنا التلّ الحادّ قبل منزل الجار راين مباشرة. هناك أمامنا كان المستودع القديم، وعلى الجانب الآخر كان السياج العالي الذي يمنع كلب بيرس الشرير من الخروج. بدأ قلبي يخفق بسرعة. هممت أفكر شاكرةً: ‹ربما لم يرنا ذلك الكلب بعد›، وهمست لنفسي مرة أخرى: ‹سأتوكّل ولن أخاف.›

فجأة، تحطّم الصمت بصهيل ذلك الكلب الشرس حين انقضّ حول زاوية المستودع! تجمّدنا أنا ولوري في أماكننا! وبينما ذلك الكلب الغاضب يندفع نحونا، صرخت لوري. وفي اللحظة التالية أدركت أنها سقطت وجلست في منتصف الطريق الترابي، ويديها وراءها على الحصى المضغوط، وقدماها وساقاها في الهواء، تركل وتتركّل، وتدور وتدور بينما ذلك الكلب الغاضب يدور حولها، يقفز عليها ويعضّ في قدميها وساقيها! كنت مرعوبة جدًا. ببَساطة وقفت مشلولة. لا أذكر إن كنت قد صرخت أم صليت. لكن فجأة جاء صياح! كان بيرس، وهو يحمل سوطًا في يده. ركض حول المستودع وخرج إلى الطريق. سوط سوط ذلك الكلب حتى أبعده عن لوري وأعادَه داخل السياج حيث ينتمي، بينما وقفت أنا ولوري هناك نرتجف ونبكي من الفرج.»

«يا للروعة!» قالت شارون. «كان ذلك مخيفًا حقًا، أليس كذلك؟»

«هل كان على بيرس أن يتخلّص من كلبه؟» سأل ميخا.

«نعم، يا شارون، كان ذلك مخيفًا جدًا»، أجابت الجدة. «ولا، يا ميخا، لم يتخلّ بيرس عن كلبه. كنّا نحن الأطفال محتاجين أن نستمر في الاتكال على الرب الصالح ليحمينا كل يوم.»

«لا أذكر ما الذي حدث بعد أن أبعد بيرس الكلب في ذلك اليوم، أو إن كنا قد أحضرنا سكر الأم في نهاية المطاف، لكنني لن أنسى ما جرى في ذلك اليوم.

لقد كان معجزة أننا أنا ولوري لم نتعرّضا لإصابة. هناك آية في المزامير تقول: خَلِّصْنِي مِنْ فَمِ الأَسَدِ… – مزمور 22:21. كم كنا شاكرين لأننا نُجِّيْنا من فمِ الكلب! أحب أن أتصوّر أن ملاك الرب كان مسلولًا بسيفه أمام فم ذلك الكلب في كل مرة كان يقفز فيها نحو شقيقتي العزيزة.»

Greetings to each one in the worthy name of Jesus Christ, our Saviour, and our Redeemer.

This magazine issue may seem to be arriving more quickly on the heels of the last one. True. We are continuing to tighten up our schedule as we work towards getting each quarterly issue out in a more timely manner. Our ultimate goal is to have them arrive in your mailboxes in the months of March, June, September, and December of each year. Pray for us as we continue moving towards that schedule.

From time to time, we receive feedback—suggestions, concerns, and encouragement. We value this feedback. It is filed away and used by the board as we continually evaluate ways to make our magazine better. One final thought on this matter… when we receive feedback of encouragement regarding a specific article, it is helpful for us, and it is encouraging for our authors as we pass that along to them. We welcome your ongoing feedback.

As previously mentioned, we are including several new categories in this issue. One on Church History that is being written by two young brothers from our church. And one on Hymn Histories being written by one of our board members, a middle-aged married man, who is also from our church.

In “Moses in Midian”, we take a walk in Moses’ footsteps during the mid-section of his life. He was uprooted from his comfortable lifestyle in Egypt as an adopted son of royalty and was then sent by God into the desert to learn some much-needed lessons in further preparation towards becoming God’s servant. As we take a look at the life of Jonah, we glean glimpses of “The God Who Will Not Let Go”. Often a struggling believer loses sight of the Truth of God because they believe the lie that no one cares, yet the truth of the matter is this—the God of the Bible doesn’t just drop us, or turn His back on us, the instant that we take a wrong turn or a misstep. Let’s allow this article to help us to become rooted and grounded in the biblical Truth of Abba Father—a Father who cares for His children. We also have the second article in a continuing series on discipleship, as well as an article written by a middle-aged, spiritually-mature sister who shares her encouragement for sisters to evaluate what God thinks of their attire.

Church History and Should A Christian Vote

Finally, let’s consider the two short articles on church history. One of our goals for this issue is burdened with the awareness that the country in which we live (the U.S.) is approaching mid-term elections in November of this year and that there will be a strong push for many conservative Anabaptists to become involved in the voting process to ensure a proper outcome for the good of their perceived cause or goals.

In the natural world our “old man” has the tendency to think that we must “do something” if we expect things to go in a “right” direction. The spiritual Truth is this: The king’s heart is in the hand of the LORD, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will –Proverbs 21:1. If we think that, as believers, we will have a part in electing the “right” person in an election if we personally vote, let’s stop to consider what God Himself told Nebuchadnezzar. …That the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will –Daniel 4:31-32.

Throughout the history of the Anabaptist people there have been varied opinions on this matter, however, it is our wish to lift up the perspective that Jesus said …My kingdom is not of this world: if my kingdom were of this world, then would my servants fight … but now is my kingdom not from hence –John 18:36. When we understand and develop a personal world view that is founded on the two-kingdom principle, we realize that we must function as …strangers and pilgrims on the earth. [While we] …declare plainly that [we] seek a country …a better country, that is, an heavenly: wherefore God is not ashamed to be called [our] God: for he hath prepared for [us] a city –Hebrews 11:13-16. In all things involving political involvement, it is our encouragement that New Testament believers should obey the command to …come out from among them, and be ye separate… –2 Corinthians 6:17.

Let’s always cultivate a right attitude in our hearts so that our talk and actions reflect God’s view on the matter when He through the Apostle Paul tells us to: Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God … For he is the minister of God to thee… –Romans 13:1-4.

It is in consideration of these thoughts that we wrote the two articles detailing very different times in the history of the church and what it was like for Christians to relate to the government of their day. Let us seriously ponder whether we can do more good by getting involved in politics, especially in the voting process. Or whether God wants us to pray for our elected officials, to view them as His servants, and to speak about them with respect. Ultimately, we must trust God to bring about His will for the winding down of the “clock of time” as time speeds onward towards the end of time. God will do this through hardening the hearts of ungodly men in positions of power, just like Pharaoh of old, to accomplish His sovereign will for the world.

So, what is the solution when we struggle within our hearts about the direction of our country and its growing instability or when we experience so much pressure from our peers or the society around us to get involved to make a difference? The Apostle Paul gives us very clear direction when he says, I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men; For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty. 1 Timothy 2:1-2. The Christian’s secret power of influence lies in the power of prayer that is produced in the privacy of his or her closet. However, for this prayer to have power it must be produced out of a heart of faith—And Jesus said unto them … verily I say unto you, If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you –Matthew 17:20. Let us always remember that …The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much –James 5:16.

Until the next time, may God be with each one and grant you grace and peace as you walk faithfully according to His Word. Let us pray for each other as we go through the trying times in our world today.

Saudações a cada um no digno nome de Jesus Cristo, nosso Salvador e Redentor.

Esta edição da revista pode parecer estar chegando mais rapidamente após a anterior. Verdade. Estamos continuando a ajustar nosso cronograma enquanto trabalhamos para que cada edição trimestral seja lançada de maneira mais pontual. Nosso objetivo final é que cheguem às suas caixas de correio nos meses de março, junho, setembro e dezembro de cada ano. Orem por nós enquanto continuamos avançando em direção a esse cronograma.

De tempos em tempos, recebemos feedback — sugestões, preocupações e encorajamento. Valorizamos esse feedback. Ele é arquivado e usado pelo conselho enquanto continuamente avaliamos maneiras de tornar nossa revista melhor. Um pensamento final sobre este assunto... quando recebemos feedback de encorajamento a respeito de um artigo específico, isso nos é útil e é encorajador para nossos autores quando lhes repassamos. Acolhemos seu feedback contínuo.

Como mencionado anteriormente, estamos incluindo várias novas categorias nesta edição. Uma sobre História da Igreja que está sendo escrita por dois jovens irmãos de nossa igreja. E outra sobre Histórias de Hinos sendo escrita por um dos membros do nosso conselho, um homem casado de meia-idade, que também é da nossa igreja.

Em “Moisés em Midiã”, caminhamos nas pegadas de Moisés durante a parte intermediária de sua vida. Ele foi arrancado de seu estilo de vida confortável no Egito como filho adotivo da realeza e então enviado por Deus ao deserto para aprender algumas lições muito necessárias, em maior preparação para se tornar servo de Deus. Ao olharmos para a vida de Jonas, percebemos vislumbres de “O Deus Que Não Larga”. Frequentemente um crente em luta perde de vista a Verdade de Deus porque crê na mentira de que ninguém se importa, porém a verdade é esta — o Deus da Bíblia não nos abandona nem vira as costas para nós no instante em que damos uma guinada errada ou cometemos um passo em falso. Permita que este artigo nos ajude a nos enraizar e firmar na Verdade bíblica do Abba Pai — um Pai que cuida de seus filhos. Também temos o segundo artigo de uma série contínua sobre discipulado, assim como um artigo escrito por uma irmã de meia-idade espiritualmente madura que compartilha seu encorajamento para que as irmãs avaliem o que Deus pensa sobre suas vestimentas.

História da Igreja e Deve um Cristão Votar

Por fim, consideremos os dois artigos curtos sobre história da igreja. Um de nossos objetivos para esta edição carrega a consciência de que o país em que vivemos (os EUA) se aproxima das eleições de meio de mandato em novembro deste ano e de que haverá um forte impulso para que muitos anabatistas conservadores se envolvam no processo de votação para garantir um resultado considerado apropriado para o bem de sua causa ou objetivos percebidos.

No mundo natural, nosso “velho homem” tende a pensar que devemos “fazer alguma coisa” se esperarmos que as coisas sigam numa direção “certa”. A Verdade espiritual é esta: O coração do rei está na mão do SENHOR, como as águas; ele o inclina para onde quer – Provérbios 21:1. Se pensamos que, como crentes, teremos alguma participação em eleger a pessoa “certa” numa eleição se votarmos pessoalmente, paremos para considerar o que Deus mesmo disse a Nabucodonosor. …Que o Altíssimo domina no reino dos homens, e o dá a quem quer – Daniel 4:31-32.

Ao longo da história do povo anabatista houve opiniões variadas sobre este assunto; contudo, nosso desejo é apresentar a perspectiva que Jesus disse: …O meu reino não é deste mundo; se o meu reino fosse deste mundo, os meus servos lutariam… mas agora o meu reino não é daqui – João 18:36. Quando entendemos e desenvolvemos uma cosmovisão pessoal fundada no princípio dos dois reinos, percebemos que devemos funcionar como …estrangeiros e peregrinos sobre a terra. [Enquanto] …declaramos francamente que buscamos uma pátria… uma pátria melhor, isto é, celestial: por isso Deus não se envergonha de ser chamado o Deus deles: pois lhes preparou uma cidade – Hebreus 11:13-16. Em tudo o que envolve envolvimento político, nosso encorajamento é que os crentes do Novo Testamento obedeçam ao mandamento de …sair do meio deles e separar-vos… – 2 Coríntios 6:17.

Cultivemos sempre uma atitude correta em nossos corações para que nossas palavras e ações reflitam o ponto de vista de Deus sobre o assunto quando Ele, por meio do apóstolo Paulo, nos diz: Todos devam sujeitar-se às autoridades superiores. Porque não há autoridade que não venha de Deus; as autoridades que existem foram por ele ordenadas… Porque o magistrado é servo de Deus para teu bem… – Romanos 13:1-4.

É em consideração a esses pensamentos que escrevemos os dois artigos detalhando épocas muito diferentes na história da igreja e como era para os cristãos relacionarem-se com o governo de seu tempo. Vamos ponderar seriamente se podemos fazer mais bem envolvendo-nos na política, especialmente no processo de votação. Ou se Deus quer que oremos por nossos governantes eleitos, que os vejamos como servos dele e que falemos deles com respeito. Em última análise, devemos confiar em Deus para cumprir a Sua vontade no desenrolar do “relógio do tempo” enquanto o tempo avança rumo ao fim. Deus fará isso endurecendo os corações de homens ímpios em posições de poder, assim como o fez com o Faraó de outrora, para realizar Sua vontade soberana para o mundo.

Então, qual é a solução quando lutamos em nosso íntimo sobre a direção do nosso país e sua crescente instabilidade, ou quando experimentamos tanta pressão de nossos pares ou da sociedade ao nosso redor para nos envolvermos a fim de fazer a diferença? O apóstolo Paulo nos dá orientação muito clara quando diz: Exorto, pois, que se use de súplicas, orações, intercessões e ações de graças por todos os homens; pelos reis e por todos os que se acham em eminência; para que vivamos uma vida tranquila e sossegada em toda piedade e honestidade. – 1 Timóteo 2:1-2. O poder secreto de influência do cristão reside no poder da oração que é produzida na privacidade do seu aposento. Contudo, para que essa oração tenha poder ela deve brotar de um coração de fé — E Jesus disse-lhes… na verdade vos digo que, se tiverdes fé como um grão de mostarda, direis a este monte: Passa daqui para acolá, e ele passará; e nada vos será impossível – Mateus 17:20. Lembremo-nos sempre de que …A oração eficaz do justo pode muito – Tiago 5:16.

Até a próxima vez, que Deus esteja com cada um e conceda graça e paz enquanto andais fielmente segundo a Sua Palavra. Oremos uns pelos outros enquanto atravessamos os tempos difíceis em nosso mundo hoje.
