Du är värdig, Herre, att ta emot härlighet och ära och makt; ty du har skapat allt, och därigenom, att de finns till och blev skapade – Uppenbarelseboken 4:11.

Denna hymn, ofta kallad ”Kristenhetens nationalsång”, är kanske en av de största hymnerna genom tiderna. Den skrevs av Edward Perronet och publicerades första gången i Gospel Magazine i november 1779. Den redigerades av Augustus Toplady, som också är författare till en annan välkänd hymn, ”Rock of Ages”. Texten till denna hymn, All Hail the Power of Jesus Name, har översatts till nästan varje språk där kristendomen är känd. Varhelst den sjungs, talar den till människohjärtats andliga behov. En författare har sagt: ”Så länge det finns kristna på jorden kommer den att fortsätta sjungas; och efter det, i himlen.”

Edward Perronet föddes i Sundridge i Kent, England, 1726. Han var ättling till en framstående fransk hugenottfamilj som flytt till Schweiz och senare till England på grund av religionsförföljelserna i Frankrike. Edwards far, en pastor i Engelska statskyrkan, var starkt sympatisk med den evangeliska rörelse som leddes av Wesley-bröderna och George Whitefield. Edward blev liksom sin far präst i den anglikanska kyrkan men var alltid kritisk mot dess sätt. En gång skrev han: ”Jag föddes och jag kommer troligen att dö i den skakande gemenskapen i Engelska kyrkan, men jag föraktar hennes enfald.” Snart bröt han emellertid med kyrkan och kastade sig kraftfullt in i Wesley-brödernas evangeliska arbete under 1740- och 1750-talen.

Charles Wesley skriver om Edward Perronets frimodighet i predikan. Vid ett tillfälle blev han och Perronet instängda i ett hus av en hop råa smädare, vilka Perronet modigt bemötte medan de förolämpade honom och kastade jord på honom. Det var under denna tid som Wesleys och deras anhängare led mycket förföljelse och till och med våld från dem som var oeniga med deras tjänst. Om dessa erfarenheter noterade Wesley i sin dagbok: ”Från Rockdale gick vi till Bolton, och fann snart att Rockdales lejon var lamm jämfört med de i Bolton.” Edward Perronet blev nedkastad och rullad i lera och dyn; stenar kastades och fönster krossades.

En annan intressant berättelse ges om förhållandet mellan Wesley-bröderna och Perronet. John Wesley ville höra Perronet predika, och han, som var 18 år yngre än John, hade alltid vägrat att predika i den äldre kyrkomannens närvaro. Så en dag, då Wesley såg Edward i församlingen, tillkännagav han att han skulle predika vid nästa gudstjänst. För att undvika en offentlig konflikt med Wesley steg Perronet upp i predikstolen nästa morgon, men förklarade snabbt att han aldrig hade samtyckt till att predika. ”Dock,” tillade han, ”ska jag hålla den största predikan som någonsin hållits på jorden.” Han läste då Bergspredikan och satte sig utan kommentar.

Efter åtta års samarbete med Wesley-bröderna orsakade Perronets starka vilja och fria ande en spricka mellan dem, då han var oenig med några av deras föreskrifter. De fortsatte dock att uppskatta och älska varandra.

Perronets sista år tillbringades i Canterbury, där han var pastor i en oberoende församling, och där han dog 1792, vid sextiosex års ålder. Hans sista ord har också blivit klassiska: ”Ära vara Gud i hans gudomliga höjd! Ära vara Gud i hans mänskliga djup! Ära vara Gud i hans allmakt! I hans händer överlämnar jag min ande.”

Fastän Perronet skrev många andra hymner och dikter, har ingen av dem uppnått berömmelse utom den odödliga ”All Hail the Power of Jesus Name.” Denna texts framgång har utan tvivel främjats av tre fina melodier. ”Coronation”, komponerad av Oliver Holden, en snickare från Massachusetts, självlärd musiker och respekterad lärare i sångskola, används mest i Amerika. ”Miles Lane”, komponerad av William Shrubsole, Perronets personliga vän, är mest populär i Storbritannien. Den festliga melodin ”Diadem”, komponerad 1838 för denna text av James Ellor, en engelsk lekmannamusiker, används ofta som ett körnummer. Denna hymn skrevs ursprungligen med titeln ”On the Resurrection” och hade åtta verser, som följer:

All hail the power of Jesus’ name,
Let angels prostrate fall
Bring forth the royal diadem,
To crown Him Lord of all!

Let high born seraphs tune the lyre,
And, as they tune it, fall
Before His face who tunes their choir,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Crown Him, ye morning stars of light,
Who fixed this floating ball,
Now hail the Strength of Israel’s might,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Crown Him, ye martyrs of your God,
Who from His altar call;
Extol the stem of Jesse’s rod,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Ye seed of Israel’s chosen race,
Ye ransomed of the fall,
Hail Him who saves you by His grace
And crown Him Lord of all!

Hail Him, ye heirs of David’s line,
Whom David Lord did call.
The God incarnate, Man divine,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Sinners, whose love can ne’er forget
The wormwood and the gall,
Go spread your trophies at His feet,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Let every tribe and every tongue
That bound creation’s call
Now shout in universal song,
The crowned Lord of all!

Som den nu står i våra sångböcker är hymnen förkortad och förändrad, och en vers lades till av den berömde hymninsamlaren, präst John Rippon, 1787.

Oh, that with yonder sacred throng
We at His feet may fall;
We’ll join the everlasting song,
And crown Him Lord of all.

När vi avslutar denna anmärkningsvärda berättelse om Edward Perronets liv och om dem som haft del i att föra denna odödliga hymn till oss, låt oss till slut se på hymnens effekt på hedningar som intet visste om Jesus. Den mest berömda berättelsen i samband med Perronets stora hymn handlar om missionären i Indien, präst E. P. Scott. En dag såg han på gatan en man med så märkligt utseende att han frågade om honom och fick veta att han tillhörde en vild bergstam bland vilka Kristus aldrig hade predikats. Herr Scott bad över ärendet och bestämde sig för att besöka den stammen. Så snart han nådde deras bergshem föll han in bland en vild skara mordiska stammän som var ute på ett krigståg och som drog ihop sig mot honom med sina spjut. De grep honom och riktade sina spjut mot hans hjärta. Omedelbart drog missionären fram violinen som han alltid bar med sig och började spela och sjunga på modersmålet, ”All hail the power of Jesus’ name!” Han slöt ögonen och väntade vilken minut som helst på döden. När han nått den fjärde versen och ingenting hade hänt, öppnade han ögonen och blev förbluffad över att se att spjuten hade fallit ur de vildas händer och stora tårar fyllde deras ögon! De bjöd in herr Scott till sina hem, och han tillbringade de återstående åren av sitt liv med att predika och tjäna Guds kärlek och frälsning för dessa människor. Gud i sin försorg använde en enkel hymn som medel för att föra evangeliet till en grupp behövande hedningar.

”Diadem” melodi - James Elliot, 1838
”Let Us Crown Him” melodi - James McGranahan 1840–1907

Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted?… –Matthew 5:13.

One might wonder as to why the Anabaptists, the early church fathers, church history writers, and especially the progenitor (originator or author) of our beliefs, Christ Himself, effected such a vehement and absolute approach to a separated church and state. Why did they unanimously preach, write, and otherwise caution against political involvement of any kind by Christians? Perhaps this is best answered by looking at the results of Christians ignoring these sincere warnings, casting off their Godly allegiance, and pledging themselves to a flawed and ultimately futile earthly kingdom.

The Mennonites of Germany are a particularly intriguing and cautionary episode of Christian and Anabaptist histories—not only because of their relative proximity to our time—but also because of their almost wholesale devotion to a worldly leader and agenda. What led them to such an un-Christ-like position? A true understanding of their story must begin, naturally, with their beginnings.

The Mennonites of 20th century Germany were descended from the first Anabaptist groups, but unlike our ancestors, they stayed in the Old World instead of emigrating to the New World. There, a number of factors led them to a unique position within world events, a position that would test their mettle on a global stage.

The beginnings of the 20th century brought about the first World War, which ended with the defeat of Germany and its allies. The resulting peace treaties were structured to humiliate and crush Germany, saddling it with an almost unpayable war debt, and restricting its rights to build a military. The German people, unsurprisingly, resented this insult being added to the injury of having lost the War. Their resentment festered, and soon manifested itself in nationalistic movements, the most notable of which was the National Socialist German Workers Party (or the Nazi Party). The party was founded in 1919, and Hitler was amongst its first members. He quickly assumed party leadership, attracting followers with his “us vs. them” rhetoric and strong leadership.

Party growth was small in the decade following its founding. During this time, Hitler continued to shape the Nazis according to his wishes. Hatred for most non-German (Aryan) groups became a central party theme, along with a violent distaste for communism. However, the party was not large enough to be anything but a fringe voice, representing only a small portion of German voters.

Insignificance did not last, however. The Great Depression brought the catalyst for the Nazi’s rise to power. When the global market crashed, over 2 million Germans lost their jobs. Unemployed, they rallied around the charismatic leadership that promised to give them jobs, give them power, to “Make Germany great again”. Moving quickly, Hitler added legions to his followers.

The thousands of new Nazi Party members enabled the Nazi Party to seriously contest many local elections, and in Germany’s Parliament, they were able to control enough votes to sway policy making. In the long run, their political might handed Hitler the office of prime minister. Having secured that position, he went on to overthrow the German government, establishing himself and his party as the undisputed rulers of Germany.

Why did such a man, and such a movement, attract the attention and adoration of a church that professed much of what we do? Loving our enemies, separation from the world, and nonresistance did not seem to combine with the message of the Nazis. The answer, like most backsliding churches, is best portrayed as happening in small steps and over time.

In 1929, the Mennonites came under the eye of Germany and its rapidly expanding Nazi Party. 13,000 Russian Mennonite refugees descended on Moscow, seeking an exit from the Communist-run country. The Nazis seized the situation, using the Mennonites as supposed evidence that Aryans (peoples of German lineage, such as the Mennonites) were being unjustly used by the rest of the world. This image was pushed by state propaganda departments, who circulated writings, pamphlets, and even two immensely popular movies, depicting the Mennonites as strong, red-blooded Germans valiantly striving against the unjust oppression of the Russian Communists. These efforts afforded the refugees national attention, which subsequently led to them being admitted into Germany.

While many Mennonites entered Germany, as refugees and otherwise, there were also thriving, established communities that were given the same patriotic make-over by the Nazi propogandists. Unfortunately, these churches welcomed the Nazi attention, going so far as to send Hitler a letter thanking him for being the “savior of the German peoples” and pledging their support to his government. It is of note that Hitler, a man quite busy running an emerging world power, personally responded to this letter with a memo thanking the churches for their support and expressing a desire for further cooperation to the benefit of both the Nazis and the Mennonites. The church further weakened under these seemingly beneficial relations.

A particularly shocking case of Mennonite political involvement came from the churches in or around Danzig. Danzig and the surrounding countryside had long been a part of the German Empire, until the end of World War I, when the region was separated from Germany, essentially becoming a buffer zone between Germany and Poland. In 1939, Hitler would make one of his first moves on Europe by annexing Danzig, where the Nazis had been building party influence for most of the 1930’s. The Mennonites of the area, having been German only a generation before, welcomed their new part in the Germany of the future, becoming involved in almost every level of the Nazi Party. Otto Andres became the second-highest ranked Nazi of the Danzig area, and scores of the 6,000 believers in the surrounding congregations joined various Nazi organizations. The men often took part in the paramilitary SA and SS, while their wives and daughters took part in corresponding women’s groups. Churches became saturated with active Nazis, even going so far as to accept them into church leadership. At one point, five of the seven local churches were led by active party members.

World War II was the final step in the Mennonites’ integration with the Nazis. The German concentration camp of Stutthof supplied slave labor to numerous Mennonite businesses. Mennonite churches organized war efforts, including recruiting their young men to serve in the German army. In a particularly twisted case, a Mennonite doctor, Johan Klassen, was personally responsible for the deaths of more than one hundred disabled children.

Perhaps the most concerning episode in this dismal tale of backsliding comes after the war. Mennonite leadership, recognizing to some extent the terrible depths to which they had fallen, and noting the justice that was to come through the Nuremburg trials, effectively shrugged the blame from off their shoulders. Appealing to their Mennonite brothers across the ocean, they convinced them of their innocence, twisting their involvement in the Nazi regime to make themselves appear the victims. American Mennonites helped these now-refugees in many ways, providing all manner of assistance, and ultimately keeping most of them from facing possible prison time or death sentences. The surviving German churches eventually disintegrated or emigrated to the Americas.

If a group who originally held beliefs identical to our own could stray to the point of child murder and slave labor, then the question must be asked: “Are we seeing their folly for what it was?” Why did the churches of Danzig accept the advances of what, in retrospect, was a clearly un-biblical, un-Christlike movement?

The origin for their downfall was surprisingly simple. The Mennonites of Germany forgot who their true Ruler was. No earthly kingdom at war tolerates an allegiance to the enemy, and neither does the Kingdom of Heaven. The pride in their earthly kingdom, the pursuit of prestige and power, all led to a foreseeable end. Their salt had lost its savor, and they were cast out and trodden underfoot. This is a cautionary tale of the dangers of an unequal yoking of the church with the world.

Vós sois o sal da terra; mas se o sal perder o seu sabor, com que se há de salgar?… –Mateus 5:13.

Pode-se perguntar por que os anabatistas, os primeiros pais da igreja, os historiadores eclesiásticos e, especialmente, o progenitor (originador ou autor) de nossas crenças, o próprio Cristo, adotaram uma abordagem tão veemente e categórica quanto à separação entre igreja e estado. Por que pregaram, escreveram e alertaram unanimemente contra qualquer envolvimento político dos cristãos? Talvez isso seja melhor respondido observando os resultados de cristãos que ignoraram esses avisos sinceros, abandonaram sua lealdade a Deus e se comprometeram com um reino terrestre falho e, no fim, fútil.

Os menonitas da Alemanha constituem um episódio particularmente intrigante e instrutivo na história cristã e anabatista — não apenas por sua relativa proximidade no tempo — mas também por sua quase devoção total a um líder e a uma agenda mundana. O que os levou a uma posição tão não cristã? Uma compreensão verdadeira de sua história deve começar, naturalmente, por suas origens.

Os menonitas da Alemanha do século XX descendiam dos primeiros grupos anabatistas, mas, ao contrário de nossos antepassados, permaneceram no Velho Mundo em vez de emigrar para o Novo Mundo. Ali, diversos fatores os conduziram a uma posição singular no contexto dos acontecimentos mundiais, uma posição que testaria sua fibra em palco global.

O início do século XX trouxe a Primeira Guerra Mundial, que terminou com a derrota da Alemanha e de seus aliados. Os tratados de paz resultantes foram estruturados para humilhar e esmagar a Alemanha, impondo-lhe uma dívida de guerra quase impagável e restringindo seus direitos de construir um exército. O povo alemão, não surpreendentemente, ressentiu esse insulto acrescentado à dor de ter perdido a guerra. O ressentimento fermentou e logo se manifestou em movimentos nacionalistas, o mais notável dos quais foi o Partido Nacional Socialista dos Trabalhadores Alemães (ou Partido Nazista). O partido foi fundado em 1919, e Hitler estava entre seus primeiros membros. Rapidamente assumiu a liderança do partido, atraindo seguidores com sua retórica de “nós contra eles” e sua liderança forte.

O crescimento do partido foi pequeno na década seguinte à sua fundação. Durante esse tempo, Hitler continuou a moldar os nazistas segundo seus desejos. O ódio contra a maioria dos grupos não germânicos (arianos) tornou-se tema central do partido, junto com um gosto violento pelo anticomunismo. Contudo, o partido não era grande o suficiente e permanecia uma voz marginal, representando apenas uma pequena parte dos eleitores alemães.

Essa insignificância não durou, porém. A Grande Depressão trouxe o catalisador para a ascensão nazista. Quando o mercado global quebrou, mais de 2 milhões de alemães perderam seus empregos. Desempregados, juntaram-se à liderança carismática que prometia dar-lhes trabalho, dar-lhes poder, “fazer a Alemanha grande outra vez”. Agindo rapidamente, Hitler somou legiões de seguidores.

Os milhares de novos membros do Partido Nazista permitiram que o partido disputasse seriamente muitas eleições locais e, no Parlamento alemão, eles conseguiram controlar votos suficientes para influenciar a elaboração de políticas. A longo prazo, seu poder político concedeu a Hitler o cargo de chanceler. Tendo assegurado essa posição, ele tomou o governo alemão e estabeleceu-se, junto com seu partido, como os governantes indiscutíveis da Alemanha.

Por que um homem assim, e um movimento assim, atraíram a atenção e a adoração de uma igreja que professava grande parte do que professamos? Amar nossos inimigos, a separação do mundo e a não resistência não pareciam combinar com a mensagem dos nazistas. A resposta, como na maioria das igrejas apostatadas, revela-se melhor como ocorrendo em pequenos passos e ao longo do tempo.

Em 1929, os menonitas atraíram o olhar da Alemanha e de seu Partido Nazista em rápida expansão. 13.000 refugiados menonitas russos chegaram a Moscou, buscando sair do país dominado pelos comunistas. Os nazistas aproveitaram a situação, usando os menonitas como suposta evidência de que os arianos (povos de linhagem alemã, como os menonitas) eram injustamente tratados pelo resto do mundo. Essa imagem foi promovida pelos departamentos estatais de propaganda, que circularam escritos, panfletos e até dois filmes imensamente populares, retratando os menonitas como alemães fortes e de sangue quente, lutando valentemente contra a injusta opressão dos comunistas russos. Esses esforços deram atenção nacional aos refugiados, o que levou subsequentemente à sua admissão na Alemanha.

Enquanto muitos menonitas entraram na Alemanha como refugiados e de outras formas, havia também comunidades estabelecidas e prósperas que receberam a mesma transformação patriótica pelos propagandistas nazistas. Infelizmente, essas igrejas acolheram a atenção nazista, chegando a enviar a Hitler uma carta agradecendo-lhe por ser o “salvador do povo alemão” e prometendo seu apoio ao seu governo. É de notar que Hitler, um homem bastante ocupado em dirigir uma potência emergente, respondeu pessoalmente a essa carta com um memorando agradecendo às igrejas pelo apoio e expressando desejo de cooperação futura em benefício tanto dos nazistas quanto dos menonitas. A igreja enfraqueceu ainda mais sob essas relações aparentemente benéficas.

Um caso particularmente chocante de envolvimento político menonita veio das igrejas em ou ao redor de Danzig. Danzig e o campo ao redor haviam sido por muito tempo parte do Império Alemão, até o fim da Primeira Guerra Mundial, quando a região foi separada da Alemanha, tornando-se essencialmente uma zona tampão entre a Alemanha e a Polônia. Em 1939, Hitler faria um de seus primeiros movimentos na Europa ao anexar Danzig, onde os nazistas vinham construindo influência partidária durante a maior parte da década de 1930. Os menonitas da área, tendo sido alemães apenas uma geração antes, acolheram seu novo papel na Alemanha do futuro, envolvendo-se em quase todos os níveis do Partido Nazista. Otto Andres tornou-se o nazista de segunda hierarquia na área de Danzig, e dezenas dos 6.000 crentes das congregações circunvizinhas juntaram-se a várias organizações nazistas. Os homens muitas vezes participavam das paramilitares SA e SS, enquanto suas esposas e filhas participavam de grupos femininos correspondentes. As igrejas tornaram-se saturadas de nazistas ativos, chegando até a aceitá-los na liderança eclesiástica. Em certo momento, cinco das sete igrejas locais eram lideradas por membros ativos do partido.

A Segunda Guerra Mundial foi o passo final na integração dos menonitas com os nazistas. O campo de concentração alemão de Stutthof forneceu trabalho escravo para numerosas empresas menonitas. Igrejas menonitas organizaram esforços de guerra, incluindo o recrutamento de seus jovens para servir no exército alemão. Em um caso particularmente distorcido, um médico menonita, Johan Klassen, foi pessoalmente responsável pela morte de mais de cem crianças com deficiência.

Talvez o episódio mais preocupante nesta sombria narrativa de apostasia ocorra depois da guerra. A liderança menonita, reconhecendo em certa medida as profundezas terríveis a que haviam caído e observando a justiça que viria pelos julgamentos de Nuremberg, efetivamente desviou de si a culpa. Apelando a seus irmãos menonitas do outro lado do oceano, convenceram-nos de sua inocência, deturparam seu envolvimento no regime nazista para se mostrarem como vítimas. Os menonitas americanos ajudaram esses agora refugiados de várias maneiras, fornecendo todo tipo de assistência e, em última instância, impedindo a maioria deles de enfrentar possíveis penas de prisão ou de morte. As igrejas alemãs sobreviventes acabaram por se desintegrar ou emigrar para as Américas.

Se um grupo que originalmente professava crenças idênticas às nossas pôde desviar-se até o ponto do assassinato infantil e do trabalho escravo, então a questão deve ser colocada: “Estamos vendo a sua tolice pelo que foi?” Por que as igrejas de Danzig aceitaram os avanços do que, em retrospectiva, foi um movimento claramente não bíblico e não cristão?

A origem de sua queda foi surpreendentemente simples. Os menonitas da Alemanha esqueceram quem era seu verdadeiro Governante. Nenhum reino terreno em guerra tolera uma lealdade ao inimigo, e o Reino dos Céus também não. O orgulho em seu reino terreno, a busca por prestígio e poder, tudo conduziu a um fim previsível. Seu sal perdera o sabor, e foram lançados fora e pisados. Esta é uma narrativa de advertência sobre os perigos de um jugo desigual da igreja com o mundo.

Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created –Revelation 4:11.

This hymn, often called the “National Anthem of Christendom,” is perhaps one of the greatest of hymns of all time. It was written by Edward Perronet, first appearing in the November 1779 issue of Gospel Magazine. It was edited by Augustus Toplady, who is also the author of another well-known hymn, “Rock of Ages”. The text of this hymn, All Hail the Power of Jesus Name, has been translated into almost every language where Christianity is known. Wherever it is sung, it communicates to the spiritual needs of human hearts. One writer has said, “So long as there are Christians on earth, it will continue to be sung; and after that, in heaven.”

Edward Perronet was born at Sundridge, Kent, England, in 1726. He was a descendant of a distinguished French Huguenot family who had fled to Switzerland and later to England because of the religious persecution in France. Edward’s father, a pastor in the State Church of England, was strongly sympathetic with the evangelical movement spearheaded by the Wesleys and George Whitefield. Edward, too, like his father, became a minister in the Anglican Church but was always critical of its ways. Once he wrote, “I was born and I am likely to die in the tottering communion of the Church of England, but I despise her nonsense.” Soon, however, he broke from the Church and threw himself strenuously into the evangelistic endeavors of the Wesleys during the 1740s and 1750s.

Charles Wesley writes of Edward Perronet’s boldness in preaching. At one time he and Perronet were beset in a house by a mob of rough revilers, whom Perronet opposed courageously, while they abused him and threw dirt on him. It was during this time that the Wesleys and their followers suffered much persecution and even violence from those who disagreed with their ministry. Concerning these experiences, Wesley made the following notation in his diary: “From Rockdale we went to Bolton, and soon found that the Rockdale lions were lambs in comparison with those of Bolton.” Edward Perronet was thrown down and rolled in mud and mire. Stones were hurled and windows broken.

Another interesting account is given regarding the relationship between the Wesleys and Perronet. John Wesley wanted to hear Perronet preach, and he, being 18 years younger than John had always refused to preach in the older churchman’s presence. So, one day Wesley seeing Edward in the congregation announced that he would preach at the next service. Desiring to avoid a public conflict with Wesley, Perronet mounted the pulpit the next morning, but quickly explained that he had never consented to preach. “However,” he added, “I shall deliver the greatest sermon that has ever been preached on earth.” He then read the Sermon on the Mount and sat down without comment.

After eight years of co-operation with the Wesleys, Perronet’s strong-mindedness and free spirit caused a division between them, as he disagreed with some of their regulations. They continued, however, to esteem and love each other.

The last years of Perronet were spent at Canterbury, where he was pastor of an independent church, and where he died in 1792, at the age of sixty-six. His last words have also become a classic: “Glory to God in the height of His divinity! Glory to God in the depth of His humanity! Glory to God in His all-sufficiency! Into His hands I commend my spirit.”

Though Perronet wrote many other hymns and forms of poetry, none of them, have attained fame except the immortal “All Hail the Power of Jesus Name.” The success of this text has, no doubt, been furthered by three fine tunes. “Coronation,” composed by Oliver Holden, a Massachusetts carpenter, self-taught musician, and respected singing-school teacher, is most widely used in America. “Miles Lane” composed by William Shrubsole, Perronet’s personal friend, is the most popular in Great Britain. While the festive “Diadem” tune, composed in 1838 for this text by James Ellor, an English layman, is frequently used as a choir number. This hymn was originally written having the title, “On the Resurrection,” and there were eight stanzas, as follows:

All hail the power of Jesus’ name,
Let angels prostrate fall
Bring forth the royal diadem,
To crown Him Lord of all!

Let high born seraphs tune the lyre,
And, as they tune it, fall
Before His face who tunes their choir,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Crown Him, ye morning stars of light,
Who fixed this floating ball,
Now hail the Strength of Israel’s might,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Crown Him, ye martyrs of your God,
Who from His altar call;
Extol the stem of Jesse’s rod,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Ye seed of Israel’s chosen race,
Ye ransomed of the fall,
Hail Him who saves you by His grace
And crown Him Lord of all!

Hail Him, ye heirs of David’s line,
Whom David Lord did call.
The God incarnate, Man divine,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Sinners, whose love can ne’er forget
The wormwood and the gall,
Go spread your trophies at His feet,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Let every tribe and every tongue
That bound creation’s call
Now shout in universal song,
The crowned Lord of all!

As it now stands in our hymnbooks, the hymn is shortened and changed, and one stanza has been added by the famous hymn collector, Rev. John Rippon, in 1787.

Oh, that with yonder sacred throng
We at His feet may fall;
We’ll join the everlasting song,
And crown Him Lord of all.

As we wrap up this amazing story of the life of Edward Perronet and the others who have had their part in bringing this immortal hymn to us, let’s take a look in closing at the effect this hymn has had on heathens who knew nothing about Jesus. The most famous story connected with Perronet’s great hymn is told of the missionary to India, Rev. E.P. Scott. One day he saw on the street a man of so strange an appearance that he inquired about him and learned that he belonged to a wild mountain tribe among whom Christ had never been preached. Mr. Scott prayed over the matter and decided to visit that tribe. As soon as he reached their mountain home, he fell in among a savage band of murderous tribesmen who were on a war expedition, and who were closing in on him with their spears. They seized him and pointed their spears at his heart. At once the missionary drew out the violin that he always carried with him and began to play and sing in the native language, “All hail the power of Jesus’ name!” He closed his eyes, expecting death at any minute. When he reached the fourth stanza, and nothing had happened, he opened his eyes, and was amazed to see that the spears had fallen from the hands of the savages, and big tears were in their eyes! They invited Mr. Scott to their homes, and he spent the remaining years of his life preaching and ministering God’s love and redemption to these people. God in His providence used a simple hymn as a means of introducing the gospel to a group of needy pagans.

Εσύ είσαι άξιος, Κύριε, να λάβεις δόξα και τιμή και δύναμη· επειδή εσύ δημιούργησες τα πάντα, και για τη θέλησή σου είναι και δημιουργήθηκαν –Αποκάλυψις 4:11.

Αυτός ο ύμνος, που συχνά αποκαλείται «Εθνικός Ύμνος της Χριστιανοσύνης», είναι ίσως ένας από τους σπουδαιότερους ύμνους όλων των εποχών. Τον έγραψε ο Έντγουαρντ Περνόνετ και πρωτοεμφανίστηκε στο τεύχος του Νοεμβρίου του 1779 του Gospel Magazine. Τον επεξεργάστηκε ο Όγκουστους Τόπλαδι, που είναι επίσης ο συγγραφέας ενός άλλου γνωστού ύμνου, του “Rock of Ages”. Το κείμενο αυτού του ύμνου, All Hail the Power of Jesus Name, έχει μεταφραστεί σε σχεδόν κάθε γλώσσα όπου είναι γνωστή ο Χριστιανισμός. Όπου και αν τραγουδιέται, ανταποκρίνεται στις πνευματικές ανάγκες της ανθρώπινης καρδιάς. Ένας συγγραφέας έχει πει, «Όσο θα υπάρχουν χριστιανοί στη γη, θα συνεχίσει να τραγουδιέται· και μετά από αυτό, στον ουρανό.»

Ο Έντγουαρντ Περνόνετ γεννήθηκε στο Σάνντριτζ, στο Κεντ της Αγγλίας, το 1726. Ήταν απόγονος μιας εξέχουσας γαλλικής οικογένειας Ουγκώ, που είχε καταφύγει στην Ελβετία και αργότερα στην Αγγλία εξαιτίας της θρησκευτικής διωγμού στη Γαλλία. Ο πατέρας του Έντγουαρντ, πάστορας στην Κρατική Εκκλησία της Αγγλίας, ήταν έντονα συμπαθών στο ευαγγελικό κίνημα που προωθούσαν οι Γουέσλι και ο Τζορτζ Γουάιτφιλντ. Ο Έντγουαρντ, όπως και ο πατέρας του, έγινε επίσης κληρικός στην Αγγλικανική Εκκλησία, αλλά πάντοτε ήταν κριτικός απέναντί της. Μια φορά έγραψε, «Γεννήθηκα και πιθανόν θα πεθάνω στην τρεμουλιαστή κοινωνία της Εκκλησίας της Αγγλίας, αλλά περιφρονώ τη βλακεία της.» Σύντομα, ωστόσο, αποχώρησε από την Εκκλησία και ρίχτηκε έντονα στις ευαγγελικές προσπάθειες των αδερφών Γουέσλι κατά τη δεκαετία του 1740 και του 1750.

Ο Τσαρλς Γουέσλι γράφει για το θάρρος του Έντγουαρντ Περνόνετ στο κήρυγμα. Κάποτε αυτός και ο Περνόνετ βρέθηκαν περικυκλωμένοι σε ένα σπίτι από όχλο άγριων συκοφαντών, τους οποίους ο Περνόνετ αντιτάχθηκε με γενναιότητα, ενώ τον έβριζαν και του πετούσαν χώμα. Ήταν εκείνη την εποχή που οι Γουέσλι και οι ακόλουθοί τους υπέστησαν πολλή δίωξη και ακόμη και βία από εκείνους που αντιτιθόντουσαν στη διακονία τους. Σχετικά με αυτές τις εμπειρίες, ο Γουέσλι σημείωσε στο ημερολόγιό του: «Από το Ρόκντεϊλ πήγαμε στο Μπόλτον, και σύντομα ανακαλύψαμε ότι τα λιοντάρια του Ρόκντεϊλ ήταν αμνοί σε σύγκριση με εκείνα του Μπόλτον.» Ο Έντγουαρντ Περνόνετ ρίχτηκε κάτω και κυλίστηκε σε λάσπη και βούρκο. Πέτρες εκτοξεύτηκαν και παράθυρα σπάστηκαν.

Δίνεται επίσης μια άλλη ενδιαφέρουσα αφήγηση σχετικά με τη σχέση των αδελφών Γουέσλι με τον Περνόνετ. Ο Τζον Γουέσλι ήθελε να ακούσει τον Περνόνετ να κηρύττει, και εκείνος, που ήταν 18 χρόνια νεότερος από τον Τζον, πάντα αρνιόταν να κηρύξει παρουσία του μεγαλύτερου κληρικού. Έτσι, μια μέρα ο Γουέσλι, βλέποντας τον Έντγουαρντ στην εκκλησία, ανακοίνωσε ότι θα κηρύξει στην επόμενη λειτουργία. Θέλοντας να αποφύγει μια δημόσια αντιπαράθεση με τον Γουέσλι, ο Περνόνετ ανέβηκε στο άμβωνα το επόμενο πρωί, αλλά εξήγησε γρήγορα ότι ποτέ δεν είχε συναινέσει να κηρύξει. «Ωστόσο,» πρόσθεσε, «θα εκθέσω τον μεγαλύτερο λόγο που έχει ποτέ κηρυχθεί στη γη.» Έπειτα διάβασε το Κήρυγμα του Όρους και καθίσθηκε χωρίς σχόλιο.

Μετά από οκτώ χρόνια συνεργασίας με τους Γουέσλι, η ισχυρογνωμοσύνη και το ανεξάρτητο πνεύμα του Περνόνετ προκάλεσαν ρήξη μεταξύ τους, καθώς διαφώνησε με μερικούς από τους κανονισμούς τους. Συνεχώς, όμως, συνέχισαν να τρέφουν εκτίμηση και αγάπη ο ένας για τον άλλον.

Τα τελευταία χρόνια της ζωής του Περνόνετ πέρασαν στην Κάντερμπερι, όπου ήταν πάστορας μιας ανεξάρτητης εκκλησίας, και εκεί πέθανε το 1792, σε ηλικία εξήντα έξι ετών. Τα τελευταία του λόγια έγιναν επίσης κλασικά: «Δόξα στο Θεό στο ύψος της θεότητάς Του! Δόξα στο Θεό στο βάθος της ανθρωπιάς Του! Δόξα στο Θεό στην παντελή επάρκειά Του! Στα χέρια Του παραθέτω το πνεύμα μου.»

Αν και ο Περνόνετ έγραψε πολλούς άλλους ύμνους και ποιήματα, κανένας από αυτούς δεν απέκτησε φήμη εκτός από τον αθάνατο «All Hail the Power of Jesus’ Name.» Η επιτυχία αυτού του κειμένου, αναμφίβολα, έχει ενισχυθεί από τρεις ωραίες μελωδίες. Το «Coronation», σύνθεση του Όλιβερ Χόλντεν, ενός μαραγκού από τη Μασαχουσέτη, αυτοδίδακτου μουσικού και σεβαστού δασκάλου τραγουδιού, είναι το πιο διαδεδομένο στην Αμερική. Το «Miles Lane», σύνθεση του Ουίλιαμ Σράμπσολ, προσωπικού φίλου του Περνόνετ, είναι το πιο δημοφιλές στη Μεγάλη Βρετανία. Ενώ η εορταστική μελωδία «Diadem», συντεθειμένη το 1838 για αυτό το κείμενο από τον Τζέιμς Έλλορ, έναν Άγγλο λαϊκό, χρησιμοποιείται συχνά ως χορωδιακός αριθμός. Αυτός ο ύμνος αρχικά γράφτηκε με τον τίτλο, «Περί της Αναστάσεως», και είχε οκτώ στροφές, ως εξής:

All hail the power of Jesus’ name,
Let angels prostrate fall
Bring forth the royal diadem,
To crown Him Lord of all!

Let high born seraphs tune the lyre,
And, as they tune it, fall
Before His face who tunes their choir,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Crown Him, ye morning stars of light,
Who fixed this floating ball,
Now hail the Strength of Israel’s might,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Crown Him, ye martyrs of your God,
Who from His altar call;
Extol the stem of Jesse’s rod,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Ye seed of Israel’s chosen race,
Ye ransomed of the fall,
Hail Him who saves you by His grace
And crown Him Lord of all!

Hail Him, ye heirs of David’s line,
Whom David Lord did call.
The God incarnate, Man divine,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Sinners, whose love can ne’er forget
The wormwood and the gall,
Go spread your trophies at His feet,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Let every tribe and every tongue
That bound creation’s call
Now shout in universal song,
The crowned Lord of all!

Όπως εμφανίζεται τώρα στα βιβλία ύμνων μας, ο ύμνος έχει συντομευτεί και τροποποιηθεί, και μια στροφή έχει προστεθεί από τον διάσημο συλλέκτη ύμνων, τον Rev. John Rippon, το 1787.

Oh, that with yonder sacred throng
We at His feet may fall;
We’ll join the everlasting song,
And crown Him Lord of all.

Καθώς ολοκληρώνουμε αυτή την εκπληκτική αφήγηση της ζωής του Έντγουαρντ Περνόνετ και των άλλων που συνέβαλαν στο να φτάσει σε εμάς αυτός ο αθάνατος ύμνος, ας ρίξουμε μια ματιά στο τέλος στην επίδραση που είχε αυτός ο ύμνος σε ειδωλολάτρες που δεν γνώριζαν τίποτα για τον Ιησού. Η πιο διάσημη ιστορία συνδεδεμένη με τον μεγάλο ύμνο του Περνόνετ αφηγείται για τον ιεραπόστολο στην Ινδία, Rev. E.P. Scott. Μια μέρα έβλεπε στον δρόμο έναν άνδρα τόσο αλλόκοτης εμφάνισης που τον ρώτησε γι’ αυτόν και έμαθε ότι ανήκε σε μια άγρια ορεινή φυλή, ανάμεσα στην οποία ο Χριστός ποτέ δεν είχε κηρυχθεί. Ο κ. Σκοτ προσευχήθηκε γι’ αυτό το θέμα και αποφάσισε να επισκεφθεί εκείνη τη φυλή. Μόλις έφτασε στο ορεινό τους σπίτι, βρέθηκε ανάμεσα σε μια άγρια συμμορία δολοφονικών φυλών που ήταν σε πολεμική εκστρατεία, και που τον περικύκλωναν με τις λόγχες τους. Τον συνέλαβαν και σήκωσαν τις λόγχες τους προς την καρδιά του. Αμέσως ο ιεραπόστολος τράβηξε το βιολί που πάντα κουβαλούσε μαζί του και άρχισε να παίζει και να τραγουδά στη ντόπια γλώσσα, “All hail the power of Jesus’ name!” Έκλεισε τα μάτια του, περιμένοντας το θάνατο ανά πάσα στιγμή. Όταν έφτασε στην τέταρτη στροφή, και τίποτα δεν είχε συμβεί, άνοιξε τα μάτια του και έμεινε έκπληκτος στο θέαμα ότι οι λόγχες είχαν πέσει από τα χέρια των αγρίων, και μεγάλα δάκρυα βρισκόταν στα μάτια τους! Προσκάλεσαν τον κ. Σκοτ στα σπίτια τους, και εκείνος πέρασε τα υπόλοιπα χρόνια της ζωής του κηρύττοντας και διακονώντας την αγάπη και τη λύτρωση του Θεού σε αυτούς τους ανθρώπους. Ο Θεός στην πρόνοιά Του χρησιμοποίησε έναν απλό ύμνο ως μέσον για να εισαγάγει το ευαγγέλιο σε μια ομάδα αναγκεμένων ειδωλολατρών.

I have enjoyed listening to, and even taking part in, discussions about the Covid shot—about why someone has, and why the other has not, received it. I venture to say we could have seven people give their viewpoint on the subject and maybe have eight different ideas.

I begin with the disclaimer that these are my thoughts, and I am quite okay with someone disagreeing. In fact, I would welcome others to share their viewpoints.

One of the things you will notice in this writing is that I don’t call the Covid shot a ‘vaccine’. Not that it doesn’t technically fit the official definition, but rather that it doesn’t function the way we have known vaccines to work. I remember when I was a lad about four years of age, I went with my mother to the health department and received a vaccination in my upper arm for smallpox. (The pock mark is still there) I remember some years later when the whole community gathered at our local public school for the sugar cube treatment which was an oral vaccination against polio. I don’t remember if I had any other vaccinations or not. My point is that these vaccinations were immunizations against a disease. We were assured that we would not get smallpox, polio, measles or whatever else we were vaccinated for. And we didn’t—not just a lesser amount or a case not as severe. We understood that we were immunized, and the fight was over.

During the current pandemic we kept hearing about the vaccination that was coming. It sounded like this was going to be the answer to this pestilence that had settled on the world. Some of us wondered if this would be like the flu shot that targets certain viruses, while it misses the other flu viruses. As the drama unfolded, we soon began to hear of variants and the need for booster shots. We now know for sure that this shot does not give an immunization for Covid 19, and hence, for clarity it is better to call it a flu shot.

I remember so well farming in the early 90’s and hearing about Roundup-Ready crops. It seemed too good to be true to be able to spray glyphosate (Roundup) over the top of the crop and take out all the weeds while doing no harm to the crop. The manufacturer did keep telling us to spray maximum rates so as to ‘kill’ every weed. Theoretically they were right, if we could have killed every weed, without missing one, we would not have had the next problem—spray-resistant weeds. We didn’t realize how fast our troublesome ‘pigweeds’ (and other weeds) in the south, would mutate and develop a resistance to glyphosate.

Sure, farmers had several good years with an easy way to keep out the weeds, but that didn’t last and now the situation is worse than it was before. Today, every farmer knows about ‘Palmer amaranth Pigweed’. You can almost ‘pour’ glyphosate on it, and still it thrives. These weeds mutated very rapidly and became resistant.

I think we have a similar scenario with the Covid shot. I’m certainly not a scientist but it does seem to me that since the shot admittedly mostly reduces symptoms instead of producing immunity, then it will most likely speed up the mutation of the Covid-19 virus. This seems like the normal ‘struggle for survival’ principle of life.

The rapid speed with which this shot came on the market is another concern. We really don’t know what all it will bring down the road nor the side effects it may cause. We don’t know how many boosters will be called for. It seems the world is the test field at the moment, and from what I’m seeing it is not working too well and many of the people who have had the shot don’t really trust it. The people who have had the virus have built an immunity that is far superior to the protection of the shot. We’ve known since childhood that when we had the flu, our body would build immunity to that strain. This is the way our Maker designed us. One of the first people I personally knew that had Covid was told they would have six months of immunity. I wondered how they figured that out so quickly. This was a new virus, and we had no experience to draw on for this virus. Also, the viruses we were familiar with gave lifetime immunity to that strain. So what science was behind this?

Hence, I think it much better to take precautions and do what we can to boost our immune system. It is an excellent time to remember we are to be stewards of the body that God gave us. It’s a good time to put a plan in place of good nutrition, exercise, and weight loss. If you are overweight, you are much more likely to be affected by this pestilence and many other illnesses. If you regularly consume sugary drinks or unhealthy foods of any kind, it is an excellent time to kick the habit and reduce your sugar consumption. If you are overweight or out of shape physically, there is no better time than now to bring your body into a condition that will be much healthier, so you will be better able to ward off this virus and many other illnesses.

My belief is that in the long run it will be safer and better to do my part and let this body build the immunities to protect itself against this virus. I realize there are those who have died after contracting this illness. I don’t belittle this fact and I am sorry for the loss of life. I do believe too that we as Christians should constantly commit our lives to God and look at the whole picture of life and its preservation through the lens of Christian ethics.

It is unprecedented that an illness with a recovery rate of somewhere around 99%, would cause such a stir, the world over. We know that if it wouldn’t be for the invention of social media there would not have been near the panic and turmoil. One of my greatest concerns is how we are being ‘conditioned’ for more to come. Who would have ever thought that a flu virus would be the instrument that ushers in a global push for something that will be the benchmark for whether we can travel, go to eating places, gather for public events and other such restrictions. It sounds strangely similar to what God says will one day be a reality—And he causeth all, both small and great, rich and poor, free and bond, to receive a mark in their right hand, or in their foreheads: And that no man might buy or sell, save he that had the mark, or the name of the beast, or the number of his name –Revelation 13:16-17.

I have been almost ridiculed for even mentioning the mark of the beast. Still others think this passage is to be spiritualized and has nothing to do with the end time system of government. Still others think the bride will be raptured before this, hence nothing for us to be concerned with. I could wish one of these views would be right, then I could move along in silence hoping that all would be well.

I will hasten to say that I don’t think this is the ‘mark of the beast’, but rather I see it as another step closer to that event. I also hasten to say that this is not a writing to ridicule another belief nor is it an effort to try to pull together certain Scriptures to try to support a particular doctrinal agenda such as the idea that all believers will be raptured prior to the unfolding of end time events, thereby escaping what the Bible refers to as “great tribulation”. –See Matthew 24:21 and Revelation 7:14. It’s time we open our eyes to the ‘conditioning’ that our society is having upon us in general, and the conditioning of this shot in particular. There are all kinds of good reasons we will go ahead with it—it makes good sense, it defies science not to, I’ve even heard we can be better witnesses if we have had it, and the list goes on. All the while we are being ‘conditioned’ to do what it takes to keep rolling down our economic road.

So, my plea is that we consider where we are headed. One day God’s people will need to jump off the train of this world—Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you –2 Corinthians 6:17. Revelation 14:10-11 declares that all who take the mark will seal their destiny in hell. The next verse gives a calling for the endurance of the saints—Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus –Revelation 14:12.

There will be hard times—Read Matthew 24:4-28. Consider the famines, pestilences, and earthquakes that are promised will come. Jesus said all these are the beginnings of sorrows—literally birth pangs. He said along with this, ‘the end is not yet’. Yet we have the promise of triumph—And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death –Revelation 12:11. I say again, “One day the saints will need to jump off the economic train.”

I think now is an excellent time to evaluate our attachment, whether it is connected to this world or to our future heavenly reward. Let’s make a commitment anew to identify with our soon coming Lord and King. Also, it’s an excellent time to share the gospel of Jesus’ Kingdom with a society that is bent on going away from the Creator.

So, for now, I’m content to feel safe with the immunity in my body as God created it and I am purposing in a new way to seek the immunity from the ways of sin and evil and to be inoculated with the Holy Ghost from heaven. Will you join me in this commitment?

मैंने कोविड शॉट के बारे में सुनकर और यहां तक ​​कि इस विषय पर बहसों में भाग लेकर आनंद लिया है—क्यों किसी ने इसे लिया है, और क्यों किसी ने नहीं लिया। मैं कहने की हिम्मत करता हूँ कि हम सात लोगों से उनका दृष्टिकोण सुन सकते हैं और शायद आठ अलग-अलग विचार मिल सकते हैं।

मैं यह स्पष्ट करते हुए शुरू करता हूँ कि ये मेरे विचार हैं, और मुझे ठीक लगता है अगर कोई असहमत हो। वास्तव में, मैं दूसरों से उनके दृष्टिकोण साझा करने का स्वागत करूंगा।

इस लेख में आप जो बात देखेंगे वह यह है कि मैं कोविड शॉट को 'वैक्सीन' नहीं कहता। यह तकनीकी रूप से आधिकारिक परिभाषा में फिट न बैठने के कारण नहीं है, बल्कि इसलिए कि यह उसी तरह काम नहीं करता जैसा हमने वैक्सीनों को काम करते देखा है। मुझे याद है जब मैं लगभग चार साल का था, मैं अपनी माँ के साथ स्वास्थ्य विभाग गया और मुझे ऊपरी बांह में चेचक के लिए टीका लगाया गया था। (वह दाग अभी भी है) मुझे कुछ वर्षों बाद याद है जब पूरा समुदाय हमारे स्थानीय सार्वजनिक स्कूल में पॉलियो के खिलाफ मौखिक टीकाकरण के लिए शक्कर के घन पर इकट्ठा हुआ था। मुझे याद नहीं कि मुझे और कोई टीकाकरण मिला था या नहीं। मेरा बिंदु यह है कि ये टीकाकरण किसी रोग के खिलाफ प्रतिरक्षण थे। हमें आश्वस्त किया गया था कि हमें चेचक, पॉलियो, खसरा या जिन अन्य चीज़ों के लिए हमें टीका लगाया गया था वे नहीं होंगे। और हम नहीं हुए—न केवल कम मात्रा में या हल्का मामला। हमने समझा कि हम प्रतिरक्षित हैं, और लड़ाई खत्म हो गई।

वर्तमान महामारी के दौरान हमें लगातार उस टीकाकरण के बारे में सुनने को मिलता रहा जो आने वाला था। यह लग रहा था कि यही उस प्रकोप का उत्तर होगा जिसने संसार पर कब्ज़ा कर लिया था। हम में से कुछ को आश्चर्य हुआ कि क्या यह फ्लू शॉट जैसा होगा जो कुछ वायरसों को लक्षित करता है, जबकि अन्य फ्लू वायरसों को चूक जाता है। जैसे-जैसे नाटक unfolded हुआ, हमने जल्दी ही वेरिएंट्स और बूस्टर शॉट्स की आवश्यकता के बारे में सुनना शुरू कर दिया। अब हम निश्चित रूप से जानते हैं कि इस शॉट से कोविड-19 के लिए प्रतिरक्षण नहीं मिलता, और इसलिए, स्पष्टता के लिए इसे फ्लू शॉट कहना बेहतर है।

मुझे ठीक-ठीक याद है कि 90 के दशक की शुरुआत में खेती करते हुए राउंडअप-रीडी फसलों के बारे में सुनना। ऐसा लगता था कि यह सच होने के लिए बहुत अच्छा है कि आप फसल के ऊपर ग्लाइफोसेट (राउंडअप) छिड़क सकें और सभी खरपतवारों को मार सकें जबकि फसल को कोई नुकसान न पहुंचे। निर्माता हमें लगातार अधिकतम दर पर छिड़कने के लिए कहता रहा ताकि हर एक खरपतवार को ‘मार’ दिया जाए। सैद्धांतिक रूप से वे सही थे, यदि हम हर एक खरपतवार को मार सकते थे, बिना किसी को छोड़ें, तो हमें अगली समस्या—स्प्रे-प्रतिरोधी खरपतवार—नहीं होती। हमें एहसास नहीं था कि हमारे दक्षिण के कष्टप्रद 'पिगवीड्स' (और अन्य खरपतवार) कितनी तेज़ी से उत्परिवर्तित होंगे और ग्लाइफोसेट के प्रति प्रतिरोध विकसित कर लेंगे।

ज़रूर, किसानों के कुछ अच्छे साल थे जब खरपतवारों को रोके रखने का सरल तरीका था, पर वह टिक नहीं सका और अब स्थिति पहले से भी खराब है। आज, हर किसान 'पालमर अमरन्थ पिगवीड' के बारे में जानता है। आप उस पर लगभग ग्लाइफोसेट 'पोर' कर सकते हैं, और फिर भी वह पनपता है। ये खरपतवार बहुत तेज़ी से उत्परिवर्तित हुए और प्रतिरोधी बन गए।

मुझे लगता है कि कोविड शॉट के साथ भी एक समान परिदृश्य है। मैं निश्चित रूप से वैज्ञानिक नहीं हूं लेकिन मुझे ऐसा लगता है कि चूंकि शॉट स्पष्ट रूप से ज्यादातर लक्षणों को कम करता है बजाय प्रतिरक्षण पैदा करने के, यह संभावित रूप से कोविड-19 वायरस के उत्परिवर्तन को तेज कर देगा। यह जीवन के सामान्य 'जीवन के लिए संघर्ष' सिद्धांत जैसा लगता है।

जिस तेजी से यह शॉट बाजार में आया वह एक और चिंता का विषय है। हमें वास्तव में नहीं पता कि इससे आगे क्या कुछ आएगा और कौन-कौन से साइड इफेक्ट्स हो सकते हैं। हमें यह नहीं पता कि कितने बूस्टर्स की मांग की जाएगी। ऐसा लगता है कि इस समय दुनिया परीक्षण क्षेत्र है, और जो मैं देख रहा हूँ उससे यह ठीक नहीं चल रहा और जिन कई लोगों ने शॉट लिया है वे वास्तव में उस पर भरोसा नहीं करते। जिन लोगों को वायरस हुआ है उन्होंने जो प्रतिरक्षा बनाई है वह शॉट की सुरक्षा से कहीं अधिक श्रेष्ठ है। बचपन से ही हम जानते हैं कि जब हमें फ्लू होता था, तो हमारे शरीर उस स्ट्रेन के प्रति प्रतिरक्षा बना लेते थे। यही हमारा बनाने वाला हमें डिजाइन करने के तरीके के अनुरूप है। जिन्हें मैंने व्यक्तिगत रूप से कोविड हुआ देखा उनमें से एक को बताया गया कि उनके पास छह महीने की प्रतिरक्षा होगी। मुझे अचरज हुआ कि उन्होंने यह इतनी जल्दी कैसे निकाला। यह एक नया वायरस था, और हमारे पास इस वायरस के लिए अनुभव के रूप में कुछ भी नहीं था। साथ ही, जिन वायरसों से हम परिचित थे वे उस स्ट्रेन के लिए जीवन भर की प्रतिरक्षा देते थे। तो इसके पीछे क्या विज्ञान था?

इसलिए, मुझे लगता है कि सावधानी बरतना और अपने प्रतिरक्षा तंत्र को बढ़ाने के लिए जो कुछ भी हम कर सकते हैं वह करना बेहतर है। यह याद रखने का एक उत्कृष्ट समय है कि हमें उस शरीर का संरक्षक होना चाहिए जो परमेश्वर ने हमें दिया है। अच्छा समय है कि अच्छे पोषण, व्यायाम और वजन घटाने की योजना बनायी जाए। यदि आप अधिक वजन वाले हैं, तो आप इस महामारी और कई अन्य बीमारियों से प्रभावित होने की अधिक संभावना रखते हैं। यदि आप नियमित रूप से चीनी युक्त पेय या किसी भी प्रकार के अस्वस्थ भोजन का सेवन करते हैं, तो यह आदत छोड़ने और अपनी चीनी की खपत कम करने का उत्तम समय है। यदि आप अधिक वजन या शारीरिक रूप से बेढंगे हैं, तो अपने शरीर को एक ऐसी स्थिति में लाने के लिए अब से बेहतर समय नहीं है जो बहुत अधिक स्वस्थ होगी, ताकि आप इस वायरस और कई अन्य बीमारियों से खुद का बेहतर तरीके से रक्षा कर सकें।

मेरा विश्वास है कि दीर्घकाल में यह अधिक सुरक्षित और बेहतर होगा कि मैं अपना हिस्सा करूँ और इस शरीर को अपने आप के प्रति सुरक्षा बनाने दूँ ताकि यह इस वायरस के खिलाफ खुद को संरक्षित करे। मुझे एहसास है कि ऐसे लोग हैं जो इस बीमारी से संक्रमित होने के बाद मरे। मैं इस तथ्य को छोटा नहीं समझता और जीवन के खो जाने के लिए दुखी हूँ। मैं यह भी मानता हूँ कि हमें, ईसाईयों के रूप में, लगातार अपने जीवन को परमेश्वर को सौंपना चाहिए और जीवन के पूरे परिदृश्य और उसकी रक्षा को ईसाइयाई नैतिकता के लेंस के माध्यम से देखना चाहिए।

यह अभूतपूर्व है कि लगभग 99% के आसपास की रिकवरी दर वाली बीमारी ने दुनिया भर में इतनी हलचल पैदा कर दी। हम जानते हैं कि अगर सोशल मीडिया का आविष्कार न होता तो इतनी घबराहट और उथल-पुथल नहीं होती। मेरी सबसे बड़ी चिंताओं में से एक यह है कि हमें और आने वाली चीजों के लिए कैसे 'कंडीशन्ड' किया जा रहा है। कौन सोच सकता था कि एक फ्लू वायरस वह यंत्र होगा जो वैश्विक दबाव को शुरू करेगा—कुछ ऐसा जो यह तय करेगा कि हम यात्रा कर सकते हैं या नहीं, भोजनालयों में जा सकते हैं, सार्वजनिक कार्यक्रमों के लिए इकट्ठा हो सकते हैं और अन्य सीमाओं के लिए। यह उस चीज़ के अजीब समान लगता है जो परमेश्वर कहता है कि एक दिन वास्तविकता होगी—And he causeth all, both small and great, rich and poor, free and bond, to receive a mark in their right hand, or in their foreheads: And that no man might buy or sell, save he that had the mark, or the name of the beast, or the number of his name –Revelation 13:16-17.

मुझे लगभग टोकहंसा झेलनी पड़ी जब मैंने यहाँ दैत्य के चिह्न का उल्लेख किया। फिर भी अन्य लोग सोचते हैं कि इस पद्यांश को आध्यात्मिकृत किया जाना चाहिए और इसका अंतकालीन शासन प्रणाली से कोई संबंध नहीं है। कुछ अन्य लोग सोचते हैं कि दुल्हन इस सब से पहले ही रैप्चर हो जाएगी, इसलिए हमें चिंतित होने की कोई जरूरत नहीं। काश इनमें से कोई दृष्टिकोण सही होता, तो मैं चुपचाप आगे बढ़ सकता और आशा कर सकता कि सब ठीक हो जाएगा।

मैं जल्दी कह दूँ कि मुझे नहीं लगता यह 'दैत्य का चिह्न' है, बल्कि मैं इसे उस घटना के और करीब जाने वाला एक और कदम देखता हूँ। मैं यह भी शीघ्रता से कहता हूँ कि यह लेख किसी अन्य विश्वास का मजाक उड़ाने के लिए नहीं है और न ही यह कुछ विशिष्ट शास्त्रीय एजेंडा का समर्थन करने के लिए कुछ शास्त्रों को जोड़ने का प्रयत्न है, जैसे कि विचार कि सभी विश्वासी अंतकालीन घटनाओं के प्रकट होने से पहले ही रैप्चर हो जाएंगे, और इस प्रकार बाइबल द्वारा "महान विपत्ति" कहलाने वाली चीज़ से बच जाएंगे। –See Matthew 24:21 and Revelation 7:14. यह समय है कि हम अपनी आँखें खोलें कि हमारी समाज पर सामान्य रूप से क्या 'कंडीशनिंग' हो रही है, और इस शॉट की कंडीशनिंग विशेष रूप से। इसके समर्थन में तरह-तरह के अच्छे कारण हैं—यह तर्कसंगत लगता है, यह विज्ञान के खिलाफ नहीं जाना चाहिए, मैंने यहाँ तक सुना है कि अगर हमने इसे लिया है तो हम बेहतर साक्षी बन सकते हैं, और सूची चलती रहती है। इसी बीच हम 'कंडीशन्ड' हो रहे हैं ताकि अपने आर्थिक मार्ग पर बने रहें।

तो, मेरी विनती है कि हम विचार करें कि हम कहां जा रहे हैं। एक दिन परमेश्वर के लोगों को इस दुनिया की ट्रेन से कूदना होगा—Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you –2 Corinthians 6:17. प्रकाशितवाक्य 14:10-11 बताता है कि जो भी चिह्न लेगा वह अपने भाग्य को नर्क में सील कर देगा। अगला पद्यांश धर्मियों की धैर्य की पुकार देता है—Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus –Revelation 14:12.

कठिन समय आने वाले हैं—Read Matthew 24:4-28. उन अकालों, महामारी और भूकंपों पर विचार करें जो आने का वादा किया गया है। यीशु ने कहा कि ये सब वे दुखों की शुरुआत हैं—शब्दशः प्रसव वेदनाएँ। उन्होंने यह भी कहा कि 'अंत अभी नहीं है'। फिर भी हमारे पास विजय का वादा है—And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death –Revelation 12:11. मैं फिर कहता हूँ, "एक दिन धर्मियों को आर्थिक ट्रेन से कूदना होगा।"

The angel of the LORD encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them –Psalm 34:7.

“Tell us a story, Grandma,” begged two eager children as they crowded around her rocking chair.

“My, my, you children like to hear stories, don’t you?” replied Grandma, with a twinkle in her eye. “All right, I’ll tell you about a time when I was about eight years old, and my sister Lori was nine.

We lived on an old farm, back a short lane along a dirt road. One morning, Mother called us in from our play and said she was out of sugar. She asked us to walk to Mrs. Brightbill to see if she had any sugar to spare. You see, we didn’t have telephones when I was a little girl, so she couldn’t call the neighbor and ask her. Neighbors often shared back and forth because we didn’t go shopping at the store very often either. So, mother gave us a container, and we started out on our long walk as Mother called after us and reminded us not to loiter along the way.”

“How far was it to the Brightbills?” asked Sharon.

“Oh, it was about half a mile to our closest neighbor, the Rhine’s place, and then about another quarter of a mile to the Brightbills,” replied Grandma.

“Oh, that’s far. Mother won’t let us walk on the road at all,” added Micah.

“I’m sure you are right,” agreed Grandma. “And I hope you never walk on the road without your parents’ permission. But things were much different when I was a little girl. We also walked every day to school, which was quite a bit further than the Brightbill farm. So, the little errand we were doing on this morning for Mother seemed like fun. There was only one problem though. The Rhine family had an old man living in their summer house. His name was Pierce, and he had a very fierce dog; at least he acted very fierce! He was kept behind a high wire fence connected to an old shed.

Every day when we walked to school, that dog frightened us terribly with his fierce barking and growling. But Mother always reminded us to pray and remember the Bible verse which says: What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee –Psalm 56:3. Still, we hurried by as fast as our legs could take us.

Lori and I started out happily on our errand for Mother. We skipped along, watching the dust swirl beneath our feet on that warm summer morning. Everything seemed unusually quiet and still as we passed through the gully, over the rippling creek, and up the steep hill right before Neighbor Rhine’s place. There before us was the old shed, and on the other side was the high fence which kept in Pierce’s mean dog. My heart began to thump rapidly. ‘Maybe that bad dog hadn’t seen us yet,’ I thought gratefully as I whispered once more to myself, ‘I will trust and not be afraid.’

Suddenly, the air was shattered by the ferocious barking of that mean dog as he sprang around the corner of the old shed! Lori and I froze in our tracks! As that angry dog raced toward us, Lori screamed. The next moment, I realized she had fallen down and was sitting in the middle of the dirt road, with her hands behind her on the hard packed gravel, feet and legs in the air, kicking and kicking, spinning around and around as that angry dog circled her, jumping in at her and nipping at her feet and legs! I was so scared. I just stood frozen to the spot. I don’t remember if I screamed, or if I prayed. But suddenly there was a shout! It was Pierce, with a whip in his hand. He came running around the shed and out on the road. He whipped and whipped that dog and finally got him away from Lori and back inside the fence where he belonged, as Lori and I stood there, trembling, and crying with relief.”

“Wow!” exclaimed Sharon. “That was really scary, wasn’t it?”

“Did Pierce need to get rid of his dog?” asked Micah.

“Yes, Sharon, it was very scary,” answered Grandma. “And no, Micah, Pierce did not get rid of his dog. We children needed to keep trusting the good Lord to keep us safe every day.”

“I don’t remember what happened after Pierce got the dog away that day, or if we ever got Mother’s sugar, but I will never forget what happened that day.

It was a miracle that Lori and I were not injured. There is a verse in Psalms which says: Save me from the lion’s mouth… –Psalm 22:21. How thankful we were to be delivered from the dog’s mouth! I like to think that the Lord’s angel had his sword drawn in front of that dog’s mouth every time he leaped at my dear sister.”

Malaika wa Bwana huweka kambi karibu na wale wamnaye hofu, na kuwaokoa –Zaburi 34:7.

“Tuambie hadithi, Bibi,” walimwomba watoto wawili wenye hamu waliokuwa wamekataana kando ya kiti chake cha kuzunguka.

“Ee, nyinyi watoto mnapenda kusikia hadithi, sivyo?” Bibi akajibu kwa tabasamu machoni. “Sawa, nitawaambia kuhusu wakati nilipokuwa na umri wa takriban miaka nane, na dada yangu Lori alikuwa na miaka tisa.

Tulikaa kwenye shamba la zamani, nyuma ya barabara fupi iliyo na udongo. Siku moja asubuhi, Mama alitutaka tupite kutoka kwenye mchezo na alisema chakula cha sukari kimeisha. Alituomba tukatembee hadi kwa Bi. Brightbill kuona kama angeweza kutushiria sukari. Tazama, hatukuwa na simu nilipokuwa mtoto, kwa hivyo hakuweza kumpigia jirani simu kumuomba. Majirani mara nyingi walishirikiana kwa kubadilishana kwa sababu hatukuenda kununua dukani sana pia. Hivyo, mama alitupa chombo, na tukaanza kutembea umbali mrefu huku mama akitutaka nyuma na kutukumbusha tusibaki kando ya njia.”

“Ilikuwa mbali kiasi gani hadi kwa nyumba ya Brightbill?” Sharon aliuliza.

“Oh, ilikuwa takriban nusu maili hadi kwa jirani wetu wa karibu, nyumba ya Rhine, na kisha karibu robo ya maili nyingine hadi kwa Brightbill,” Bibi akajibu.

“Oh, ni mbali. Mama hataturuhusu kutembea barabarani kabisa,” Micah aliongeza.

“Nina hakika uko sawa,” Bibi akakubali. “Na natumai hamtawahi kutembea barabarani bila ruhusa ya mzazi wenu. Lakini mambo yalikuwa tofauti sana nilipokuwa mtoto. Pia tulitembea kila siku kwenda shule, ambayo ilikuwa mbali zaidi kuliko shamba la Brightbill. Hivyo, kazi ndogo tuliyokuwa tukifanya asubuhi hiyo kwa ajili ya mama ilionekana kuwa ya kufurahisha. Kulikuwa na tatizo moja tu. Familia ya Rhine waliokuwa na mzee aliyeishi kwenye nyumba yao ya majira ya joto. Jina lake lilikuwa Pierce, na alikuwa na mbwa mwenye hasira kali; angalau hufanya kiwoga! Alihifadhiwa nyuma ya uzio wa waya mrefu uliounganishwa na gereji ya zamani.

Kila siku tulipokuwa tukitembea shule, mbwa huyo alitutisha sana kwa kulemaza na kupiga kelele. Lakini Mama kila mara alitukumbusha kuomba na kukumbuka mstari wa Biblia unaosema: Iwapo nitakuwa na hofu, nitakuamini –Zaburi 56:3. Bado, tulikimbia kwa haraka kadiri miguu yetu ilivyoweza.

Lori na mimi tulianza kwa furaha kwenye kazi yetu ya kumwendea mama. Tuliruka-ruka tukitazama vumbi likizunguka chini ya miguu yetu katika asubuhi ya joto ya majira ya msimu. Kila kitu kilionekana kimetiwa kimya sana tulipopita kwenye mto mdogo, kuvuka kijito kinachotiririka, na kupanda kilima chenye mteremko kabla kabisa ya nyumba ya jirani Rhine. Hapo mbele yetu ilikuwa gereji ya zamani, na upande mwingine kulikuwa uzio mrefu uliokuwa umeweka mbwa mchafu wa Pierce ndani. Moyo wangu ulianza kupiga kwa nguvu. ‘Labda mbwa huyo mbaya hakuwa ametuona bado,’ nilifikiria kwa shukrani nikiwa ninamnong’ona kwa mara nyingine ndani yangu, ‘nitaamini na sitatafuta hofu.’

Ghafula, anga likavunjika kwa mkwavyo mkali wa mbwa huyo mchafu aliporuka pembezoni mwa gereji ya zamani! Lori na mimi tulishika mguu pale tuliposimama! Wakati mbwa huyo mwenye hasira alipokimbia kuelekea kwetu, Lori alilia kwa sauti. Wakati uliofuata, nilitambua alikuwa ameporomoka chini na kukaa katikati ya barabara ya udongo, akiwa mikononi nyuma kwenye lulu ya changarawe ngumu, miguu na mabega juu angani, akiruka na kuruka, akizunguka kwa mviringo huku mbwa huyo mwenye hasira akimzunguka, akiruka kumgonga na kumkamata kwa miguu na mabega! Nilikuwa na hofu sana. Nilisimama tu nikiwa nimekatizwa mahali. Sihukumi kama nililia, au kama niliomba. Lakini ghatia ghafla kulikuwa na kupiga kelele! Ilikuwa Pierce, akiwa na fimbo mkononi. Alikuja akikimbia akizunguka gereji na kutoka barabarani. Alimpiga fimbo mbwa huyo mara nyingi na mara nyingi hadi awasafishe kutoka kwa Lori na kumrudisha ndani ya uzio pale alipotakiwa, wakati Lori na mimi tulisimama pale, tukitetemeka, na kuangua machozi kwa ahueni.”

“Nzuri!” Sharon alisema kwa mshangao. “Hilo lilikuwa la kutisha sana, sivyo?”

“Je, Pierce alihitaji kuondoa mbwa wake?” Micah aliuliza.

“Ndiyo, Sharon, lilikuwa la kutisha sana,” Bibi akajibu. “Na la, Micah, Pierce hakuondoa mbwa wake. Sisi watoto tulihitaji kuendelea kumtumainia Bwana mrefu kuwalinda kila siku.”

“Sikumbuki kilichotokea baada ya Pierce kumpa mbwa ghafla siku hiyo, au kama hatukuwahi kupata sukari ya Mama, lakini sitasahau kile kilichotokea siku hiyo.

Ilikuwa muujiza kwamba Lori na mimi hatukujeruhiwa. Kuna mistari katika Zaburi inayosema: Niniondoshe kinywani pa simba… –Zaburi 22:21. Tulikuwa na shukrani sana kuokolewa kutoka kinywani pa mbwa! Napenda kufikiria kuwa malaika wa Bwana alikuwa amepiga upanga mbele ya kinywa cha mbwa kila wakati alipopiga shika kwa dada yangu mpendwa.”

Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted?… –Matthew 5:13.

One might wonder as to why the Anabaptists, the early church fathers, church history writers, and especially the progenitor (originator or author) of our beliefs, Christ Himself, effected such a vehement and absolute approach to a separated church and state. Why did they unanimously preach, write, and otherwise caution against political involvement of any kind by Christians? Perhaps this is best answered by looking at the results of Christians ignoring these sincere warnings, casting off their Godly allegiance, and pledging themselves to a flawed and ultimately futile earthly kingdom.

The Mennonites of Germany are a particularly intriguing and cautionary episode of Christian and Anabaptist histories—not only because of their relative proximity to our time—but also because of their almost wholesale devotion to a worldly leader and agenda. What led them to such an un-Christ-like position? A true understanding of their story must begin, naturally, with their beginnings.

The Mennonites of 20th century Germany were descended from the first Anabaptist groups, but unlike our ancestors, they stayed in the Old World instead of emigrating to the New World. There, a number of factors led them to a unique position within world events, a position that would test their mettle on a global stage.

The beginnings of the 20th century brought about the first World War, which ended with the defeat of Germany and its allies. The resulting peace treaties were structured to humiliate and crush Germany, saddling it with an almost unpayable war debt, and restricting its rights to build a military. The German people, unsurprisingly, resented this insult being added to the injury of having lost the War. Their resentment festered, and soon manifested itself in nationalistic movements, the most notable of which was the National Socialist German Workers Party (or the Nazi Party). The party was founded in 1919, and Hitler was amongst its first members. He quickly assumed party leadership, attracting followers with his “us vs. them” rhetoric and strong leadership.

Party growth was small in the decade following its founding. During this time, Hitler continued to shape the Nazis according to his wishes. Hatred for most non-German (Aryan) groups became a central party theme, along with a violent distaste for communism. However, the party was not large enough to be anything but a fringe voice, representing only a small portion of German voters.

Insignificance did not last, however. The Great Depression brought the catalyst for the Nazi’s rise to power. When the global market crashed, over 2 million Germans lost their jobs. Unemployed, they rallied around the charismatic leadership that promised to give them jobs, give them power, to “Make Germany great again”. Moving quickly, Hitler added legions to his followers.

The thousands of new Nazi Party members enabled the Nazi Party to seriously contest many local elections, and in Germany’s Parliament, they were able to control enough votes to sway policy making. In the long run, their political might handed Hitler the office of prime minister. Having secured that position, he went on to overthrow the German government, establishing himself and his party as the undisputed rulers of Germany.

Why did such a man, and such a movement, attract the attention and adoration of a church that professed much of what we do? Loving our enemies, separation from the world, and nonresistance did not seem to combine with the message of the Nazis. The answer, like most backsliding churches, is best portrayed as happening in small steps and over time.

In 1929, the Mennonites came under the eye of Germany and its rapidly expanding Nazi Party. 13,000 Russian Mennonite refugees descended on Moscow, seeking an exit from the Communist-run country. The Nazis seized the situation, using the Mennonites as supposed evidence that Aryans (peoples of German lineage, such as the Mennonites) were being unjustly used by the rest of the world. This image was pushed by state propaganda departments, who circulated writings, pamphlets, and even two immensely popular movies, depicting the Mennonites as strong, red-blooded Germans valiantly striving against the unjust oppression of the Russian Communists. These efforts afforded the refugees national attention, which subsequently led to them being admitted into Germany.

While many Mennonites entered Germany, as refugees and otherwise, there were also thriving, established communities that were given the same patriotic make-over by the Nazi propogandists. Unfortunately, these churches welcomed the Nazi attention, going so far as to send Hitler a letter thanking him for being the “savior of the German peoples” and pledging their support to his government. It is of note that Hitler, a man quite busy running an emerging world power, personally responded to this letter with a memo thanking the churches for their support and expressing a desire for further cooperation to the benefit of both the Nazis and the Mennonites. The church further weakened under these seemingly beneficial relations.

A particularly shocking case of Mennonite political involvement came from the churches in or around Danzig. Danzig and the surrounding countryside had long been a part of the German Empire, until the end of World War I, when the region was separated from Germany, essentially becoming a buffer zone between Germany and Poland. In 1939, Hitler would make one of his first moves on Europe by annexing Danzig, where the Nazis had been building party influence for most of the 1930’s. The Mennonites of the area, having been German only a generation before, welcomed their new part in the Germany of the future, becoming involved in almost every level of the Nazi Party. Otto Andres became the second-highest ranked Nazi of the Danzig area, and scores of the 6,000 believers in the surrounding congregations joined various Nazi organizations. The men often took part in the paramilitary SA and SS, while their wives and daughters took part in corresponding women’s groups. Churches became saturated with active Nazis, even going so far as to accept them into church leadership. At one point, five of the seven local churches were led by active party members.

World War II was the final step in the Mennonites’ integration with the Nazis. The German concentration camp of Stutthof supplied slave labor to numerous Mennonite businesses. Mennonite churches organized war efforts, including recruiting their young men to serve in the German army. In a particularly twisted case, a Mennonite doctor, Johan Klassen, was personally responsible for the deaths of more than one hundred disabled children.

Perhaps the most concerning episode in this dismal tale of backsliding comes after the war. Mennonite leadership, recognizing to some extent the terrible depths to which they had fallen, and noting the justice that was to come through the Nuremburg trials, effectively shrugged the blame from off their shoulders. Appealing to their Mennonite brothers across the ocean, they convinced them of their innocence, twisting their involvement in the Nazi regime to make themselves appear the victims. American Mennonites helped these now-refugees in many ways, providing all manner of assistance, and ultimately keeping most of them from facing possible prison time or death sentences. The surviving German churches eventually disintegrated or emigrated to the Americas.

If a group who originally held beliefs identical to our own could stray to the point of child murder and slave labor, then the question must be asked: “Are we seeing their folly for what it was?” Why did the churches of Danzig accept the advances of what, in retrospect, was a clearly un-biblical, un-Christlike movement?

The origin for their downfall was surprisingly simple. The Mennonites of Germany forgot who their true Ruler was. No earthly kingdom at war tolerates an allegiance to the enemy, and neither does the Kingdom of Heaven. The pride in their earthly kingdom, the pursuit of prestige and power, all led to a foreseeable end. Their salt had lost its savor, and they were cast out and trodden underfoot. This is a cautionary tale of the dangers of an unequal yoking of the church with the world.

너희는 세상의 소금이니 소금이 만일 그 맛을 잃으면 무엇으로 짜게 하리요 … –마태복음 5:13.

어째서 아나바프티스트, 초대 교부들, 교회사 저자들 그리고 무엇보다 우리의 신앙의 창시자이신 그리스도 자신이 그렇게도 단호하고 절대적인 교회와 국가의 분리를 주장했는지 의아해할 수 있다. 왜 그들은 만장일치로 기독교인의 어떤 형태의 정치적 개입에 대해서도 설교하고 글을 쓰며 경고했는가? 아마도 가장 잘 답할 수 있는 방법은 이런 진실한 경고들을 무시하고 그들의 경건한 충성을 버리며 결함 있고 궁극적으로 헛된 이 세상의 왕국에 충성을 맹세한 결과를 보는 것일 것이다.

독일의 메노나이트들은 특히 흥미롭고 경계할 만한 기독교 및 아나바프티스트 역사상의 한 에피소드이다—그들이 우리의 시대와 비교적 가깝다는 점뿐만 아니라—그들이 거의 전적으로 세속적 지도자와 의제에 헌신했다는 점 때문이다. 무엇이 그들을 그렇게 비그리스도적인 입장으로 이끌었는가? 그들의 이야기를 진정으로 이해하려면, 당연히 그들의 시작부터 출발해야 한다.

20세기 독일의 메노나이트들은 초기 아나바프티스트 집단의 후손이었지만, 우리의 조상들과 달리 신대륙으로 이주하지 않고 구세계에 남아 있었다. 그곳에서 여러 요인이 그들을 세계사적 사건들 속에서 독특한 위치로 이끌었고, 그 위치는 그들의 용기를 세계 무대에서 시험에 들게 했다.

20세기 초의 시작은 제1차 세계대전을 가져왔고 그 전쟁은 독일과 동맹국의 패배로 끝났다. 그 결과의 평화 조약들은 독일을 굴욕적으로 압박하도록 구성되어 거의 갚을 수 없을 정도의 전쟁 배상금을 부과하고 군대 유지 권리를 제한했다. 독일 국민은 당연히 전쟁에서 패한 부상 위에 이런 모욕이 더해진 것을 분개했다. 그들의 분노는 곪아 터졌고 곧 국가주의 운동으로 표출되었으며, 그 중 가장 주목할 만한 것이 국가사회주의 독일 노동자당(또는 나치당)이었다. 이 당은 1919년에 창당되었고 히틀러는 초기 구성원 중 하나였다. 그는 곧 당의 지도자가 되어 '우리 대 그들'이라는 수사와 강한 리더십으로 추종자들을 끌어모았다.

창당 이후 10년 동안 당의 성장은 미미했다. 이 기간 동안 히틀러는 나치를 자신의 뜻대로 계속 형성해 나갔다. 대부분의 비(非)독일(아리안) 집단에 대한 증오는 당의 중심 주제가 되었고 공산주의에 대한 폭력적 혐오도 함께하였다. 그러나 당은 독일 유권자의 극히 일부만을 대표하는 변두리적 목소리에 불과했다.

그러나 무의미함은 오래가지 못했다. 대공황은 나치의 집권을 촉발시키는 계기가 되었다. 세계 시장이 붕괴했을 때 200만 명이 넘는 독일인들이 일자리를 잃었다. 실업 상태에 처한 그들은 일자리를 주고 권력을 주며 '독일을 다시 위대하게 만들겠다'고 약속한 카리스마 있는 지도력 주위에 결집했다. 히틀러는 신속히 추종자들을 늘렸다.

새로 가입한 수천 명의 나치당원들은 나치당이 여러 지역 선거에서 진지하게 경쟁할 수 있게 했고, 독일 의회에서는 정책을 좌우할 만큼의 표를 확보할 수 있게 했다. 장기적으로 그들의 정치적 힘은 히틀러에게 총리의 자리를 안겨주었다. 그 자리를 확보한 후 그는 독일 정부를 전복시키고 자신과 그의 당을 독일의 논쟁의 여지 없는 지배자로 세웠다.

어째서 그러한 인물과 운동이 우리와 많은 점에서 동일한 신앙을 고백했던 한 교회의 주목과 숭배를 끌었는가? 원수를 사랑하고 세상과의 분리와 비저항을 가르치던 메시지가 나치의 메시지와 결코 일치하지 않는 것으로 보였는데 말이다. 그 해답은 대부분 타락한 교회들처럼 작은 단계로, 그리고 시간이 흐르며 일어난 일로 가장 잘 설명된다.

1929년에 메노나이트들은 독일과 빠르게 팽창하던 나치당의 눈에 띄게 되었다. 13,000명의 러시아 메노나이트 난민들이 모스크바로 몰려들어 공산주의 치하의 국가에서 탈출구를 찾았다. 나치는 이 상황을 이용하여 메노나이트들을 아리안(메노나이트와 같은 독일 혈통 민족)이 온 세상으로부터 불공정하게 박해받고 있다는 소위 증거로 사용했다. 국영 선전 기관들은 메노나이트들을 강건하고 혈기 왕성한 독일인으로 묘사하여 러시아 공산주의자들의 부당한 압제로부터 용감히 싸우는 모습을 그린 글, 팸플릿, 심지어 두 편의 대단히 인기 있는 영화를 유포했다. 이러한 노력은 난민들에게 국가적 관심을 가져다주었고, 그 결과 그들이 독일에 입국하는 길이 열렸다.

많은 메노나이트들이 난민으로서 독일에 입국했을 뿐 아니라 이미 번성하고 정착한 공동체들도 있었고, 이들 또한 나치 선전가들에 의해 같은 애국적 이미지로 치장되었다. 불행히도 이 교회들은 나치의 관심을 환영했고, 심지어 히틀러에게 그를 '독일 민족의 구원자'라 칭하며 그의 정부에 대한 지지를 약속하는 편지를 보내기까지 했다. 바쁜 세계 강국을 운영하던 한 남성이었던 히틀러는 이 편지에 대해 직접 메모로 교회들의 지지에 감사를 표하고 나치와 메노나이트 양쪽에 유익한 추가 협력을 희망한다는 뜻을 표명하며 응답했다는 점은 주목할 만하다. 이러한 겉으로는 유익해 보이는 관계 아래에서 교회는 더욱 약화되었다.

메노나이트의 정치적 개입에서 특히 충격적인 사례는 단치히와 그 주변 교회들에서 나왔다. 단치히와 그 주변 지역은 오랫동안 독일 제국의 일부였으나 제1차 세계대전의 종결 때 그 지역이 독일에서 분리되어 사실상 독일과 폴란드 사이의 완충지대가 되었다. 1939년에 히틀러는 단치히를 합병함으로써 유럽에 대한 첫 번째 움직임 중 하나를 했고, 나치들은 1930년대 대부분 동안 그곳에서 당의 영향력을 구축해 왔다. 그 지역의 메노나이트들은 한 세대 전만 해도 독일 사람이었기에 미래의 독일에서 자신들의 새로운 몫을 환영했고, 나치당의 거의 모든 수준에 관여하게 되었다. 오토 안드레스는 단치히 지역에서 두 번째로 높은 계급의 나치가 되었고, 주변 회중에 속한 6,000명 신자 중 수십 명이 다양한 나치 조직에 가입했다. 남성들은 종종 준군사조직인 SA와 SS에 참여했고, 아내들과 딸들은 해당 여성 단체들에 참여했다. 교회들은 적극적인 나치들로 포화되었고, 심지어 그들을 교회 지도자로 받아들이기까지 했다. 한때 일곱 지역 교회 중 다섯 곳이 활동적인 당원들에 의해 이끌리기도 했다.

제2차 세계대전은 메노나이트들이 나치와 통합되는 마지막 단계였다. 독일의 수트호프(Stutthof) 강제수용소는 수많은 메노나이트 사업체에 노예 노동을 공급했다. 메노나이트 교회들은 전쟁 노력을 조직했고, 젊은이들을 독일군에 징집하도록 했다. 특히 왜곡된 사례로는 메노나이트 의사 요한 클라센(Johan Klassen)이 백 명이 넘는 장애 아동들의 죽음에 개인적으로 책임이 있었다는 일이 있다.

이 암담한 타락 이야기에서 아마도 가장 우려스러운 에피소드는 전쟁 이후에 일어났다. 메노나이트 지도자들은 어느 정도 자신들이 빠진 끔찍한 나락을 인식했고 뉘른베르크 재판을 통해 내려질 정의를 알았음에도 불구하고 책임을 사실상 회피했다. 그들은 대서양 건너편의 메노나이트 형제들에게 호소하여 자신들의 무죄를 납득시키고, 나치 정권에서의 관여를 자신들이 피해자였던 것처럼 왜곡했다. 미국의 메노나이트들은 이러한 이제 난민이 된 이들을 여러 방식으로 도왔고 온갖 도움을 제공했으며 궁극적으로 그들 대부분이 감옥형이나 사형을 면하게 했다. 살아남은 독일 교회들은 결국 해체되거나 아메리카로 이주했다.

원래 우리와 동일한 신앙을 지녔던 집단이 아동 살해와 노예 노동의 지경까지 벗어날 수 있었다면, 질문을 던지지 않을 수 없다: "우리는 그들의 어리석음을 당시 그대로 보고 있는가?" 단치히의 교회들이 지금 돌이켜보면 명백히 비성경적이고 비그리스도적인 운동의 진척을 왜 받아들였는가?

그들의 몰락의 원인은 놀랍도록 단순했다. 독일의 메노나이트들은 그들의 참된 통치자가 누구인지 잊었다. 전쟁 중인 어떤 세속 왕국도 적에게 대한 충성을 용납하지 않으며, 천국의 왕국도 그렇지 않다. 그들의 세속 왕국에 대한 자부심과 명성과 권력을 추구한 것이 모두 예견 가능한 결말로 이어졌다. 그들의 소금은 맛을 잃었고 버림을 받아 사람들에게 밟혔다. 이것은 교회와 세상의 불평등한 멍에의 위험에 대한 경계 이야기이다.
