Greetings to each one in the worthy name of Jesus Christ, our Saviour, and our Redeemer.

This magazine issue may seem to be arriving more quickly on the heels of the last one. True. We are continuing to tighten up our schedule as we work towards getting each quarterly issue out in a more timely manner. Our ultimate goal is to have them arrive in your mailboxes in the months of March, June, September, and December of each year. Pray for us as we continue moving towards that schedule.

From time to time, we receive feedback—suggestions, concerns, and encouragement. We value this feedback. It is filed away and used by the board as we continually evaluate ways to make our magazine better. One final thought on this matter… when we receive feedback of encouragement regarding a specific article, it is helpful for us, and it is encouraging for our authors as we pass that along to them. We welcome your ongoing feedback.

As previously mentioned, we are including several new categories in this issue. One on Church History that is being written by two young brothers from our church. And one on Hymn Histories being written by one of our board members, a middle-aged married man, who is also from our church.

In “Moses in Midian”, we take a walk in Moses’ footsteps during the mid-section of his life. He was uprooted from his comfortable lifestyle in Egypt as an adopted son of royalty and was then sent by God into the desert to learn some much-needed lessons in further preparation towards becoming God’s servant. As we take a look at the life of Jonah, we glean glimpses of “The God Who Will Not Let Go”. Often a struggling believer loses sight of the Truth of God because they believe the lie that no one cares, yet the truth of the matter is this—the God of the Bible doesn’t just drop us, or turn His back on us, the instant that we take a wrong turn or a misstep. Let’s allow this article to help us to become rooted and grounded in the biblical Truth of Abba Father—a Father who cares for His children. We also have the second article in a continuing series on discipleship, as well as an article written by a middle-aged, spiritually-mature sister who shares her encouragement for sisters to evaluate what God thinks of their attire.

Church History and Should A Christian Vote

Finally, let’s consider the two short articles on church history. One of our goals for this issue is burdened with the awareness that the country in which we live (the U.S.) is approaching mid-term elections in November of this year and that there will be a strong push for many conservative Anabaptists to become involved in the voting process to ensure a proper outcome for the good of their perceived cause or goals.

In the natural world our “old man” has the tendency to think that we must “do something” if we expect things to go in a “right” direction. The spiritual Truth is this: The king’s heart is in the hand of the LORD, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will –Proverbs 21:1. If we think that, as believers, we will have a part in electing the “right” person in an election if we personally vote, let’s stop to consider what God Himself told Nebuchadnezzar. …That the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will –Daniel 4:31-32.

Throughout the history of the Anabaptist people there have been varied opinions on this matter, however, it is our wish to lift up the perspective that Jesus said …My kingdom is not of this world: if my kingdom were of this world, then would my servants fight … but now is my kingdom not from hence –John 18:36. When we understand and develop a personal world view that is founded on the two-kingdom principle, we realize that we must function as …strangers and pilgrims on the earth. [While we] …declare plainly that [we] seek a country …a better country, that is, an heavenly: wherefore God is not ashamed to be called [our] God: for he hath prepared for [us] a city –Hebrews 11:13-16. In all things involving political involvement, it is our encouragement that New Testament believers should obey the command to …come out from among them, and be ye separate… –2 Corinthians 6:17.

Let’s always cultivate a right attitude in our hearts so that our talk and actions reflect God’s view on the matter when He through the Apostle Paul tells us to: Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God … For he is the minister of God to thee… –Romans 13:1-4.

It is in consideration of these thoughts that we wrote the two articles detailing very different times in the history of the church and what it was like for Christians to relate to the government of their day. Let us seriously ponder whether we can do more good by getting involved in politics, especially in the voting process. Or whether God wants us to pray for our elected officials, to view them as His servants, and to speak about them with respect. Ultimately, we must trust God to bring about His will for the winding down of the “clock of time” as time speeds onward towards the end of time. God will do this through hardening the hearts of ungodly men in positions of power, just like Pharaoh of old, to accomplish His sovereign will for the world.

So, what is the solution when we struggle within our hearts about the direction of our country and its growing instability or when we experience so much pressure from our peers or the society around us to get involved to make a difference? The Apostle Paul gives us very clear direction when he says, I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men; For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty. 1 Timothy 2:1-2. The Christian’s secret power of influence lies in the power of prayer that is produced in the privacy of his or her closet. However, for this prayer to have power it must be produced out of a heart of faith—And Jesus said unto them … verily I say unto you, If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you –Matthew 17:20. Let us always remember that …The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much –James 5:16.

Until the next time, may God be with each one and grant you grace and peace as you walk faithfully according to His Word. Let us pray for each other as we go through the trying times in our world today.

हमारे उद्धारकर्ता और हमारे मुक्तिदाता, प्रभु यीशु मसीह के योग्य नाम में प्रत्येक को अभिवादन।

यह पत्रिका अंक पिछले अंक की तुलना में अधिक शीघ्रता से दिखाई दे रहा होगा। सही कहा। हम प्रत्येक त्रैमासिक अंक को अधिक समय पर प्रकाशित करने की दिशा में काम करते हुए अपनी समय-सारिणी को लगातार कस रहे हैं। हमारा अंतिम लक्ष्य यह है कि ये अंक प्रत्येक वर्ष मार्च, जून, सितंबर और दिसंबर के महीनों में आपके मेलबॉक्स में पहुँचें। कृपया हमारे लिए प्रार्थना कीजिए क्योंकि हम उस समय-सारिणी की ओर बढ़ रहे हैं।

समय-समय पर हमें प्रतिक्रिया प्राप्त होती है—सुझाव, चिंताएँ, और प्रोत्साहन। हम इन प्रतिक्रियों को महत्व देते हैं। इन्हें फाइल किया जाता है और हमारे बोर्ड द्वारा हमारी पत्रिका को बेहतर बनाने के तरीकों का मूल्यांकन करते समय उपयोग किया जाता है। इस विषय पर एक अंतिम विचार… जब हमें किसी विशेष लेख के संबंध में प्रोत्साहन वाली प्रतिक्रिया मिलती है, तो यह हमारे लिए सहायक होता है, और इसे हम अपने लेखकों तक पहुँचाते हुए उन्हें प्रोत्साहित करते हैं। हम आपकी सतत प्रतिक्रिया का स्वागत करते हैं।

जैसा कि पहले उल्लेख किया गया है, हम इस अंक में कई नए वर्ग शामिल कर रहे हैं। एक चर्च इतिहास पर है जिसे हमारी चर्च के दो युवा भाइयों द्वारा लिखा जा रहा है। और एक भजन इतिहास पर है जिसे हमारे बोर्ड के एक सदस्य, एक मध्य-आयु के विवाहितชาย, जो हमारे चर्च से भी हैं, द्वारा लिखा जा रहा है।

“मिडियन में मूसा” में, हम मूसा के जीवन के मध्य भाग में उसके पदचिन्हों पर चलते हैं। उन्हें मिस्र में राजसी दत्तक पुत्र के आरामदायक जीवन से उखाड़ा गया और फिर परमेश्वर द्वारा रेगिस्तान भेजा गया ताकि वे परमेश्वर के सेवक बनने की आगे की तैयारी में कुछ बहुत आवश्यक पाठ सीख सकें। जब हम योना के जीवन को देखते हैं, तो हम “उस परमेश्वर” की झलकियाँ पाते हैं जो पकड़ना नहीं छोड़ेगा। अक्सर एक संघर्ष कर रहा विश्वासी परमेश्वर की सत्यता से दूर हो जाता है क्योंकि वह उस झूठ को मान लेता है कि कोई परवाह नहीं करता, परन्तु सच्चाई यह है—बाइबिल का परमेश्वर हमें बस छोड़कर नहीं चला जाता, न ही हम एक गलत मोड़ या गलती करते ही वह हमारी पीठ घुमा लेता है। आइए यह लेख हमें अब्बा पिता की बाइबिलीय सत्यता में जड़ और आधार पाने में मदद करे—एक ऐसा पिता जो अपने बच्चों की परवाह करता है। हमारे पास शिष्यत्व पर चल रही शृंखला का दूसरा लेख भी है, साथ ही एक मध्य-आयु, आध्यात्मिक रूप से परिपक्व बहन द्वारा लिखा एक लेख है जो बहनों को प्रोत्साहित करती है कि वे अपने वस्त्र पर परमेश्वर का क्या विचार है, इसका मूल्यांकन करें।

चर्च इतिहास और क्या एक ईसाई को वोट देना चाहिए

अंत में, आइए चर्च इतिहास पर दो संक्षिप्त लेखों पर विचार करें। इस अंक के लिए हमारे उद्देश्यों में से एक यह भी है कि जिस देश में हम रहते हैं (यू.एस.) वहां इस वर्ष नवंबर में मध्यावधि चुनाव आने वाले हैं और कई रूढ़िवादी अनाबप्तिस्टों के लिए मतदान प्रक्रिया में शामिल होने का एक मजबूत दबाव होगा ताकि वे अपने देखे हुए कारणों या लक्ष्यों के लिए एक उपयुक्त परिणाम सुनिश्चित कर सकें।

प्राकृतिक संसार में हमारा “पुराना मनुष्य” यह सोचने की प्रवृत्ति रखता है कि यदि हम चाहते हैं कि चीजें “सही” दिशा में जाएँ तो हमें “कुछ करना” चाहिए। आध्यात्मिक सत्य यह है: The king’s heart is in the hand of the LORD, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will –Proverbs 21:1. यदि हम सोचते हैं कि, विश्वासी होने के नाते, यदि हम व्यक्तिगत रूप से मतदान करें तो हम किसी चुनाव में “सही” व्यक्ति को चुनने में भूमिका निभाएंगे, तो आईए हम यह विचार करें कि परमेश्वर ने नेबूचादनेज़र को क्या कहा था। …That the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will –Daniel 4:31-32.

अनाबप्तिस्ट लोगों के इतिहास में इस मुद्दे पर विभिन्न मत रहे हैं, तथापि, हमारी इच्छा यह दृष्टि उठाने की है कि यीशु ने कहा …My kingdom is not of this world: if my kingdom were of this world, then would my servants fight … but now is my kingdom not from hence –John 18:36. जब हम उस व्यक्तिगत विश्वदृष्टि को समझते और विकसित करते हैं जो दो-राज्य सिद्धांत पर आधारित है, तो हम समझते हैं कि हमें …strangers and pilgrims on the earth. [While we] …declare plainly that [we] seek a country …a better country, that is, an heavenly: wherefore God is not ashamed to be called [our] God: for he hath prepared for [us] a city –Hebrews 11:13-16. के रूप में कार्य करना चाहिए। राजनीतिक भागीदारी से संबंधित सभी मामलों में, हमारा प्रोत्साहन यह है कि नए नियम के विश्वासी उस आज्ञा का पालन करें कि …come out from among them, and be ye separate… –2 Corinthians 6:17.

आइए हम हमेशा अपने हृदय में एक यथोचित दृष्टिकोण पालें ताकि हमारी बात और कार्य परमेश्वर के इस विषय पर दृष्टि को परिलक्षित करें जब वह प्रेरित पौलुस के माध्यम से हमें बताता है: Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God … For he is the minister of God to thee… –Romans 13:1-4.

इन विचारों के परिप्रेक्ष्य में ही हमने दो ऐसे लेख लिखे हैं जो चर्च के इतिहास में बहुत अलग समयों का विवरण देते हैं और यह कि उस समय के ईसाइयों के लिए अपने दिन के सरकार से संबंधित होना कैसा था। आइए गंभीरता से विचार करें कि क्या राजनीति में, विशेषकर मतदान प्रक्रिया में शामिल होकर, हम अधिक भला कर सकते हैं। या क्या परमेश्वर चाहता है कि हम अपने निर्वाचित अधिकारियों के लिए प्रार्थना करें, उन्हें उसके सेवकों के रूप में देखें, और उनके बारे में सम्मानपूर्वक बोलें। अंततः, हमें यह भरोसा करना चाहिए कि परमेश्वर समय के “घड़ी” के कम होने के लिए अपनी इच्छा पूरा करेगा जैसे-जैसे समय तेजी से अंत की ओर बढ़ता है। परमेश्वर दुनिया के लिए अपनी सार्वभौमिक इच्छा को पूरा करने के लिए सत्ता में अस्थिर पुरुषों के हृदय को कठोर करने के माध्यम से ऐसा करेगा, बिलकुल जैसे पुराने फ़िरौन के साथ, ताकि अपना परलोकीय विधान पूरा कर सके।

तो, क्या समाधान है जब हम अपने हृदय में हमारे देश की दिशा और उसकी बढ़ती अस्थिरता के बारे में संघर्ष करते हैं या जब हमें अपने साथियों या आस-पास के समाज से इतना दबाव महसूस होता है कि हमें शामिल होना चाहिए ताकि फर्क पड़े? प्रेरित पौलुस हमें बहुत स्पष्ट दिशा देता है जब वह कहता है, I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men; For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty. 1 Timothy 2:1-2. ईसाई का गुप्त प्रभावशाली बल उसके कपाट के भीतर पैदा होने वाली प्रार्थना की शक्ति में निहित है। हालांकि, इस प्रार्थना में शक्ति होने के लिए यह विश्वास के हृदय से उत्पन्न होनी चाहिए—And Jesus said unto them … verily I say unto you, If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you –Matthew 17:20. आइए हम सदैव यह याद रखें कि …The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much –James 5:16.

अगली बार तक, परमेश्वर प्रत्येक के साथ रहें और आपको उस अनुग्रह और शांति से परिपूर्ण करें जैसा कि आप उसकी वचन के अनुसार विश्वासनिष्ठ रूप से चलते हैं। आइए आज की दुनिया के कठिन समयों से गुजरते हुए एक-दूसरे के लिए प्रार्थना करें।

Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created –Revelation 4:11.

This hymn, often called the “National Anthem of Christendom,” is perhaps one of the greatest of hymns of all time. It was written by Edward Perronet, first appearing in the November 1779 issue of Gospel Magazine. It was edited by Augustus Toplady, who is also the author of another well-known hymn, “Rock of Ages”. The text of this hymn, All Hail the Power of Jesus Name, has been translated into almost every language where Christianity is known. Wherever it is sung, it communicates to the spiritual needs of human hearts. One writer has said, “So long as there are Christians on earth, it will continue to be sung; and after that, in heaven.”

Edward Perronet was born at Sundridge, Kent, England, in 1726. He was a descendant of a distinguished French Huguenot family who had fled to Switzerland and later to England because of the religious persecution in France. Edward’s father, a pastor in the State Church of England, was strongly sympathetic with the evangelical movement spearheaded by the Wesleys and George Whitefield. Edward, too, like his father, became a minister in the Anglican Church but was always critical of its ways. Once he wrote, “I was born and I am likely to die in the tottering communion of the Church of England, but I despise her nonsense.” Soon, however, he broke from the Church and threw himself strenuously into the evangelistic endeavors of the Wesleys during the 1740s and 1750s.

Charles Wesley writes of Edward Perronet’s boldness in preaching. At one time he and Perronet were beset in a house by a mob of rough revilers, whom Perronet opposed courageously, while they abused him and threw dirt on him. It was during this time that the Wesleys and their followers suffered much persecution and even violence from those who disagreed with their ministry. Concerning these experiences, Wesley made the following notation in his diary: “From Rockdale we went to Bolton, and soon found that the Rockdale lions were lambs in comparison with those of Bolton.” Edward Perronet was thrown down and rolled in mud and mire. Stones were hurled and windows broken.

Another interesting account is given regarding the relationship between the Wesleys and Perronet. John Wesley wanted to hear Perronet preach, and he, being 18 years younger than John had always refused to preach in the older churchman’s presence. So, one day Wesley seeing Edward in the congregation announced that he would preach at the next service. Desiring to avoid a public conflict with Wesley, Perronet mounted the pulpit the next morning, but quickly explained that he had never consented to preach. “However,” he added, “I shall deliver the greatest sermon that has ever been preached on earth.” He then read the Sermon on the Mount and sat down without comment.

After eight years of co-operation with the Wesleys, Perronet’s strong-mindedness and free spirit caused a division between them, as he disagreed with some of their regulations. They continued, however, to esteem and love each other.

The last years of Perronet were spent at Canterbury, where he was pastor of an independent church, and where he died in 1792, at the age of sixty-six. His last words have also become a classic: “Glory to God in the height of His divinity! Glory to God in the depth of His humanity! Glory to God in His all-sufficiency! Into His hands I commend my spirit.”

Though Perronet wrote many other hymns and forms of poetry, none of them, have attained fame except the immortal “All Hail the Power of Jesus Name.” The success of this text has, no doubt, been furthered by three fine tunes. “Coronation,” composed by Oliver Holden, a Massachusetts carpenter, self-taught musician, and respected singing-school teacher, is most widely used in America. “Miles Lane” composed by William Shrubsole, Perronet’s personal friend, is the most popular in Great Britain. While the festive “Diadem” tune, composed in 1838 for this text by James Ellor, an English layman, is frequently used as a choir number. This hymn was originally written having the title, “On the Resurrection,” and there were eight stanzas, as follows:

All hail the power of Jesus’ name,
Let angels prostrate fall
Bring forth the royal diadem,
To crown Him Lord of all!

Let high born seraphs tune the lyre,
And, as they tune it, fall
Before His face who tunes their choir,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Crown Him, ye morning stars of light,
Who fixed this floating ball,
Now hail the Strength of Israel’s might,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Crown Him, ye martyrs of your God,
Who from His altar call;
Extol the stem of Jesse’s rod,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Ye seed of Israel’s chosen race,
Ye ransomed of the fall,
Hail Him who saves you by His grace
And crown Him Lord of all!

Hail Him, ye heirs of David’s line,
Whom David Lord did call.
The God incarnate, Man divine,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Sinners, whose love can ne’er forget
The wormwood and the gall,
Go spread your trophies at His feet,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Let every tribe and every tongue
That bound creation’s call
Now shout in universal song,
The crowned Lord of all!

As it now stands in our hymnbooks, the hymn is shortened and changed, and one stanza has been added by the famous hymn collector, Rev. John Rippon, in 1787.

Oh, that with yonder sacred throng
We at His feet may fall;
We’ll join the everlasting song,
And crown Him Lord of all.

As we wrap up this amazing story of the life of Edward Perronet and the others who have had their part in bringing this immortal hymn to us, let’s take a look in closing at the effect this hymn has had on heathens who knew nothing about Jesus. The most famous story connected with Perronet’s great hymn is told of the missionary to India, Rev. E.P. Scott. One day he saw on the street a man of so strange an appearance that he inquired about him and learned that he belonged to a wild mountain tribe among whom Christ had never been preached. Mr. Scott prayed over the matter and decided to visit that tribe. As soon as he reached their mountain home, he fell in among a savage band of murderous tribesmen who were on a war expedition, and who were closing in on him with their spears. They seized him and pointed their spears at his heart. At once the missionary drew out the violin that he always carried with him and began to play and sing in the native language, “All hail the power of Jesus’ name!” He closed his eyes, expecting death at any minute. When he reached the fourth stanza, and nothing had happened, he opened his eyes, and was amazed to see that the spears had fallen from the hands of the savages, and big tears were in their eyes! They invited Mr. Scott to their homes, and he spent the remaining years of his life preaching and ministering God’s love and redemption to these people. God in His providence used a simple hymn as a means of introducing the gospel to a group of needy pagans.

Tu es digne, ô Seigneur, de recevoir la gloire, l'honneur et la puissance: car tu as créé toutes choses, et c'est pour ton plaisir qu'elles existent et ont été créées –Apocalypse 4:11.

Cet hymne, souvent appelé «l'hymne national du christianisme», est peut-être l'un des plus grands hymnes de tous les temps. Il a été écrit par Edward Perronet et est paru pour la première fois dans le numéro de novembre 1779 du Gospel Magazine. Il a été édité par Augustus Toplady, qui est aussi l'auteur d'un autre hymne bien connu, «Rock of Ages». Le texte de cet hymne, All Hail the Power of Jesus Name, a été traduit dans presque toutes les langues où le christianisme est connu. Partout où il est chanté, il répond aux besoins spirituels des cœurs humains. Un écrivain a dit : «Tant qu'il y aura des chrétiens sur terre, il continuera d'être chanté; et ensuite, au ciel.»

Edward Perronet est né à Sundridge, dans le Kent, en Angleterre, en 1726. Il descendait d'une illustre famille huguenote française qui avait fui en Suisse puis en Angleterre à cause des persécutions religieuses en France. Le père d'Edward, pasteur dans l'Église d'Angleterre, était fortement sympathisant du mouvement évangélique mené par les frères Wesley et George Whitefield. Edward, lui aussi, comme son père, devint ministre dans l'Église anglicane mais fut toujours critique à l'égard de ses façons. Il écrivit une fois : «Je suis né et je suis susceptible de mourir dans la communion vacillante de l'Église d'Angleterre, mais je méprise ses absurdités.» Bientôt cependant, il rompit avec l'Église et se lança avec énergie dans les œuvres évangéliques des Wesley durant les années 1740 et 1750.

Charles Wesley écrit sur l'audace d'Edward Perronet dans la prédication. À une époque, lui et Perronet furent assiégés dans une maison par une foule de grossiers vociférateurs, que Perronet affronta courageusement, tandis qu'ils l'insultaient et lui jetaient de la terre. C'est à cette période que les Wesley et leurs partisans subirent beaucoup de persécution et même de la violence de la part de ceux qui désapprouvaient leur ministère. Concernant ces expériences, Wesley nota dans son journal : «De Rockdale nous sommes allés à Bolton, et nous avons bientôt trouvé que les lions de Rockdale étaient des agneaux comparés à ceux de Bolton.» Edward Perronet fut jeté à terre et roulé dans la boue et la fange. Des pierres furent lancées et des fenêtres brisées.

Un autre récit intéressant est donné concernant la relation entre les Wesley et Perronet. John Wesley désirait entendre Perronet prêcher, et lui, étant de dix-huit ans plus jeune que John, avait toujours refusé de prêcher en présence du vieux pasteur. Ainsi, un jour, Wesley voyant Edward dans la congrégation annonça qu'il prêcherait au service suivant. Désirant éviter un conflit public avec Wesley, Perronet monta en chaire le lendemain matin, mais expliqua rapidement qu'il n'avait jamais consenti à prêcher. «Cependant,» ajouta-t-il, «je livrerai le plus grand sermon qui ait jamais été prêché sur la terre.» Il lut alors le Sermon sur la montagne et s'assit sans commentaire.

Après huit années de coopération avec les Wesley, l'entêtement et l'esprit libre de Perronet provoquèrent une division entre eux, car il était en désaccord avec certaines de leurs règlements. Ils continuèrent néanmoins à s'estimer et à s'aimer.

Les dernières années de Perronet se passèrent à Canterbury, où il fut pasteur d'une église indépendante, et où il mourut en 1792, à l'âge de soixante-six ans. Ses dernières paroles sont également devenues un classique : «Gloire à Dieu dans la hauteur de Sa divinité! Gloire à Dieu dans la profondeur de Son humanité! Gloire à Dieu dans Sa suffisance totale! Entre Ses mains je recommande mon esprit.»

Bien que Perronet ait écrit de nombreux autres hymnes et poèmes, aucun d'eux n'a acquis de renommée excepté l'immortel «All Hail the Power of Jesus' Name». Le succès de ce texte a sans doute été favorisé par trois beaux airs. «Coronation», composé par Oliver Holden, un charpentier du Massachusetts, musicien autodidacte et respecté professeur d'école de chant, est le plus largement utilisé en Amérique. «Miles Lane», composé par William Shrubsole, ami personnel de Perronet, est le plus populaire en Grande-Bretagne. Tandis que l'air festif «Diadem», composé en 1838 pour ce texte par James Ellor, un laïc anglais, est fréquemment utilisé comme pièce de chœur. Cet hymne a été à l'origine écrit sous le titre «On the Resurrection», et il y avait huit strophes, comme suit :

Salut au pouvoir du nom de Jésus,
Que les anges se prosternent et tombent!
Apportez la diadème royal,
Pour le couronner Seigneur de tout!

Que les séraphins nés en haut accordent la lyre,
Et, tandis qu'ils l'accordent, s'inclinent,
Devant Sa face qui règle leur chœur,
Et le couronner Seigneur de tout!

Couronnez-Le, ô étoiles matinales de lumière,
Qui avez fixé cette boule flottante,
Saluez maintenant la Force de la puissance d'Israël,
Et couronnez-Le Seigneur de tout!

Couronnez-Le, ô martyrs de votre Dieu,
Qui l'appelez de son autel;
Exaltez la tige du bâton de Jessé,
Et couronnez-Le Seigneur de tout!

Vous, semence de la race choisie d'Israël,
Vous, rachetés de la chute,
Saluez Celui qui vous sauve par Sa grâce
Et couronnez-Le Seigneur de tout!

Saluez-Le, héritiers de la lignée de David,
Que David appelait Seigneur.
Le Dieu incarné, l'Homme divin,
Et couronnez-Le Seigneur de tout!

Pécheurs, dont l'amour ne peut jamais oublier
L'absinthe et la bile,
Allez répandre vos trophées à Ses pieds,
Et couronnez-Le Seigneur de tout!

Que chaque tribu et chaque langue
Qui a lié l'appel de la création
Crie maintenant dans un chant universel,
Le Seigneur couronné de tout!

Tel qu'il figure maintenant dans nos recueils d'hymnes, l'hymne est abrégé et modifié, et une strophe a été ajoutée par le célèbre collecteur d'hymnes, le révérend John Rippon, en 1787.

Oh, que nous, avec cette sainte multitude là-bas,
Puissions tomber à Ses pieds;
Nous nous joindrons au chant éternel,
Et le couronnerons Seigneur de tout.

Alors que nous concluons cette histoire étonnante de la vie d'Edward Perronet et des autres qui ont contribué à nous transmettre cet hymne immortel, examinons enfin l'effet qu'a eu cet hymne sur des païens qui ne connaissaient rien de Jésus. L'histoire la plus célèbre liée au grand hymne de Perronet est racontée au sujet du missionnaire en Inde, le rév. E. P. Scott. Un jour il vit dans la rue un homme d'apparence si étrange qu'il s'enquit à son sujet et apprit qu'il appartenait à une tribu montagnarde sauvage parmi laquelle le Christ n'avait jamais été prêché. M. Scott pria sur la question et décida de visiter cette tribu. Dès qu'il atteignit leur demeure montagneuse, il tomba au milieu d'une bande sauvage de tribus meurtrières qui étaient en expédition de guerre, et qui l'entouraient avec leurs lances. Ils le saisirent et pointèrent leurs lances vers son cœur. Aussitôt le missionnaire sortit le violon qu'il portait toujours avec lui et se mit à jouer et chanter dans la langue native, «All hail the power of Jesus' name!» Il ferma les yeux, s'attendant à la mort à tout instant. Lorsqu'il atteignit la quatrième strophe, et que rien ne se fut produit, il ouvrit les yeux, et fut étonné de voir que les lances étaient tombées des mains des sauvages, et de grosses larmes brillaient dans leurs yeux! Ils invitèrent M. Scott dans leurs foyers, et il passa les années restantes de sa vie à prêcher et à manifester l'amour et la rédemption de Dieu à ces peuples. Dieu, dans Sa providence, utilisa un simple hymne comme moyen d'introduire l'Évangile à un groupe de païens dans le besoin.

The angel of the LORD encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them –Psalm 34:7.

“Tell us a story, Grandma,” begged two eager children as they crowded around her rocking chair.

“My, my, you children like to hear stories, don’t you?” replied Grandma, with a twinkle in her eye. “All right, I’ll tell you about a time when I was about eight years old, and my sister Lori was nine.

We lived on an old farm, back a short lane along a dirt road. One morning, Mother called us in from our play and said she was out of sugar. She asked us to walk to Mrs. Brightbill to see if she had any sugar to spare. You see, we didn’t have telephones when I was a little girl, so she couldn’t call the neighbor and ask her. Neighbors often shared back and forth because we didn’t go shopping at the store very often either. So, mother gave us a container, and we started out on our long walk as Mother called after us and reminded us not to loiter along the way.”

“How far was it to the Brightbills?” asked Sharon.

“Oh, it was about half a mile to our closest neighbor, the Rhine’s place, and then about another quarter of a mile to the Brightbills,” replied Grandma.

“Oh, that’s far. Mother won’t let us walk on the road at all,” added Micah.

“I’m sure you are right,” agreed Grandma. “And I hope you never walk on the road without your parents’ permission. But things were much different when I was a little girl. We also walked every day to school, which was quite a bit further than the Brightbill farm. So, the little errand we were doing on this morning for Mother seemed like fun. There was only one problem though. The Rhine family had an old man living in their summer house. His name was Pierce, and he had a very fierce dog; at least he acted very fierce! He was kept behind a high wire fence connected to an old shed.

Every day when we walked to school, that dog frightened us terribly with his fierce barking and growling. But Mother always reminded us to pray and remember the Bible verse which says: What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee –Psalm 56:3. Still, we hurried by as fast as our legs could take us.

Lori and I started out happily on our errand for Mother. We skipped along, watching the dust swirl beneath our feet on that warm summer morning. Everything seemed unusually quiet and still as we passed through the gully, over the rippling creek, and up the steep hill right before Neighbor Rhine’s place. There before us was the old shed, and on the other side was the high fence which kept in Pierce’s mean dog. My heart began to thump rapidly. ‘Maybe that bad dog hadn’t seen us yet,’ I thought gratefully as I whispered once more to myself, ‘I will trust and not be afraid.’

Suddenly, the air was shattered by the ferocious barking of that mean dog as he sprang around the corner of the old shed! Lori and I froze in our tracks! As that angry dog raced toward us, Lori screamed. The next moment, I realized she had fallen down and was sitting in the middle of the dirt road, with her hands behind her on the hard packed gravel, feet and legs in the air, kicking and kicking, spinning around and around as that angry dog circled her, jumping in at her and nipping at her feet and legs! I was so scared. I just stood frozen to the spot. I don’t remember if I screamed, or if I prayed. But suddenly there was a shout! It was Pierce, with a whip in his hand. He came running around the shed and out on the road. He whipped and whipped that dog and finally got him away from Lori and back inside the fence where he belonged, as Lori and I stood there, trembling, and crying with relief.”

“Wow!” exclaimed Sharon. “That was really scary, wasn’t it?”

“Did Pierce need to get rid of his dog?” asked Micah.

“Yes, Sharon, it was very scary,” answered Grandma. “And no, Micah, Pierce did not get rid of his dog. We children needed to keep trusting the good Lord to keep us safe every day.”

“I don’t remember what happened after Pierce got the dog away that day, or if we ever got Mother’s sugar, but I will never forget what happened that day.

It was a miracle that Lori and I were not injured. There is a verse in Psalms which says: Save me from the lion’s mouth… –Psalm 22:21. How thankful we were to be delivered from the dog’s mouth! I like to think that the Lord’s angel had his sword drawn in front of that dog’s mouth every time he leaped at my dear sister.”

Die engel van die HERE kamp rondom die wat Hom vrees, en red hulle – Psalm 34:7.

“Vertel vir ons ’n storie, Ouma,” het twee gretige kinders gesmeek terwyl hulle om haar skommelstoel saamgedrom het.

“My, my, julle kinders hou daarvan om stories te hoor, nie waar nie?” antwoord Ouma met ’n vonkel in haar oog. “Goed dan, ek sal julle vertel van ’n tyd toe ek sowat agt jaar oud was, en my suster Lori was nege.

Ons het op ’n ou plaas gewoon, agter ’n kort paadjie langs ’n vuilpad. Een oggend het Ma ons opgeroep uit ons speel en gesê sy is uit suiker. Sy het ons gevra om na Mev. Brightbill te stap om te kyk of sy dalk suiker oor het om te leen. Sien julle, ons het nie telefone gehad toe ek ’n dogtertjie was nie, so sy kon nie die buurvrou bel en vra nie. Bure het dikwels mekaar gehelp omdat ons ook nie gereeld by die winkel inkopies gaan doen het nie. Dus het Ma vir ons ’n houer gegee, en ons het aan die lang wandeling begin terwyl Ma agterna geroep het en ons daaraan herinner het om nie langs die pad te talm nie.”

“Hoe ver was dit na die Brightbills?” vra Sharon.

“O, dit was omtrent ’n halwe myl na ons naaste buur, die Rhine se plek, en toe omtrent nog ’n kwart myl na die Brightbills,” antwoord Ouma.

“Ag, dis ver. Ma laat ons glad nie op die pad loop nie,” voeg Micah by.

“Ek is seker julle is reg,” stem Ouma toe. “En ek hoop julle sal nooit op die pad loop sonder julle ouers se toestemming nie. Maar dinge was baie anders toe ek ’n klein dogtertjie was. Ons het ook elke dag skool toe gestap, wat nogal verder was as die Brightbill-plaas. Dus het die klein boodskap wat ons daardie oggend vir Ma gedoen het, soos pret gevoel. Daar was net een probleem. Die familie Rhine het ’n ou man gehad wat in hul somerhuis gewoon het. Sy naam was Pierce, en hy het ’n baie woeste hond gehad; in elk geval het hy baie woest voorgekom! Hy is agter ’n hoë draaddraadheining gehou wat aan ’n ou skuur vasgemaak was.

Elke dag toe ons skool toe stap, het daardie hond ons vreeslik laat skrik met sy woeste blaf en gegrom. Maar Ma het ons altyd daaraan herinner om te bid en die Bybelvers te onthou wat sê: Wanneer ek bevrees is, sal ek op U betrou – Psalm 56:3. Ons het steeds so vinnig as wat ons pote kon gegaan het verbygehardloop.

Lori en ek het vrolik aan ons boodskap vir Ma begin. Ons het gespring terwyl ons stof onder ons voete sien opwaai op daardie warm someroggend. Alles het vreemd stil gelyk terwyl ons deur die kloof verbygestap het, oor die kolkende stroompie en die steil heuwel net voor Buurman Rhine se plek op. Daar voor ons was die ou skuur, en aan die ander kant die hoë heining wat Pierce se gemene hond binnehou. My hart het vinnig begin bons. ‘Miskien het daardie slegte hond ons nog nie gesien nie,’ het ek dankbaar gedink en weer by myself gefluister, ‘Ek sal vertrou en nie bang wees nie.’

Skielik is die lug verskeur deur die woeste geblaf van daardie gemene hond toe hy om die hoek van die ou skuur uitspring! Lori en ek het soos aan stokke versteen! Toe daardie woedende hond op ons afstorm, gil Lori. Die volgende oomblik besef ek sy het geval en sit in die middel van die gruispad, met haar hande agter haar op die hardgepakke gruis, voete en bene in die lug, gee en gee, draai en draai terwyl daardie woedende hond om haar bly draai, inspring by haar en byt na haar voete en bene! Ek was so bang. Ek het net versteen daar gestaan. Ek onthou nie of ek geskree het nie, of of ek gebid het. Maar skielik was daar ’n geroep! Dit was Pierce, met ’n sweep in sy hand. Hy het om die skuur aangeloop en op die pad uitgekom. Hy het daardie hond geslaan en geslaan en het hom uiteindelik van Lori weggekry en terug binne die heining plaas waar hy hoort te wees, terwyl Lori en ek daar getril het en van verligting gehuil het.”

“Woe!” roep Sharon uit. “Dis regtig scary, was dit nie?”

“Moes Pierce sy hond wegdoen?” vra Micah.

“Ja, Sharon, dit was baie eng,” antwoord Ouma. “En nee, Micah, Pierce het nie sy hond weggedoen nie. Ons kinders moes elke dag aanhou vertrou dat die Here ons veilig sal hou.”

“Ek onthou nie wat daarna gebeur het toe Pierce die hond daardie dag weggekry het nie, of of ons ooit Ma se suiker gekry het nie, maar ek sal nooit vergeet wat daardie dag gebeur het nie.

Dit was ’n wonderwerk dat Lori en ek nie beseer is nie. Daar is ’n vers in die Psalms wat sê: Red my uit die leeuwemond… – Psalm 22:21. Hoe dankbaar was ons om uit die hond se mond gered te wees! Ek hou daarvan om te dink dat die Here se engel sy swaard voor daardie hond se mond getrek gehad het elke keer toe hy na my liewe suster opgespring het.”

O anjo do SENHOR acampa ao redor dos que o temem, e os livra –Salmo 34:7.

“Conte-nos uma história, vovó”, imploraram duas crianças ansiosas enquanto se amontoavam em torno de sua cadeira de balanço.

“Ora, ora, vocês crianças gostam de ouvir histórias, não gostam?” respondeu a vovó, com um brilho no olhar. “Tudo bem, vou contar sobre uma vez em que eu tinha cerca de oito anos, e minha irmã Lori tinha nove.

Nós morávamos numa velha fazenda, ao fim de uma pequena estrada de terra. Certa manhã, mamãe nos chamou de nossa brincadeira e disse que estava sem açúcar. Pediu que fôssemos até a casa da Sra. Brightbill ver se ela tinha algum açúcar para emprestar. Veja, não tínhamos telefones quando eu era menina, então ela não podia ligar para a vizinha e perguntar. Os vizinhos frequentemente se ajudavam porque também não íamos ao mercado com muita frequência. Então, mamãe nos deu um recipiente, e começamos nossa longa caminhada enquanto mamãe nos chamava e lembrava para não nos demorarmos pelo caminho.”

“Quão longe era até a casa dos Brightbill?” perguntou Sharon.

“Ah, era cerca de meia milha até nosso vizinho mais próximo, a propriedade dos Rhine, e então mais cerca de um quarto de milha até os Brightbill”, respondeu a vovó.

“Oh, isso é longe. Mamãe não deixa a gente andar na estrada de jeito nenhum”, acrescentou Micah.

“Tenho certeza de que vocês estão certos”, concordou a vovó. “E espero que vocês nunca andem na estrada sem a permissão dos pais. Mas as coisas eram bem diferentes quando eu era menina. Também caminhávamos todo dia até a escola, que ficava bem mais longe do que a fazenda dos Brightbill. Então, o pequeno recado que estávamos fazendo naquela manhã para a mamãe parecia divertido. Havia apenas um problema, porém. A família Rhine tinha um homem idoso morando em sua casa de verão. O nome dele era Pierce, e ele tinha um cachorro muito feroz; pelo menos ele parecia muito feroz! Ele ficava preso atrás de uma cerca alta de arame ligada a um velho celeiro.

Todo dia, quando íamos para a escola, aquele cachorro nos aterrorizava com seus latidos e rosnados ferozes. Mas mamãe sempre nos lembrava de orar e recordar o versículo da Bíblia que diz: Quando eu tiver medo, confiarei em ti –Salmo 56:3. Mesmo assim, passávamos apressados o mais rápido que nossas pernas podiam levar.

Lori e eu saímos felizes cumprindo o recado para mamãe. Pulávamos, observando a poeira rodopiar sob nossos pés naquela manhã quente de verão. Tudo parecia incomumente quieto e calmo enquanto passávamos pelo barranco, sobre o riacho ondulante e subíamos a íngreme colina logo antes da propriedade do vizinho Rhine. Ali diante de nós estava o velho celeiro, e do outro lado ficava a cerca alta que mantinha o cachorro malvado de Pierce. Meu coração começou a bater rapidamente. ‘Talvez aquele cachorro mau ainda não nos tenha visto’, pensei agradecida enquanto sussurrava mais uma vez para mim mesma, ‘Confiarei e não temerei.’

De repente, o ar foi rasgado pelos latidos ferozes daquele cachorro mau enquanto ele surgiu em torno do canto do velho celeiro! Lori e eu congelamos no lugar! Quando aquele cão zangado correu em nossa direção, Lori gritou. No momento seguinte, percebi que ela havia caído e estava sentada no meio da estrada de terra, com as mãos apoiadas atrás dela sobre o cascalho firme, pés e pernas no ar, chutando e chutando, girando e girando enquanto aquele cão zangado circulava ao redor dela, investindo e mordiscando seus pés e pernas! Eu estava tão assustada. Fiquei simplesmente paralisada no lugar. Não me lembro se gritei, ou se orei. Mas de repente houve um grito! Era Pierce, com um chicote na mão. Ele correu em volta do celeiro e saiu para a estrada. Chicoteou e chicoteou aquele cão e finalmente o afastou de Lori e o fez voltar para dentro da cerca onde ele pertencia, enquanto Lori e eu permanecíamos ali, tremendo e chorando de alívio.”

“Uau!” exclamou Sharon. “Isso foi mesmo assustador, não foi?”

“Pierce precisou se livrar do cão?” perguntou Micah.

“Sim, Sharon, foi muito assustador”, respondeu a vovó. “E não, Micah, Pierce não se livrou do cão. Nós, crianças, precisávamos continuar confiando que o bom Senhor nos protegeria a cada dia.”

“Não me lembro do que aconteceu depois que Pierce afastou o cão naquele dia, nem se conseguimos o açúcar da mamãe, mas nunca esquecerei o que aconteceu naquele dia.

Foi um milagre que Lori e eu não ficássemos feridas. Há um versículo nos Salmos que diz: Livra-me da boca do leão… –Salmo 22:21. Quão agradecidas ficamos por sermos livradas da boca do cachorro! Gosto de pensar que o anjo do Senhor tinha a sua espada erguida diante da boca daquele cão toda vez que ele saltava contra minha querida irmã.”

Greetings to each one in the worthy name of Jesus Christ, our Saviour, and our Redeemer.

This magazine issue may seem to be arriving more quickly on the heels of the last one. True. We are continuing to tighten up our schedule as we work towards getting each quarterly issue out in a more timely manner. Our ultimate goal is to have them arrive in your mailboxes in the months of March, June, September, and December of each year. Pray for us as we continue moving towards that schedule.

From time to time, we receive feedback—suggestions, concerns, and encouragement. We value this feedback. It is filed away and used by the board as we continually evaluate ways to make our magazine better. One final thought on this matter… when we receive feedback of encouragement regarding a specific article, it is helpful for us, and it is encouraging for our authors as we pass that along to them. We welcome your ongoing feedback.

As previously mentioned, we are including several new categories in this issue. One on Church History that is being written by two young brothers from our church. And one on Hymn Histories being written by one of our board members, a middle-aged married man, who is also from our church.

In “Moses in Midian”, we take a walk in Moses’ footsteps during the mid-section of his life. He was uprooted from his comfortable lifestyle in Egypt as an adopted son of royalty and was then sent by God into the desert to learn some much-needed lessons in further preparation towards becoming God’s servant. As we take a look at the life of Jonah, we glean glimpses of “The God Who Will Not Let Go”. Often a struggling believer loses sight of the Truth of God because they believe the lie that no one cares, yet the truth of the matter is this—the God of the Bible doesn’t just drop us, or turn His back on us, the instant that we take a wrong turn or a misstep. Let’s allow this article to help us to become rooted and grounded in the biblical Truth of Abba Father—a Father who cares for His children. We also have the second article in a continuing series on discipleship, as well as an article written by a middle-aged, spiritually-mature sister who shares her encouragement for sisters to evaluate what God thinks of their attire.

Church History and Should A Christian Vote

Finally, let’s consider the two short articles on church history. One of our goals for this issue is burdened with the awareness that the country in which we live (the U.S.) is approaching mid-term elections in November of this year and that there will be a strong push for many conservative Anabaptists to become involved in the voting process to ensure a proper outcome for the good of their perceived cause or goals.

In the natural world our “old man” has the tendency to think that we must “do something” if we expect things to go in a “right” direction. The spiritual Truth is this: The king’s heart is in the hand of the LORD, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will –Proverbs 21:1. If we think that, as believers, we will have a part in electing the “right” person in an election if we personally vote, let’s stop to consider what God Himself told Nebuchadnezzar. …That the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will –Daniel 4:31-32.

Throughout the history of the Anabaptist people there have been varied opinions on this matter, however, it is our wish to lift up the perspective that Jesus said …My kingdom is not of this world: if my kingdom were of this world, then would my servants fight … but now is my kingdom not from hence –John 18:36. When we understand and develop a personal world view that is founded on the two-kingdom principle, we realize that we must function as …strangers and pilgrims on the earth. [While we] …declare plainly that [we] seek a country …a better country, that is, an heavenly: wherefore God is not ashamed to be called [our] God: for he hath prepared for [us] a city –Hebrews 11:13-16. In all things involving political involvement, it is our encouragement that New Testament believers should obey the command to …come out from among them, and be ye separate… –2 Corinthians 6:17.

Let’s always cultivate a right attitude in our hearts so that our talk and actions reflect God’s view on the matter when He through the Apostle Paul tells us to: Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God … For he is the minister of God to thee… –Romans 13:1-4.

It is in consideration of these thoughts that we wrote the two articles detailing very different times in the history of the church and what it was like for Christians to relate to the government of their day. Let us seriously ponder whether we can do more good by getting involved in politics, especially in the voting process. Or whether God wants us to pray for our elected officials, to view them as His servants, and to speak about them with respect. Ultimately, we must trust God to bring about His will for the winding down of the “clock of time” as time speeds onward towards the end of time. God will do this through hardening the hearts of ungodly men in positions of power, just like Pharaoh of old, to accomplish His sovereign will for the world.

So, what is the solution when we struggle within our hearts about the direction of our country and its growing instability or when we experience so much pressure from our peers or the society around us to get involved to make a difference? The Apostle Paul gives us very clear direction when he says, I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men; For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty. 1 Timothy 2:1-2. The Christian’s secret power of influence lies in the power of prayer that is produced in the privacy of his or her closet. However, for this prayer to have power it must be produced out of a heart of faith—And Jesus said unto them … verily I say unto you, If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you –Matthew 17:20. Let us always remember that …The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much –James 5:16.

Until the next time, may God be with each one and grant you grace and peace as you walk faithfully according to His Word. Let us pray for each other as we go through the trying times in our world today.

愿向在配得的救主和救赎主耶稣基督名下的各位问安。

本期杂志看起来似乎比上一期来得更快些。确实如此。我们正不断收紧出版日程，力图使每期季刊更及时地出版。我们的最终目标是使每年的三月、六月、九月和十二月的刊期到达你们的邮箱。请为我们祷告，助我们继续朝这一日程前进。

我们不时会收到反馈——建议、关切与鼓励。我们重视这些反馈。它们被归档并由董事会在持续评估改善杂志的方式时加以利用。关于这一点还有最后一点想说……当我们收到针对某篇具体文章的鼓励性反馈时，这对我们有帮助，也会使我们在转呈作者时鼓励到他们。我们欢迎你们持续的反馈。

如前所述，本期我们加入了几类新栏目。一则是由我们教会的两位年轻弟兄撰写的教会史；另一则是由我们董事会的一位中年已婚弟兄撰写的圣诗来历专栏，他也是来自我们教会的人。

在“Moses in Midian”（《米甸时期的摩西》）一文中，我们沿着摩西生命中间段的足迹行走。他被从在埃及舒适的王室养子身份中拔出，随后被上帝差到旷野里学习一些非常需要的功课，以便更进一步地预备成为上帝的仆人。当我们审视约拿的一生时，我们得以一窥“那位不放手的神”。常有挣扎的信徒因信了“没人关心我”的谬论而失去对神真理的视野，然而事情的真相是——圣经的上帝并不会在我们一走错路或失足时就抛下我们或转身不顾。愿这篇文章帮助我们在天父圣经的真理里扎根立定——这位父亲关怀祂的儿女。我们也有一篇继续门徒训练系列的第二篇文章，以及一篇由一位中年、属灵成熟的姐妹所写，呼吁众姐妹省察神对她们服饰的看法。

教会史与基督徒应否投票

最后，让我们来考虑两篇关于教会历史的短文。本期的一个目标是怀着这样一种意识：我们所居住的国家（美国）将在今年十一月迎来中期选举，并且很多保守的门诺派/再洗礼派（Anabaptists）会受到强烈呼吁，参与投票过程以求为他们所认为的事业或目标争取一个“合适”的结果。

在属世中，我们的“旧人”倾向于认为如果我们期望事情朝“正确”的方向发展，我们就必须“做点什么”。属灵的真理是：王的心在耶和华手中，好像溪水随意流转。（箴言 21:1）如果我们以为作为信徒，只要我们个人去投票就会在选举中选出“正确”的人，不妨回想上帝对尼布甲尼撒所说的话。……至高者在世人国中掌权，立人治理；立得高下，随己意转动。（但以理 4:31-32）

在门诺派（再洗礼派）历史中，对此事向来有不同意见，然而我们愿提出这样的观点：耶稣说过……我的国不属这世界；若我的国属这世界，我的臣仆必要争战，使我不至于被卖给犹太人；但我的国不属这世界。（约翰福音 18:36）当我们理解并建立以“两国论”为根基的个人世界观时，就会意识到我们必须作为……在世上的客旅和寄居的；并且明说自己是寻求一个城邑，就是那天上的。（希伯来书 11:13-16）在一切与政治介入有关的事上，我们鼓励新约信徒当遵行……你们要从他们中间出来，与他们分别…（哥林多后书 6:17）的命令。

愿我们常在心中培育正确的态度，使我们的言行能反映出神在此事上的看法，正如保罗通过使徒的职分告诉我们的：凡掌权的，人人当顺服他。因为没有掌权的不是出于神的；凡掌权的都是神所命的……为要惩罚那行恶的，称赞那行善的。你们若行恶，就当怕；因为掌权的不是枉然佩刀；他是神的执法者，向那行恶的伸怒。（罗马书 13:1-4）

正是考虑到这些思想，我们撰写了两篇文章，详述教会历史上截然不同的时期，以及基督徒当时如何与当朝政府相处。让我们认真思量：通过参与政治，尤其是投票，我们能否做更多的善事？抑或神要我们为被选出的官员祷告，把他们看作祂的仆人，并以尊重的态度谈论他们？归根到底，我们必须信靠神，会按祂的旨意使“时间的钟表”在时光向末了奔去时走向祂的旨意。神要通过使不敬虔之人在位掌权者心刚硬（就像古时的法老一样）来成就祂在世上的主权旨意。

那么，当我们在心中为国家的方向和日益增长的不稳定而挣扎，或当我们感到来自同侪与周遭社会的强大压力要我们介入以求有所作为时，解决之道是什么？使徒保罗给了我们非常清楚的指引，他说：所以我劝你們，第一要為萬人懇求、禱告、代求、感謝，為君王和一切在位的也該如此，叫我們可以敬虔端正，平安無事地度日。（提摩太前書 2:1-2）基督徒秘密的影響力就藏在他或她在密室中所生出的禱告的力量裡。然而，要使这祷告有力量，它必须出于信心的心——耶穌對他們說……我實在告訴你們，你們若有信心像一顆芥菜種，就是對這座山說：你從這裡挪到那裡，它也必挪去；並且你們沒有一件不能作的。（馬太福音 17:20）愿我们常记得：正义人的恳切祈祷，所发的力量是大有功效的。（雅各書 5:16）

在下次见面之前，愿神与各位同在，赐你们恩典与平安，使你们按着祂的话忠心行走。愿我们在当今世界艰难的时刻彼此代祷。

I have enjoyed listening to, and even taking part in, discussions about the Covid shot—about why someone has, and why the other has not, received it. I venture to say we could have seven people give their viewpoint on the subject and maybe have eight different ideas.

I begin with the disclaimer that these are my thoughts, and I am quite okay with someone disagreeing. In fact, I would welcome others to share their viewpoints.

One of the things you will notice in this writing is that I don’t call the Covid shot a ‘vaccine’. Not that it doesn’t technically fit the official definition, but rather that it doesn’t function the way we have known vaccines to work. I remember when I was a lad about four years of age, I went with my mother to the health department and received a vaccination in my upper arm for smallpox. (The pock mark is still there) I remember some years later when the whole community gathered at our local public school for the sugar cube treatment which was an oral vaccination against polio. I don’t remember if I had any other vaccinations or not. My point is that these vaccinations were immunizations against a disease. We were assured that we would not get smallpox, polio, measles or whatever else we were vaccinated for. And we didn’t—not just a lesser amount or a case not as severe. We understood that we were immunized, and the fight was over.

During the current pandemic we kept hearing about the vaccination that was coming. It sounded like this was going to be the answer to this pestilence that had settled on the world. Some of us wondered if this would be like the flu shot that targets certain viruses, while it misses the other flu viruses. As the drama unfolded, we soon began to hear of variants and the need for booster shots. We now know for sure that this shot does not give an immunization for Covid 19, and hence, for clarity it is better to call it a flu shot.

I remember so well farming in the early 90’s and hearing about Roundup-Ready crops. It seemed too good to be true to be able to spray glyphosate (Roundup) over the top of the crop and take out all the weeds while doing no harm to the crop. The manufacturer did keep telling us to spray maximum rates so as to ‘kill’ every weed. Theoretically they were right, if we could have killed every weed, without missing one, we would not have had the next problem—spray-resistant weeds. We didn’t realize how fast our troublesome ‘pigweeds’ (and other weeds) in the south, would mutate and develop a resistance to glyphosate.

Sure, farmers had several good years with an easy way to keep out the weeds, but that didn’t last and now the situation is worse than it was before. Today, every farmer knows about ‘Palmer amaranth Pigweed’. You can almost ‘pour’ glyphosate on it, and still it thrives. These weeds mutated very rapidly and became resistant.

I think we have a similar scenario with the Covid shot. I’m certainly not a scientist but it does seem to me that since the shot admittedly mostly reduces symptoms instead of producing immunity, then it will most likely speed up the mutation of the Covid-19 virus. This seems like the normal ‘struggle for survival’ principle of life.

The rapid speed with which this shot came on the market is another concern. We really don’t know what all it will bring down the road nor the side effects it may cause. We don’t know how many boosters will be called for. It seems the world is the test field at the moment, and from what I’m seeing it is not working too well and many of the people who have had the shot don’t really trust it. The people who have had the virus have built an immunity that is far superior to the protection of the shot. We’ve known since childhood that when we had the flu, our body would build immunity to that strain. This is the way our Maker designed us. One of the first people I personally knew that had Covid was told they would have six months of immunity. I wondered how they figured that out so quickly. This was a new virus, and we had no experience to draw on for this virus. Also, the viruses we were familiar with gave lifetime immunity to that strain. So what science was behind this?

Hence, I think it much better to take precautions and do what we can to boost our immune system. It is an excellent time to remember we are to be stewards of the body that God gave us. It’s a good time to put a plan in place of good nutrition, exercise, and weight loss. If you are overweight, you are much more likely to be affected by this pestilence and many other illnesses. If you regularly consume sugary drinks or unhealthy foods of any kind, it is an excellent time to kick the habit and reduce your sugar consumption. If you are overweight or out of shape physically, there is no better time than now to bring your body into a condition that will be much healthier, so you will be better able to ward off this virus and many other illnesses.

My belief is that in the long run it will be safer and better to do my part and let this body build the immunities to protect itself against this virus. I realize there are those who have died after contracting this illness. I don’t belittle this fact and I am sorry for the loss of life. I do believe too that we as Christians should constantly commit our lives to God and look at the whole picture of life and its preservation through the lens of Christian ethics.

It is unprecedented that an illness with a recovery rate of somewhere around 99%, would cause such a stir, the world over. We know that if it wouldn’t be for the invention of social media there would not have been near the panic and turmoil. One of my greatest concerns is how we are being ‘conditioned’ for more to come. Who would have ever thought that a flu virus would be the instrument that ushers in a global push for something that will be the benchmark for whether we can travel, go to eating places, gather for public events and other such restrictions. It sounds strangely similar to what God says will one day be a reality—And he causeth all, both small and great, rich and poor, free and bond, to receive a mark in their right hand, or in their foreheads: And that no man might buy or sell, save he that had the mark, or the name of the beast, or the number of his name –Revelation 13:16-17.

I have been almost ridiculed for even mentioning the mark of the beast. Still others think this passage is to be spiritualized and has nothing to do with the end time system of government. Still others think the bride will be raptured before this, hence nothing for us to be concerned with. I could wish one of these views would be right, then I could move along in silence hoping that all would be well.

I will hasten to say that I don’t think this is the ‘mark of the beast’, but rather I see it as another step closer to that event. I also hasten to say that this is not a writing to ridicule another belief nor is it an effort to try to pull together certain Scriptures to try to support a particular doctrinal agenda such as the idea that all believers will be raptured prior to the unfolding of end time events, thereby escaping what the Bible refers to as “great tribulation”. –See Matthew 24:21 and Revelation 7:14. It’s time we open our eyes to the ‘conditioning’ that our society is having upon us in general, and the conditioning of this shot in particular. There are all kinds of good reasons we will go ahead with it—it makes good sense, it defies science not to, I’ve even heard we can be better witnesses if we have had it, and the list goes on. All the while we are being ‘conditioned’ to do what it takes to keep rolling down our economic road.

So, my plea is that we consider where we are headed. One day God’s people will need to jump off the train of this world—Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you –2 Corinthians 6:17. Revelation 14:10-11 declares that all who take the mark will seal their destiny in hell. The next verse gives a calling for the endurance of the saints—Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus –Revelation 14:12.

There will be hard times—Read Matthew 24:4-28. Consider the famines, pestilences, and earthquakes that are promised will come. Jesus said all these are the beginnings of sorrows—literally birth pangs. He said along with this, ‘the end is not yet’. Yet we have the promise of triumph—And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death –Revelation 12:11. I say again, “One day the saints will need to jump off the economic train.”

I think now is an excellent time to evaluate our attachment, whether it is connected to this world or to our future heavenly reward. Let’s make a commitment anew to identify with our soon coming Lord and King. Also, it’s an excellent time to share the gospel of Jesus’ Kingdom with a society that is bent on going away from the Creator.

So, for now, I’m content to feel safe with the immunity in my body as God created it and I am purposing in a new way to seek the immunity from the ways of sin and evil and to be inoculated with the Holy Ghost from heaven. Will you join me in this commitment?

J’ai pris plaisir à écouter, et même à participer à, des discussions au sujet de l’injection contre le Covid — pourquoi quelqu’un l’a reçue et pourquoi un autre ne l’a pas reçue. J’ose dire que nous pourrions avoir sept personnes donnant leur point de vue sur le sujet et peut‑être huit idées différentes.

Je commence par la mise en garde que ce sont mes réflexions, et je suis tout à fait d’accord que quelqu’un puisse être en désaccord. En fait, j’accueillerais volontiers d’autres personnes partageant leur point de vue.

Une des choses que vous remarquerez dans cet écrit est que je n’appelle pas l’injection contre le Covid un « vaccin ». Non pas qu’elle ne corresponde pas techniquement à la définition officielle, mais plutôt parce qu’elle ne fonctionne pas de la manière dont nous avons connu les vaccins. Je me souviens quand j’étais gamin d’environ quatre ans, je suis allé avec ma mère au service de santé et j’ai reçu une vaccination dans le haut du bras contre la variole. (La cicatrice est encore là) Je me souviens quelques années plus tard quand toute la communauté s’est rassemblée à notre école publique locale pour le traitement du sucre en cube qui était une vaccination orale contre la polio. Je ne me souviens pas si j’ai eu d’autres vaccinations ou non. Mon point est que ces vaccinations étaient des immunisations contre une maladie. On nous assurait que nous n’aurions pas la variole, la polio, la rougeole ou autre pour lequel nous étions vaccinés. Et nous ne l’avons pas eue — pas seulement en moindre quantité ou un cas moins grave. Nous comprenions que nous étions immunisés, et la lutte était terminée.

Pendant la pandémie actuelle, nous n’avons cessé d’entendre parler de la vaccination qui arrivait. Cela semblait être la réponse à cette peste qui s’était abattue sur le monde. Certains d’entre nous se demandaient si ce serait comme le vaccin contre la grippe qui cible certains virus, tout en manquant d’autres virus grippaux. Au fur et à mesure que le drame se déroulait, nous avons vite entendu parler de variants et du besoin de doses de rappel. Nous savons maintenant avec certitude que cette injection n’apporte pas d’immunisation contre le Covid‑19, et donc, pour plus de clarté, il vaut mieux l’appeler un vaccin antigrippal.

Je me souviens si bien d’exploiter la ferme au début des années 90 et d’entendre parler des cultures « Roundup‑Ready ». Cela semblait trop beau pour être vrai de pouvoir pulvériser du glyphosate (Roundup) au‑dessus de la culture et éliminer toutes les mauvaises herbes sans nuire à la culture. Le fabricant ne cessait de nous dire de pulvériser aux doses maximales afin de « tuer » toute mauvaise herbe. Théoriquement, ils avaient raison : si nous avions pu tuer chaque mauvaise herbe, sans en manquer une, nous n’aurions pas eu le problème suivant — des mauvaises herbes résistantes aux traitements. Nous n’avions pas réalisé à quelle vitesse nos « amaranthes de Palmer » gênantes (et d’autres mauvaises herbes) dans le sud muteraient et développeraient une résistance au glyphosate.

Sûr, les agriculteurs ont eu plusieurs bonnes années avec un moyen facile d’éliminer les mauvaises herbes, mais cela n’a pas duré et aujourd’hui la situation est pire qu’avant. Aujourd’hui, chaque agriculteur connaît « l’amarante de Palmer ». On peut presque « verser » du glyphosate dessus, et elle prospère malgré tout. Ces mauvaises herbes ont muté très rapidement et sont devenues résistantes.

Je pense que nous avons un scénario similaire avec l’injection contre le Covid. Je ne suis certainement pas scientifique, mais il me semble que puisque l’injection réduit principalement les symptômes au lieu de produire une immunité, elle accélérera très probablement la mutation du virus Covid‑19. Cela ressemble au principe normal de « lutte pour la survie » de la vie.

La rapidité avec laquelle cette injection est arrivée sur le marché est une autre préoccupation. Nous ne savons vraiment pas ce que cela apportera à terme ni quels effets secondaires elle peut provoquer. Nous ne savons pas combien de rappels seront nécessaires. Il semble que le monde soit le champ d’essai pour le moment, et d’après ce que je vois, cela ne fonctionne pas très bien et beaucoup de personnes qui ont reçu l’injection ne lui font pas vraiment confiance. Les personnes qui ont eu le virus ont développé une immunité bien supérieure à la protection de l’injection. Nous savons depuis l’enfance que lorsque nous avions la grippe, notre corps développait une immunité à cette souche. C’est ainsi que notre Créateur nous a conçus. L’un des premiers que je connaissais personnellement et qui a eu le Covid s’est vu dire qu’il aurait six mois d’immunité. Je me suis demandé comment ils avaient pu le déterminer si rapidement. C’était un nouveau virus, et nous n’avions aucune expérience sur laquelle nous appuyer pour ce virus. De plus, les virus que nous connaissions donnaient une immunité à vie à cette souche. Alors, quelle science était derrière cela ?

C’est pourquoi je pense qu’il est bien mieux de prendre des précautions et de faire ce que nous pouvons pour renforcer notre système immunitaire. C’est un excellent moment pour se rappeler que nous devons être des intendants du corps que Dieu nous a donné. C’est un bon moment pour établir un plan de bonne nutrition, d’exercice et de perte de poids. Si vous êtes en surpoids, vous êtes beaucoup plus susceptible d’être affecté par cette peste et par bien d’autres maladies. Si vous consommez régulièrement des boissons sucrées ou des aliments malsains de quelque nature que ce soit, c’est un excellent moment pour rompre l’habitude et réduire votre consommation de sucre. Si vous êtes en surpoids ou hors de forme physiquement, il n’y a pas de meilleur moment que maintenant pour mettre votre corps dans une condition beaucoup plus saine, afin que vous puissiez mieux repousser ce virus et bien d’autres maladies.

Ma conviction est qu’à long terme il sera plus sûr et meilleur de faire ma part et de laisser ce corps développer les immunités pour se protéger contre ce virus. Je réalise qu’il y a des personnes qui sont mortes après avoir contracté cette maladie. Je ne minimise pas ce fait et je regrette la perte de vies. Je crois aussi que nous, en tant que chrétiens, devrions constamment remettre nos vies à Dieu et regarder l’ensemble du tableau de la vie et de sa préservation à travers le prisme de l’éthique chrétienne.

Il est sans précédent qu’une maladie avec un taux de guérison d’environ 99 % suscite une telle agitation, à travers le monde. Nous savons que sans l’invention des médias sociaux, il n’y aurait pas eu une panique et un trouble aussi importants. Une de mes plus grandes inquiétudes est la manière dont nous sommes « conditionnés » pour d’autres choses à venir. Qui aurait jamais pensé qu’un virus grippal serait l’instrument qui inaugurerait une poussée mondiale pour quelque chose qui servira de référence pour savoir si nous pouvons voyager, aller au restaurant, nous rassembler pour des événements publics et d’autres restrictions semblables. Cela sonne étrangement similaire à ce que Dieu dit qu’un jour sera une réalité — Et il fit en sorte que tous, petits et grands, riches et pauvres, libres et esclaves, reçoivent une marque sur leur main droite, ou sur leur front: Et que nul ne puisse acheter ni vendre, que celui qui ait la marque, ou le nom de la bête, ou le nombre de son nom – Apocalypse 13:16-17.

J’ai été presque ridiculisé pour avoir même évoqué la marque de la bête. D’autres pensent encore que ce passage doit être spiritualisé et n’a rien à voir avec le système gouvernemental de la fin des temps. D’autres pensent que l’Épouse sera enlevée avant cela, et donc rien pour nous à craindre. J’aimerais que l’une de ces opinions soit juste, alors je pourrais avancer en silence en espérant que tout ira bien.

Je me hâte de dire que je ne pense pas que ceci soit la « marque de la bête », mais plutôt que je le vois comme une étape de plus vers cet événement. Je me hâte aussi de dire que cet écrit n’a pas pour objet de ridiculiser une autre croyance ni de tenter d’assembler certains textes bibliques pour soutenir un agenda doctrinal particulier tel que l’idée que tous les croyants seront enlevés avant le déroulement des événements de la fin des temps, échappant ainsi à ce que la Bible appelle la « grande tribulation ». –Voir Matthieu 24:21 et Apocalypse 7:14. Il est temps que nous ouvrions les yeux sur le « conditionnement » que notre société exerce sur nous en général, et le conditionnement lié à cette injection en particulier. Il existe toutes sortes de bonnes raisons pour lesquelles nous irons de l’avant — cela a du sens, défier la science serait insensé, j’ai même entendu dire que nous pouvons être de meilleurs témoins si nous l’avons reçue, et la liste continue. Pendant ce temps nous sommes « conditionnés » à faire ce qu’il faut pour continuer à rouler sur notre route économique.

Ainsi, ma supplique est que nous réfléchissions à notre destination. Un jour, le peuple de Dieu devra sauter du train de ce monde — C’est pourquoi sortons du milieu d’eux, et séparons‑nous, dit le Seigneur, et ne touchons à rien d’impur; et je vous recevrai – 2 Corinthiens 6:17. Apocalypse 14:10‑11 déclare que tous ceux qui prendront la marque scelleront leur destin en enfer. Le verset suivant appelle à la persévérance des saints — Voici la patience des saints: voici ceux qui gardent les commandements de Dieu, et la foi en Jésus – Apocalypse 14:12.

Il y aura des moments difficiles — Lisez Matthieu 24:4-28. Considérez les famines, pestes et tremblements de terre qui sont promis de venir. Jésus a dit que tout cela est le commencement de douleurs — littéralement des douleurs de l’enfantement. Il a dit en même temps que « la fin n’est pas encore ». Pourtant nous avons la promesse du triomphe — Et ils l’ont vaincu à cause du sang de l’Agneau, et à cause de la parole de leur témoignage; et ils n’ont pas aimé leur vie jusqu’à la mort – Apocalypse 12:11. Je le redis, « Un jour les saints devront sauter du train économique. »

Je pense que c’est maintenant un excellent moment pour évaluer notre attachement, qu’il soit lié à ce monde ou à notre future récompense céleste. Engageons‑nous à nouveau à nous identifier à notre Seigneur et Roi qui vient bientôt. De plus, c’est un excellent moment pour partager l’Évangile du Royaume de Jésus avec une société qui a tendance à s’éloigner du Créateur.

Donc, pour l’instant, je suis content de me sentir en sécurité avec l’immunité dans mon corps telle que Dieu l’a créée et je me propose d’une nouvelle manière de rechercher l’immunité contre les voies du péché et du mal et d’être inoculé du Saint‑Esprit venu du ciel. Voulez‑vous vous joindre à moi dans cet engagement ?

Greetings to each one in the worthy name of Jesus Christ, our Saviour, and our Redeemer.

This magazine issue may seem to be arriving more quickly on the heels of the last one. True. We are continuing to tighten up our schedule as we work towards getting each quarterly issue out in a more timely manner. Our ultimate goal is to have them arrive in your mailboxes in the months of March, June, September, and December of each year. Pray for us as we continue moving towards that schedule.

From time to time, we receive feedback—suggestions, concerns, and encouragement. We value this feedback. It is filed away and used by the board as we continually evaluate ways to make our magazine better. One final thought on this matter… when we receive feedback of encouragement regarding a specific article, it is helpful for us, and it is encouraging for our authors as we pass that along to them. We welcome your ongoing feedback.

As previously mentioned, we are including several new categories in this issue. One on Church History that is being written by two young brothers from our church. And one on Hymn Histories being written by one of our board members, a middle-aged married man, who is also from our church.

In “Moses in Midian”, we take a walk in Moses’ footsteps during the mid-section of his life. He was uprooted from his comfortable lifestyle in Egypt as an adopted son of royalty and was then sent by God into the desert to learn some much-needed lessons in further preparation towards becoming God’s servant. As we take a look at the life of Jonah, we glean glimpses of “The God Who Will Not Let Go”. Often a struggling believer loses sight of the Truth of God because they believe the lie that no one cares, yet the truth of the matter is this—the God of the Bible doesn’t just drop us, or turn His back on us, the instant that we take a wrong turn or a misstep. Let’s allow this article to help us to become rooted and grounded in the biblical Truth of Abba Father—a Father who cares for His children. We also have the second article in a continuing series on discipleship, as well as an article written by a middle-aged, spiritually-mature sister who shares her encouragement for sisters to evaluate what God thinks of their attire.

Church History and Should A Christian Vote

Finally, let’s consider the two short articles on church history. One of our goals for this issue is burdened with the awareness that the country in which we live (the U.S.) is approaching mid-term elections in November of this year and that there will be a strong push for many conservative Anabaptists to become involved in the voting process to ensure a proper outcome for the good of their perceived cause or goals.

In the natural world our “old man” has the tendency to think that we must “do something” if we expect things to go in a “right” direction. The spiritual Truth is this: The king’s heart is in the hand of the LORD, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will –Proverbs 21:1. If we think that, as believers, we will have a part in electing the “right” person in an election if we personally vote, let’s stop to consider what God Himself told Nebuchadnezzar. …That the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will –Daniel 4:31-32.

Throughout the history of the Anabaptist people there have been varied opinions on this matter, however, it is our wish to lift up the perspective that Jesus said …My kingdom is not of this world: if my kingdom were of this world, then would my servants fight … but now is my kingdom not from hence –John 18:36. When we understand and develop a personal world view that is founded on the two-kingdom principle, we realize that we must function as …strangers and pilgrims on the earth. [While we] …declare plainly that [we] seek a country …a better country, that is, an heavenly: wherefore God is not ashamed to be called [our] God: for he hath prepared for [us] a city –Hebrews 11:13-16. In all things involving political involvement, it is our encouragement that New Testament believers should obey the command to …come out from among them, and be ye separate… –2 Corinthians 6:17.

Let’s always cultivate a right attitude in our hearts so that our talk and actions reflect God’s view on the matter when He through the Apostle Paul tells us to: Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God … For he is the minister of God to thee… –Romans 13:1-4.

It is in consideration of these thoughts that we wrote the two articles detailing very different times in the history of the church and what it was like for Christians to relate to the government of their day. Let us seriously ponder whether we can do more good by getting involved in politics, especially in the voting process. Or whether God wants us to pray for our elected officials, to view them as His servants, and to speak about them with respect. Ultimately, we must trust God to bring about His will for the winding down of the “clock of time” as time speeds onward towards the end of time. God will do this through hardening the hearts of ungodly men in positions of power, just like Pharaoh of old, to accomplish His sovereign will for the world.

So, what is the solution when we struggle within our hearts about the direction of our country and its growing instability or when we experience so much pressure from our peers or the society around us to get involved to make a difference? The Apostle Paul gives us very clear direction when he says, I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men; For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty. 1 Timothy 2:1-2. The Christian’s secret power of influence lies in the power of prayer that is produced in the privacy of his or her closet. However, for this prayer to have power it must be produced out of a heart of faith—And Jesus said unto them … verily I say unto you, If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you –Matthew 17:20. Let us always remember that …The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much –James 5:16.

Until the next time, may God be with each one and grant you grace and peace as you walk faithfully according to His Word. Let us pray for each other as we go through the trying times in our world today.
