Salutations à chacun au digne nom de Jésus-Christ, notre Sauveur et notre Rédempteur.

Ce numéro du magazine peut sembler paraître plus rapidement sur les talons du précédent. C’est vrai. Nous continuons de resserrer notre calendrier alors que nous travaillons pour publier chaque numéro trimestriel de manière plus ponctuelle. Notre objectif ultime est qu’ils arrivent dans vos boîtes aux lettres aux mois de mars, juin, septembre et décembre de chaque année. Priez pour nous alors que nous continuons d’avancer vers ce calendrier.

De temps à autre, nous recevons des réactions — suggestions, préoccupations et encouragements. Nous apprécions ces retours. Ils sont archivés et utilisés par le conseil alors que nous évaluons continuellement des moyens d’améliorer notre magazine. Une dernière pensée à ce sujet… lorsque nous recevons un retour d’encouragement concernant un article spécifique, cela nous est utile et c’est encourageant pour nos auteurs lorsque nous leur transmettons. Nous accueillons vos retours continus.

Comme mentionné précédemment, nous incluons plusieurs nouvelles rubriques dans ce numéro. L’une sur l’histoire de l’Église, écrite par deux jeunes frères de notre Église. Et une sur l’histoire des cantiques, écrite par un de nos membres du conseil, un homme marié d’âge moyen, qui est lui aussi de notre Église.

Dans « Moïse à Madian », nous marchons dans les pas de Moïse pendant la section médiane de sa vie. Il fut déraciné de son style de vie confortable en Égypte en tant que fils adopté de la royauté, puis envoyé par Dieu dans le désert pour apprendre des leçons fort nécessaires en vue de devenir davantage le serviteur de Dieu. En regardant la vie de Jonas, nous recueillons des aperçus de « Dieu qui ne lâche pas ». Souvent, un croyant en difficulté perd de vue la vérité de Dieu parce qu’il croit le mensonge que personne ne se soucie de lui, pourtant la vérité est la suivante — le Dieu de la Bible ne nous abandonne pas simplement, ni ne nous tourne le dos, au moment même où nous prenons un mauvais virage ou faisons un faux pas. Laissons cet article nous aider à nous enracin­er et nous établir dans la Vérité biblique d’Abba Père — un Père qui prend soin de ses enfants. Nous avons aussi le deuxième article d’une série continue sur le discipulat, ainsi qu’un article écrit par une sœur d’âge moyen, spirituellement mûre, qui partage son encouragement pour que les sœurs évaluent ce que Dieu pense de leur tenue vestimentaire.

Histoire de l’Église et Faut‑il qu’un chrétien vote

Enfin, considérons les deux courts articles sur l’histoire de l’Église. L’un de nos objectifs pour ce numéro est empreint de la conscience que le pays dans lequel nous vivons (les États‑Unis) approche des élections de mi‑mandat en novembre de cette année et qu’il y aura une forte pression pour que de nombreux anabaptistes conservateurs s’impliquent dans le processus électoral afin d’assurer un résultat jugé propre au bien de leur cause ou de leurs objectifs perçus.

Dans le monde naturel, notre « vieil homme » a tendance à penser que nous devons « faire quelque chose » si nous attendons que les choses tournent dans une direction « correcte ». La vérité spirituelle est celle-ci : Le cœur du roi est dans la main de l’Éternel, comme les rivières d’eau; il l’incline où il veut –Proverbes 21:1. Si nous pensons que, en tant que croyants, nous aurons une part à élire la « bonne » personne dans une élection si nous votons personnellement, réfléchissons à ce que Dieu dit lui‑même à Nebucadnetsar. …Que le Très‑haut domine dans le royaume des hommes, et qu’il le donne à qui il veut –Daniel 4:31-32.

Tout au long de l’histoire du peuple anabaptiste, il y a eu des opinions variées sur cette question; toutefois, nous souhaitons mettre en avant la perspective que Jésus a déclaré : …Mon royaume n’est pas de ce monde: si mon royaume était de ce monde, mes serviteurs lutteraient… mais maintenant mon royaume n’est point d’ici –Jean 18:36. Quand nous comprenons et développons une vision du monde personnelle fondée sur le principe des deux royaumes, nous réalisons que nous devons agir comme …étrangers et voyageurs sur la terre. [En déclarant] …que nous cherchons une patrie …une meilleure patrie, c’est‑à‑dire céleste: c’est pourquoi Dieu n’a pas honte d’être appelé leur Dieu: car il leur a préparé une cité –Hébreux 11:13-16. Dans toutes les choses impliquant l’engagement politique, il est notre encouragement que les croyants du Nouveau Testament obéissent au commandement de …sortir du milieu d’eux, et séparez‑vous… –2 Corinthiens 6:17.

Cultivons toujours une attitude correcte dans nos cœurs afin que nos paroles et nos actions reflètent le point de vue de Dieu sur la question lorsqu’Il, par l’apôtre Paul, nous dit : Que toute personne soit soumise aux autorités supérieures. Car il n’y a point d’autorité qui ne vienne de Dieu: les autorités qui existent ont été instituées par Dieu … Car c’est un ministre de Dieu à ton profit… –Romains 13:1-4.

C’est en considération de ces pensées que nous avons rédigé les deux articles détaillant des époques très différentes de l’histoire de l’Église et comment les chrétiens se rapportaient au gouvernement de leur temps. Réfléchissons sérieusement à la question de savoir si nous pouvons faire plus de bien en nous engageant en politique, spécialement dans le processus électoral. Ou si Dieu veut que nous priions pour nos responsables élus, que nous les regardions comme Ses serviteurs, et que nous parlions d’eux avec respect. Ultimement, nous devons faire confiance à Dieu pour accomplir Sa volonté concernant le décompte du « cadran du temps » alors que le temps file vers la fin des temps. Dieu accomplira cela en endurcissant les cœurs des hommes impies en positions de pouvoir, tout comme Pharaon jadis, afin d’accomplir Sa volonté souveraine pour le monde.

Alors, quelle est la solution lorsque nous luttons dans nos cœurs au sujet de l’orientation de notre pays et de son instabilité croissante, ou lorsque nous subissons tant de pression de la part de nos pairs ou de la société autour de nous pour nous impliquer afin de faire une différence ? L’apôtre Paul nous donne une direction très claire lorsqu’il dit : J’exhorte donc, avant toutes choses, à faire des supplications, des prières, des intercessions, et des actions de grâces, pour tous les hommes; pour les rois, et pour tous ceux qui sont en dignité; afin que nous menions une vie calme et paisible, en toute piété et honnêteté. 1 Timothée 2:1-2. Le pouvoir secret d’influence du chrétien réside dans le pouvoir de la prière produite dans l’intimité de son cabinet. Cependant, pour que cette prière ait de la puissance, elle doit provenir d’un cœur de foi — Et Jésus leur dit… je vous le dis en vérité, si vous aviez de la foi comme un grain de moutarde, vous diriez à cette montagne: Transporte‑toi d’ici là; et elle se transporterait; et rien ne vous serait impossible –Matthieu 17:20. Souvenons‑nous toujours que …La prière fervente du juste a beaucoup de succès –Jacques 5:16.

Jusqu’à la prochaine fois, que Dieu soit avec chacun et vous accorde grâce et paix tandis que vous marchez fidèlement selon Sa Parole. Prions les uns pour les autres alors que nous traversons les temps d’épreuve dans notre monde aujourd’hui.

Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted?… –Matthew 5:13.

One might wonder as to why the Anabaptists, the early church fathers, church history writers, and especially the progenitor (originator or author) of our beliefs, Christ Himself, effected such a vehement and absolute approach to a separated church and state. Why did they unanimously preach, write, and otherwise caution against political involvement of any kind by Christians? Perhaps this is best answered by looking at the results of Christians ignoring these sincere warnings, casting off their Godly allegiance, and pledging themselves to a flawed and ultimately futile earthly kingdom.

The Mennonites of Germany are a particularly intriguing and cautionary episode of Christian and Anabaptist histories—not only because of their relative proximity to our time—but also because of their almost wholesale devotion to a worldly leader and agenda. What led them to such an un-Christ-like position? A true understanding of their story must begin, naturally, with their beginnings.

The Mennonites of 20th century Germany were descended from the first Anabaptist groups, but unlike our ancestors, they stayed in the Old World instead of emigrating to the New World. There, a number of factors led them to a unique position within world events, a position that would test their mettle on a global stage.

The beginnings of the 20th century brought about the first World War, which ended with the defeat of Germany and its allies. The resulting peace treaties were structured to humiliate and crush Germany, saddling it with an almost unpayable war debt, and restricting its rights to build a military. The German people, unsurprisingly, resented this insult being added to the injury of having lost the War. Their resentment festered, and soon manifested itself in nationalistic movements, the most notable of which was the National Socialist German Workers Party (or the Nazi Party). The party was founded in 1919, and Hitler was amongst its first members. He quickly assumed party leadership, attracting followers with his “us vs. them” rhetoric and strong leadership.

Party growth was small in the decade following its founding. During this time, Hitler continued to shape the Nazis according to his wishes. Hatred for most non-German (Aryan) groups became a central party theme, along with a violent distaste for communism. However, the party was not large enough to be anything but a fringe voice, representing only a small portion of German voters.

Insignificance did not last, however. The Great Depression brought the catalyst for the Nazi’s rise to power. When the global market crashed, over 2 million Germans lost their jobs. Unemployed, they rallied around the charismatic leadership that promised to give them jobs, give them power, to “Make Germany great again”. Moving quickly, Hitler added legions to his followers.

The thousands of new Nazi Party members enabled the Nazi Party to seriously contest many local elections, and in Germany’s Parliament, they were able to control enough votes to sway policy making. In the long run, their political might handed Hitler the office of prime minister. Having secured that position, he went on to overthrow the German government, establishing himself and his party as the undisputed rulers of Germany.

Why did such a man, and such a movement, attract the attention and adoration of a church that professed much of what we do? Loving our enemies, separation from the world, and nonresistance did not seem to combine with the message of the Nazis. The answer, like most backsliding churches, is best portrayed as happening in small steps and over time.

In 1929, the Mennonites came under the eye of Germany and its rapidly expanding Nazi Party. 13,000 Russian Mennonite refugees descended on Moscow, seeking an exit from the Communist-run country. The Nazis seized the situation, using the Mennonites as supposed evidence that Aryans (peoples of German lineage, such as the Mennonites) were being unjustly used by the rest of the world. This image was pushed by state propaganda departments, who circulated writings, pamphlets, and even two immensely popular movies, depicting the Mennonites as strong, red-blooded Germans valiantly striving against the unjust oppression of the Russian Communists. These efforts afforded the refugees national attention, which subsequently led to them being admitted into Germany.

While many Mennonites entered Germany, as refugees and otherwise, there were also thriving, established communities that were given the same patriotic make-over by the Nazi propogandists. Unfortunately, these churches welcomed the Nazi attention, going so far as to send Hitler a letter thanking him for being the “savior of the German peoples” and pledging their support to his government. It is of note that Hitler, a man quite busy running an emerging world power, personally responded to this letter with a memo thanking the churches for their support and expressing a desire for further cooperation to the benefit of both the Nazis and the Mennonites. The church further weakened under these seemingly beneficial relations.

A particularly shocking case of Mennonite political involvement came from the churches in or around Danzig. Danzig and the surrounding countryside had long been a part of the German Empire, until the end of World War I, when the region was separated from Germany, essentially becoming a buffer zone between Germany and Poland. In 1939, Hitler would make one of his first moves on Europe by annexing Danzig, where the Nazis had been building party influence for most of the 1930’s. The Mennonites of the area, having been German only a generation before, welcomed their new part in the Germany of the future, becoming involved in almost every level of the Nazi Party. Otto Andres became the second-highest ranked Nazi of the Danzig area, and scores of the 6,000 believers in the surrounding congregations joined various Nazi organizations. The men often took part in the paramilitary SA and SS, while their wives and daughters took part in corresponding women’s groups. Churches became saturated with active Nazis, even going so far as to accept them into church leadership. At one point, five of the seven local churches were led by active party members.

World War II was the final step in the Mennonites’ integration with the Nazis. The German concentration camp of Stutthof supplied slave labor to numerous Mennonite businesses. Mennonite churches organized war efforts, including recruiting their young men to serve in the German army. In a particularly twisted case, a Mennonite doctor, Johan Klassen, was personally responsible for the deaths of more than one hundred disabled children.

Perhaps the most concerning episode in this dismal tale of backsliding comes after the war. Mennonite leadership, recognizing to some extent the terrible depths to which they had fallen, and noting the justice that was to come through the Nuremburg trials, effectively shrugged the blame from off their shoulders. Appealing to their Mennonite brothers across the ocean, they convinced them of their innocence, twisting their involvement in the Nazi regime to make themselves appear the victims. American Mennonites helped these now-refugees in many ways, providing all manner of assistance, and ultimately keeping most of them from facing possible prison time or death sentences. The surviving German churches eventually disintegrated or emigrated to the Americas.

If a group who originally held beliefs identical to our own could stray to the point of child murder and slave labor, then the question must be asked: “Are we seeing their folly for what it was?” Why did the churches of Danzig accept the advances of what, in retrospect, was a clearly un-biblical, un-Christlike movement?

The origin for their downfall was surprisingly simple. The Mennonites of Germany forgot who their true Ruler was. No earthly kingdom at war tolerates an allegiance to the enemy, and neither does the Kingdom of Heaven. The pride in their earthly kingdom, the pursuit of prestige and power, all led to a foreseeable end. Their salt had lost its savor, and they were cast out and trodden underfoot. This is a cautionary tale of the dangers of an unequal yoking of the church with the world.

Kamu adalah garam dunia; tetapi kalau garam itu menjadi tawar, dengan apakah ia diasinkan?… –Matius 5:13.

Seseorang mungkin bertanya-tanya mengapa kaum Anabaptis, para Bapa Gereja awal, penulis sejarah gereja, dan terutama pencetus (penggagas atau pengarang) dari keyakinan kita, Kristus sendiri, mengambil sikap yang begitu keras dan mutlak terhadap pemisahan gereja dan negara. Mengapa mereka dengan tegas berkhotbah, menulis, dan memperingatkan terhadap keterlibatan politik apa pun oleh orang Kristen? Mungkin jawaban terbaik dapat ditemukan dengan melihat hasil ketika orang Kristen mengabaikan peringatan tulus ini, melepaskan kesetiaan mereka kepada Allah, dan mengikatkan diri kepada sebuah kerajaan duniawi yang cacat dan pada akhirnya sia-sia.

Mennonit di Jerman adalah episode yang sangat menarik dan penuh peringatan dalam sejarah Kristen dan Anabaptis—bukan hanya karena kedekatan waktu mereka dengan kita—tetapi juga karena pengabdian mereka yang nyaris total kepada seorang pemimpin dan agenda duniawi. Apa yang membawa mereka ke posisi yang tidak menyerupai Kristus itu? Pemahaman yang benar tentang kisah mereka harus dimulai, tentu saja, dari asal-usul mereka.

Mennonit Jerman abad ke-20 menurunkan asal-usul dari kelompok-kelompok Anabaptis pertama, tetapi tidak seperti nenek moyang kita, mereka tetap berada di Dunia Lama dan tidak berhijrah ke Dunia Baru. Di sana, sejumlah faktor mendorong mereka ke posisi unik dalam peristiwa dunia, sebuah posisi yang akan menguji keteguhan mereka di panggung global.

Permulaan abad ke-20 membawa Perang Dunia pertama, yang berakhir dengan kekalahan Jerman dan sekutunya. Perjanjian damai yang dihasilkan disusun untuk mempermalukan dan menghancurkan Jerman, membebani negara itu dengan hutang perang yang nyaris tak terbayar, dan membatasi haknya untuk membangun militer. Warga Jerman, tidak mengherankan, merasakan penghinaan ini sebagai tambahan atas luka karena kalah perang. Kebencian mereka membusuk, dan segera memanifestasikan diri dalam gerakan nasionalis, yang paling menonjol adalah Partai Pekerja Sosialis Nasional Jerman (atau Partai Nazi). Partai itu didirikan pada 1919, dan Hitler termasuk di antara anggota awalnya. Ia segera mengambil kepemimpinan partai, menarik pengikut dengan retorika “kami melawan mereka” dan kepemimpinan yang kuat.

Pertumbuhan partai kecil pada dekade setelah pendiriannya. Selama waktu itu, Hitler terus membentuk kaum Nazi menurut kehendaknya. Kebencian terhadap sebagian besar kelompok non-Jerman (Arya) menjadi tema sentral partai, bersama dengan kebencian yang keras terhadap komunisme. Namun partai itu belum cukup besar sehingga hanya menjadi suara pinggiran, mewakili hanya sebagian kecil pemilih Jerman.

Ketidakpentingan itu tidak bertahan lama. Depresi Besar membawa katalis bagi kebangkitan Nazi. Ketika pasar global runtuh, lebih dari 2 juta orang Jerman kehilangan pekerjaan. Menganggur, mereka berkumpul di sekitar kepemimpinan karismatik yang menjanjikan pekerjaan, memberi mereka kekuasaan, untuk “Membuat Jerman hebat lagi”. Bergerak cepat, Hitler menambah barisan pengikutnya.

Ribuan anggota baru Partai Nazi memungkinkan partai tersebut untuk bersaing secara serius dalam banyak pemilihan lokal, dan di Parlemen Jerman, mereka mampu mengendalikan suara yang cukup untuk mempengaruhi pembuatan kebijakan. Dalam jangka panjang, kekuatan politik mereka memberikan Hitler jabatan perdana menteri. Setelah mengamankan posisi itu, ia kemudian menggulingkan pemerintahan Jerman, menegaskan dirinya dan partainya sebagai penguasa tak terbantahkan Jerman.

Mengapa seorang pria seperti itu, dan gerakan seperti itu, menarik perhatian dan kekaguman dari sebuah gereja yang mengakui banyak dari apa yang kita anut? Mengasihi musuh kita, pemisahan dari dunia, dan nonresistensi tampaknya tidak cocok dengan pesan Nazi. Jawabannya, seperti kebanyakan gereja yang menyimpang, paling baik digambarkan terjadi dalam langkah-langkah kecil dan selama waktu yang panjang.

Pada 1929, Mennonit berada di bawah pengamatan Jerman dan Partai Nazi yang sedang berkembang pesat. 13.000 pengungsi Mennonit Rusia turun ke Moskow, mencari jalan keluar dari negara yang dikuasai komunis. Nazi memanfaatkan situasi itu, menggunakan Mennonit sebagai bukti konon bahwa orang-orang Arya (bangsa keturunan Jerman, seperti Mennonit) diperlakukan tidak adil oleh dunia. Citra ini didorong oleh departemen propaganda negara, yang mengedarkan tulisan, pamflet, dan bahkan dua film yang sangat populer, menggambarkan Mennonit sebagai orang Jerman yang kuat dan berani yang berjuang melawan penindasan yang tidak adil oleh kaum Komunis Rusia. Upaya-upaya ini memberi perhatian nasional kepada para pengungsi, yang kemudian menyebabkan mereka diterima masuk ke Jerman.

Sementara banyak Mennonit masuk ke Jerman sebagai pengungsi dan lainnya, juga ada komunitas mapan yang berkembang yang mendapat sentuhan patriotik yang sama dari para propagandis Nazi. Sayangnya, gereja-gereja ini menyambut perhatian Nazi, sampai-sampai mengirim surat kepada Hitler yang berterima kasih atas menjadi “penyelamat bangsa Jerman” dan menyatakan kesetiaan mereka kepada pemerintahnya. Patut dicatat bahwa Hitler, seorang pria yang sangat sibuk menjalankan kekuatan dunia yang sedang muncul, secara pribadi menanggapi surat ini dengan sebuah memo yang berterima kasih kepada gereja-gereja atas dukungan mereka dan menyatakan keinginan untuk kerjasama lebih lanjut demi keuntungan Nazi dan Mennonit. Hubungan yang tampak menguntungkan ini semakin melemahkan gereja.

Sebuah kasus yang sangat mengejutkan dari keterlibatan politik Mennonit datang dari gereja-gereja di dalam atau sekitar Danzig. Danzig dan pedesaan sekitarnya lama menjadi bagian dari Kekaisaran Jerman, sampai akhir Perang Dunia I, ketika wilayah itu dipisahkan dari Jerman, pada dasarnya menjadi zona penyangga antara Jerman dan Polandia. Pada 1939, Hitler membuat salah satu langkah pertamanya di Eropa dengan menganeksasi Danzig, tempat Nazi membangun pengaruh partai selama sebagian besar tahun 1930-an. Mennonit di daerah itu, yang hanya satu generasi sebelumnya adalah Jerman, menyambut peran baru mereka dalam Jerman masa depan, terlibat dalam hampir setiap tingkat Partai Nazi. Otto Andres menjadi Nazi berpangkat kedua tertinggi di wilayah Danzig, dan puluhan dari 6.000 orang percaya di jemaat-jemaat sekitar bergabung dengan berbagai organisasi Nazi. Para pria sering ikut serta dalam paramiliter SA dan SS, sementara istri-istri dan putri-putri mereka ikut serta dalam kelompok-kelompok perempuan yang sepadan. Gereja-gereja menjadi dipenuhi oleh Nazi aktif, bahkan sampai menerima mereka ke dalam kepemimpinan gereja. Pada satu titik, lima dari tujuh gereja setempat dipimpin oleh anggota partai aktif.

Perang Dunia II adalah langkah terakhir dalam integrasi Mennonit dengan Nazi. Kamp konsentrasi Jerman Stutthof memasok tenaga paksa kepada banyak usaha Mennonit. Gereja-gereja Mennonit mengorganisir upaya perang, termasuk merekrut pemuda mereka untuk bertugas dalam tentara Jerman. Dalam sebuah kasus yang sangat bengkok, seorang dokter Mennonit, Johan Klassen, secara pribadi bertanggung jawab atas kematian lebih dari seratus anak yang cacat.

Mungkin episode yang paling mengkhawatirkan dalam kisah suram penyimpangan ini terjadi setelah perang. Kepemimpinan Mennonit, menyadari sampai tingkat tertentu kedalaman mengerikan ke mana mereka telah jatuh, dan mencatat keadilan yang akan datang melalui pengadilan Nuremberg, pada dasarnya melepaskan kesalahan dari pundak mereka. Mereka berpaling kepada saudara-saudara Mennonit mereka di seberang lautan, meyakinkan bahwa mereka tidak bersalah, memutarbalikkan keterlibatan mereka dalam rezim Nazi sehingga tampak seolah-olah mereka adalah korban. Mennonit Amerika membantu para pengungsi ini dalam banyak cara, menyediakan segala macam bantuan, dan pada akhirnya menjaga agar kebanyakan dari mereka tidak menghadapi kemungkinan hukuman penjara atau hukuman mati. Gereja-gereja Jerman yang tersisa akhirnya hancur atau bermigrasi ke Amerika.

Jika sebuah kelompok yang pada awalnya memegang keyakinan yang identik dengan kita bisa menyimpang sampai pada titik pembunuhan anak dan tenaga budak, maka pertanyaan yang harus diajukan adalah: "Apakah kita melihat kebodohan mereka sebagaimana mestinya?" Mengapa gereja-gereja Danzig menerima pendekatan apa yang, jika ditinjau kembali, adalah gerakan yang jelas tidak biblis dan tidak menyerupai Kristus?

Asal kejatuhan mereka ternyata sangat sederhana. Mennonit Jerman lupa siapa Penguasa mereka yang sejati. Tidak ada kerajaan duniawi yang sedang berperang yang mentolerir kesetiaan kepada musuh, begitu pula Kerajaan Surga. Kesombongan mereka terhadap kerajaan duniawi, pengejaran kehormatan dan kekuasaan, semuanya mengarah pada akhir yang dapat diperkirakan. Garam mereka kehilangan rasa, dan mereka dicampakkan serta diinjak-injak. Ini adalah kisah peringatan tentang bahaya pengikatan yang tidak setara antara gereja dan dunia.

The angel of the LORD encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them –Psalm 34:7.

“Tell us a story, Grandma,” begged two eager children as they crowded around her rocking chair.

“My, my, you children like to hear stories, don’t you?” replied Grandma, with a twinkle in her eye. “All right, I’ll tell you about a time when I was about eight years old, and my sister Lori was nine.

We lived on an old farm, back a short lane along a dirt road. One morning, Mother called us in from our play and said she was out of sugar. She asked us to walk to Mrs. Brightbill to see if she had any sugar to spare. You see, we didn’t have telephones when I was a little girl, so she couldn’t call the neighbor and ask her. Neighbors often shared back and forth because we didn’t go shopping at the store very often either. So, mother gave us a container, and we started out on our long walk as Mother called after us and reminded us not to loiter along the way.”

“How far was it to the Brightbills?” asked Sharon.

“Oh, it was about half a mile to our closest neighbor, the Rhine’s place, and then about another quarter of a mile to the Brightbills,” replied Grandma.

“Oh, that’s far. Mother won’t let us walk on the road at all,” added Micah.

“I’m sure you are right,” agreed Grandma. “And I hope you never walk on the road without your parents’ permission. But things were much different when I was a little girl. We also walked every day to school, which was quite a bit further than the Brightbill farm. So, the little errand we were doing on this morning for Mother seemed like fun. There was only one problem though. The Rhine family had an old man living in their summer house. His name was Pierce, and he had a very fierce dog; at least he acted very fierce! He was kept behind a high wire fence connected to an old shed.

Every day when we walked to school, that dog frightened us terribly with his fierce barking and growling. But Mother always reminded us to pray and remember the Bible verse which says: What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee –Psalm 56:3. Still, we hurried by as fast as our legs could take us.

Lori and I started out happily on our errand for Mother. We skipped along, watching the dust swirl beneath our feet on that warm summer morning. Everything seemed unusually quiet and still as we passed through the gully, over the rippling creek, and up the steep hill right before Neighbor Rhine’s place. There before us was the old shed, and on the other side was the high fence which kept in Pierce’s mean dog. My heart began to thump rapidly. ‘Maybe that bad dog hadn’t seen us yet,’ I thought gratefully as I whispered once more to myself, ‘I will trust and not be afraid.’

Suddenly, the air was shattered by the ferocious barking of that mean dog as he sprang around the corner of the old shed! Lori and I froze in our tracks! As that angry dog raced toward us, Lori screamed. The next moment, I realized she had fallen down and was sitting in the middle of the dirt road, with her hands behind her on the hard packed gravel, feet and legs in the air, kicking and kicking, spinning around and around as that angry dog circled her, jumping in at her and nipping at her feet and legs! I was so scared. I just stood frozen to the spot. I don’t remember if I screamed, or if I prayed. But suddenly there was a shout! It was Pierce, with a whip in his hand. He came running around the shed and out on the road. He whipped and whipped that dog and finally got him away from Lori and back inside the fence where he belonged, as Lori and I stood there, trembling, and crying with relief.”

“Wow!” exclaimed Sharon. “That was really scary, wasn’t it?”

“Did Pierce need to get rid of his dog?” asked Micah.

“Yes, Sharon, it was very scary,” answered Grandma. “And no, Micah, Pierce did not get rid of his dog. We children needed to keep trusting the good Lord to keep us safe every day.”

“I don’t remember what happened after Pierce got the dog away that day, or if we ever got Mother’s sugar, but I will never forget what happened that day.

It was a miracle that Lori and I were not injured. There is a verse in Psalms which says: Save me from the lion’s mouth… –Psalm 22:21. How thankful we were to be delivered from the dog’s mouth! I like to think that the Lord’s angel had his sword drawn in front of that dog’s mouth every time he leaped at my dear sister.”

L'angelo del SIGNORE si accampa intorno a quelli che lo temono e li libera –Salmo 34:7.

«Raccontaci una storia, nonna», supplicarono due bambini ansiosi mentre si stringevano intorno alla sua poltrona a dondolo.

«Oh, oh, a voi bambini piacciono le storie, vero?» rispose la nonna, con un luccichio negli occhi. «Va bene, vi racconterò di una volta in cui avevo circa otto anni, e mia sorella Lori ne aveva nove.

Abitavamo in una vecchia fattoria, lungo un brevissimo sentiero su una strada sterrata. Una mattina, mamma ci chiamò dal gioco e disse che era rimasta senza zucchero. Ci chiese di andare a piedi dalla signora Brightbill per vedere se aveva dello zucchero da prestare. Vedete, da bambina non avevamo il telefono, quindi non poteva chiamare la vicina per chiederle. I vicini spesso si scambiavano cose perché nemmeno andavamo spesso a fare la spesa al negozio. Così mia madre ci diede un contenitore, e partimmo per la nostra lunga camminata mentre lei ci chiamava dietro e ci ricordava di non trattenersi lungo la strada.»

«Quanto distava dai Brightbill?» chiese Sharon.

«Oh, era circa mezzo miglio dal nostro vicino più vicino, la fattoria dei Rhine, e poi circa un altro quarto di miglio fino ai Brightbill», rispose la nonna.

«Oh, è lontano. Mamma non ci lascia proprio camminare sulla strada», aggiunse Micah.

«Credo tu abbia ragione», concordò la nonna. «E spero che non camminerete mai sulla strada senza il permesso dei vostri genitori. Ma le cose erano molto diverse quando ero una bambina. Andavamo anche a scuola ogni giorno a piedi, che era molto più distante della fattoria dei Brightbill. Quindi la piccola commissione che stavamo svolgendo quella mattina per mamma ci sembrava divertente. C'era però un problema. La famiglia Rhine aveva un vecchio che viveva nella loro casa estiva. Si chiamava Pierce, e aveva un cane molto feroce; almeno si comportava in modo molto minaccioso! Era tenuto dietro una recinzione alta di filo collegata a un vecchio capanno.

Ogni giorno, quando andavamo a scuola, quel cane ci spaventava terribilmente con il suo abbaiare e ringhiare feroce. Ma mamma ci ricordava sempre di pregare e ricordare il verso della Bibbia che dice: Quando ho paura, in te confiderò –Salmo 56:3. Eppure noi passavamo di lì il più in fretta possibile.

Lori ed io partimmo allegre per la commissione di mamma. Saltellavamo, osservando la polvere sollevarsi sotto i nostri piedi in quella calda mattina d'estate. Tutto sembrava insolitamente calmo e tranquillo mentre attraversavamo il solco, oltrepassavamo il ruscello scintillante e salivamo il ripido colle proprio prima della casa del vicino Rhine. Là davanti a noi c'era il vecchio capanno, e dall'altro lato la recinzione alta che teneva dentro il cane cattivo di Pierce. Il mio cuore cominciò a battere forte. «Forse quel brutto cane non ci ha ancora visto», pensai riconoscente mentre sussurravo ancora a me stessa, «confiderò e non avrò paura.»

All'improvviso l'aria fu squarciata dal furore dell'abbaiare di quel cane cattivo mentre balzò oltre l'angolo del vecchio capanno! Lori ed io ci bloccammo! Quando quel cane furioso ci si avventò contro, Lori urlò. Un istante dopo, mi accorsi che era caduta e stava seduta in mezzo alla strada sterrata, con le mani dietro di sé sulla ghiaia compatta, piedi e gambe in aria, che calciavano e calciavano, girando su sé stessa mentre quel cane arrabbiato le girava intorno, saltando su di lei e mordicchiandole piedi e gambe! Ero così spaventata. Rimasi semplicemente paralizzata sul posto. Non ricordo se ho urlato, o se ho pregato. Ma all'improvviso ci fu un grido! Era Pierce, con una frusta in mano. Corse fuori dal capanno e sulla strada. Frustò e frustò quel cane e alla fine lo allontanò da Lori e lo rimise dentro la recinzione dove doveva stare, mentre Lori ed io restavamo lì, tremanti e piangendo di sollievo.»

«Wow!» esclamò Sharon. «È stato davvero spaventoso, vero?»

«Pierce ha dovuto liberarsi del suo cane?» chiese Micah.

«Sì, Sharon, è stato molto spaventoso», rispose la nonna. «E no, Micah, Pierce non si è liberato del suo cane. Noi bambini dovevamo continuare a confidare nel buon Signore affinché ci tenesse al sicuro ogni giorno.»

«Non ricordo cosa accadde dopo che Pierce allontanò il cane quel giorno, o se alla fine trovammo lo zucchero per mamma, ma non dimenticherò mai ciò che successe quel giorno.

Fu un miracolo che Lori ed io non rimanemmo ferite. C'è un verso nei Salmi che dice: Salvami dalla bocca del leone… –Salmo 22:21. Quanto fummo grati di essere state liberate dalla bocca del cane! Mi piace pensare che l'angelo del Signore avesse la sua spada sguainata davanti alla bocca di quel cane ogni volta che esso si precipitava sulla mia cara sorellina.»

L'ange de l'Éternel campe autour de ceux qui le craignent, et il les délivre – Psaume 34:7.

« Raconte-nous une histoire, Grand-mère, » supplièrent deux enfants impatients en se pressant autour de son fauteuil à bascule.

« Oh là là, vous aimez entendre des histoires, n'est-ce pas ? » répondit Grand-mère, avec une étincelle dans les yeux. « Très bien, je vais vous raconter une fois où j'avais environ huit ans, et ma sœur Lori en avait neuf.

Nous vivions dans une vieille ferme, au bout d'un petit chemin sur une route de terre. Un matin, Maman nous appela pour nous faire rentrer de nos jeux et dit qu'elle n'avait plus de sucre. Elle nous demanda d'aller chez Mme Brightbill voir si elle pouvait nous dépanner d'un peu de sucre. Vous voyez, nous n'avions pas de téléphone quand j'étais petite, donc elle ne pouvait pas appeler la voisine pour lui demander. Les voisins se rendaient souvent service, car nous n'allions pas faire des courses au magasin très souvent non plus. Alors, Maman nous donna un récipient, et nous nous mîmes en route pour notre longue promenade pendant que Maman nous rappelait de ne pas traîner en chemin. »

« À quelle distance étaient les Brightbill ? » demanda Sharon.

« Oh, c'était à environ un demi-mile jusqu'à notre voisin le plus proche, chez les Rhine, puis encore environ un quart de mile jusqu'aux Brightbill, » répondit Grand-mère.

« Oh, c'est loin. Maman ne nous laisse pas du tout marcher sur la route, » ajouta Micah.

« Je suis sûre que vous avez raison, » acquiesça Grand-mère. « Et j'espère que vous ne marcherez jamais sur la route sans la permission de vos parents. Mais les choses étaient bien différentes quand j'étais petite. Nous allions aussi à l'école à pied tous les jours, ce qui était bien plus loin que la ferme des Brightbill. Donc, la petite commission que nous faisions ce matin-là pour Maman semblait amusante. Il y avait toutefois un seul problème. La famille Rhine avait un vieil homme qui vivait dans leur maison d'été. Il s'appelait Pierce, et il avait un chien très féroce ; du moins il faisait très féroce ! Il était gardé derrière une haute clôture en fil de fer reliée à un vieux hangar.

Tous les jours, quand nous allions à l'école, ce chien nous effrayait terriblement avec ses aboiements féroces et ses grognements. Mais Maman nous rappelait toujours de prier et de nous souvenir du verset biblique qui dit : Quand je suis dans la crainte, je cherche en toi ma confiance – Psaume 56:3. Pourtant, nous passions en courant aussi vite que nos jambes pouvaient nous porter.

Lori et moi partîmes joyeuses pour notre commission pour Maman. Nous sautillions, regardant la poussière tourbillonner sous nos pieds par cette chaude matinée d'été. Tout semblait étrangement calme et immobile quand nous passâmes par le ravin, traversâmes le ruisseau qui murmurait et gravîmes la côte raide juste avant la maison du voisin Rhine. Là devant nous se trouvait le vieux hangar, et de l'autre côté la haute clôture qui retenait le méchant chien de Pierce. Mon cœur se mit à battre rapidement. « Peut-être que ce méchant chien ne nous a pas encore vus, » pensai-je avec reconnaissance en me chuchotant encore une fois, « je mettrai ma confiance et je ne craindrai pas. »

Soudain, l'air fut déchiré par les aboiements furieux de ce chien méchant lorsqu'il bondit autour du coin du vieux hangar ! Lori et moi nous figeâmes sur place ! Alors que ce chien en colère fonçait vers nous, Lori poussa un cri. L'instant d'après, je vis qu'elle était tombée et était assise au milieu de la route de terre, les mains posées derrière elle sur le gravier dur, pieds et jambes en l'air, donnant des coups de pied et tournoyant tandis que ce chien furieux tournait autour d'elle, se jetant sur elle et mordillant ses pieds et ses jambes ! J'avais si peur. Je restai là, pétrifiée. Je ne me souviens plus si j'ai crié, ou si j'ai prié. Mais soudain il y eut un cri ! C'était Pierce, avec un fouet à la main. Il arriva en courant autour du hangar et sur la route. Il fouetta et fouetta ce chien et finit par l'éloigner de Lori et le ramener à l'intérieur de la clôture où il devait être, tandis que Lori et moi restions là, tremblantes et pleines de soulagement. »

« Oh là là ! » s'exclama Sharon. « C'était vraiment effrayant, n'est-ce pas ? »

« Est-ce que Pierce a dû se débarrasser de son chien ? » demanda Micah.

« Oui, Sharon, c'était très effrayant, » répondit Grand-mère. « Et non, Micah, Pierce ne s'est pas débarrassé de son chien. Nous, les enfants, devions continuer à faire confiance au bon Seigneur pour nous garder chaque jour en sécurité. »

« Je ne me souviens plus de ce qui arriva après que Pierce eut éloigné le chien ce jour-là, ni si nous avons jamais ramené le sucre à Maman, mais je n'oublierai jamais ce qui arriva ce jour-là.

C'était un miracle que Lori et moi ne fûmes pas blessées. Il y a un verset dans les Psaumes qui dit : Délivre-moi de la gueule du lion… – Psaume 22:21. Comme nous fûmes reconnaissantes d'être délivrées de la bouche du chien ! J'aime penser que l'ange du Seigneur tenait son épée sortie devant la gueule de ce chien chaque fois qu'il bondissait sur ma chère sœur. »

Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted?… –Matthew 5:13.

One might wonder as to why the Anabaptists, the early church fathers, church history writers, and especially the progenitor (originator or author) of our beliefs, Christ Himself, effected such a vehement and absolute approach to a separated church and state. Why did they unanimously preach, write, and otherwise caution against political involvement of any kind by Christians? Perhaps this is best answered by looking at the results of Christians ignoring these sincere warnings, casting off their Godly allegiance, and pledging themselves to a flawed and ultimately futile earthly kingdom.

The Mennonites of Germany are a particularly intriguing and cautionary episode of Christian and Anabaptist histories—not only because of their relative proximity to our time—but also because of their almost wholesale devotion to a worldly leader and agenda. What led them to such an un-Christ-like position? A true understanding of their story must begin, naturally, with their beginnings.

The Mennonites of 20th century Germany were descended from the first Anabaptist groups, but unlike our ancestors, they stayed in the Old World instead of emigrating to the New World. There, a number of factors led them to a unique position within world events, a position that would test their mettle on a global stage.

The beginnings of the 20th century brought about the first World War, which ended with the defeat of Germany and its allies. The resulting peace treaties were structured to humiliate and crush Germany, saddling it with an almost unpayable war debt, and restricting its rights to build a military. The German people, unsurprisingly, resented this insult being added to the injury of having lost the War. Their resentment festered, and soon manifested itself in nationalistic movements, the most notable of which was the National Socialist German Workers Party (or the Nazi Party). The party was founded in 1919, and Hitler was amongst its first members. He quickly assumed party leadership, attracting followers with his “us vs. them” rhetoric and strong leadership.

Party growth was small in the decade following its founding. During this time, Hitler continued to shape the Nazis according to his wishes. Hatred for most non-German (Aryan) groups became a central party theme, along with a violent distaste for communism. However, the party was not large enough to be anything but a fringe voice, representing only a small portion of German voters.

Insignificance did not last, however. The Great Depression brought the catalyst for the Nazi’s rise to power. When the global market crashed, over 2 million Germans lost their jobs. Unemployed, they rallied around the charismatic leadership that promised to give them jobs, give them power, to “Make Germany great again”. Moving quickly, Hitler added legions to his followers.

The thousands of new Nazi Party members enabled the Nazi Party to seriously contest many local elections, and in Germany’s Parliament, they were able to control enough votes to sway policy making. In the long run, their political might handed Hitler the office of prime minister. Having secured that position, he went on to overthrow the German government, establishing himself and his party as the undisputed rulers of Germany.

Why did such a man, and such a movement, attract the attention and adoration of a church that professed much of what we do? Loving our enemies, separation from the world, and nonresistance did not seem to combine with the message of the Nazis. The answer, like most backsliding churches, is best portrayed as happening in small steps and over time.

In 1929, the Mennonites came under the eye of Germany and its rapidly expanding Nazi Party. 13,000 Russian Mennonite refugees descended on Moscow, seeking an exit from the Communist-run country. The Nazis seized the situation, using the Mennonites as supposed evidence that Aryans (peoples of German lineage, such as the Mennonites) were being unjustly used by the rest of the world. This image was pushed by state propaganda departments, who circulated writings, pamphlets, and even two immensely popular movies, depicting the Mennonites as strong, red-blooded Germans valiantly striving against the unjust oppression of the Russian Communists. These efforts afforded the refugees national attention, which subsequently led to them being admitted into Germany.

While many Mennonites entered Germany, as refugees and otherwise, there were also thriving, established communities that were given the same patriotic make-over by the Nazi propogandists. Unfortunately, these churches welcomed the Nazi attention, going so far as to send Hitler a letter thanking him for being the “savior of the German peoples” and pledging their support to his government. It is of note that Hitler, a man quite busy running an emerging world power, personally responded to this letter with a memo thanking the churches for their support and expressing a desire for further cooperation to the benefit of both the Nazis and the Mennonites. The church further weakened under these seemingly beneficial relations.

A particularly shocking case of Mennonite political involvement came from the churches in or around Danzig. Danzig and the surrounding countryside had long been a part of the German Empire, until the end of World War I, when the region was separated from Germany, essentially becoming a buffer zone between Germany and Poland. In 1939, Hitler would make one of his first moves on Europe by annexing Danzig, where the Nazis had been building party influence for most of the 1930’s. The Mennonites of the area, having been German only a generation before, welcomed their new part in the Germany of the future, becoming involved in almost every level of the Nazi Party. Otto Andres became the second-highest ranked Nazi of the Danzig area, and scores of the 6,000 believers in the surrounding congregations joined various Nazi organizations. The men often took part in the paramilitary SA and SS, while their wives and daughters took part in corresponding women’s groups. Churches became saturated with active Nazis, even going so far as to accept them into church leadership. At one point, five of the seven local churches were led by active party members.

World War II was the final step in the Mennonites’ integration with the Nazis. The German concentration camp of Stutthof supplied slave labor to numerous Mennonite businesses. Mennonite churches organized war efforts, including recruiting their young men to serve in the German army. In a particularly twisted case, a Mennonite doctor, Johan Klassen, was personally responsible for the deaths of more than one hundred disabled children.

Perhaps the most concerning episode in this dismal tale of backsliding comes after the war. Mennonite leadership, recognizing to some extent the terrible depths to which they had fallen, and noting the justice that was to come through the Nuremburg trials, effectively shrugged the blame from off their shoulders. Appealing to their Mennonite brothers across the ocean, they convinced them of their innocence, twisting their involvement in the Nazi regime to make themselves appear the victims. American Mennonites helped these now-refugees in many ways, providing all manner of assistance, and ultimately keeping most of them from facing possible prison time or death sentences. The surviving German churches eventually disintegrated or emigrated to the Americas.

If a group who originally held beliefs identical to our own could stray to the point of child murder and slave labor, then the question must be asked: “Are we seeing their folly for what it was?” Why did the churches of Danzig accept the advances of what, in retrospect, was a clearly un-biblical, un-Christlike movement?

The origin for their downfall was surprisingly simple. The Mennonites of Germany forgot who their true Ruler was. No earthly kingdom at war tolerates an allegiance to the enemy, and neither does the Kingdom of Heaven. The pride in their earthly kingdom, the pursuit of prestige and power, all led to a foreseeable end. Their salt had lost its savor, and they were cast out and trodden underfoot. This is a cautionary tale of the dangers of an unequal yoking of the church with the world.

你们是世上的盐；若盐失了味，可用什么叫它再咸呢？… ——马太福音 5:13。

人们可能会疑惑，为何再洗礼派（安那巴普蒂斯特）、早期教父、教会历史作者，尤其是我们信仰的发起者（起源者或著者）——基督本人，会对教会与国家分离采取如此严厉而绝对的立场。为何他们一致向基督徒宣讲、写作并极力警戒任何形式的政治参与？也许最好的回答是观察基督徒忽视这些诚挚警告、背弃他们对上帝的效忠并宣誓效忠于一个有缺陷且终将徒劳的世俗国度后的结果。

德国的门诺派在基督教与再洗礼派史上是一个尤其有趣且警示性的篇章——不仅因为他们与我们的时代相对接近——也因为他们几乎完全投身于世俗领袖与世俗议程。是什么导致他们处于这种不像基督的立场？要真正理解他们的故事，自然必须从他们的开端说起。

20 世纪的德国门诺派源自最早的再洗礼派群体，但与我们的祖先不同，他们留在旧大陆而未移民新大陆。在那里，若干因素使他们在世界事件中处于一种独特的地位，这个地位将在全球舞台上考验他们的品格。

20 世纪初的开端带来了第一次世界大战，战争以德国及其盟国的失败告终。随之而来的和约旨在羞辱并压垮德国，使其背负几乎无法偿还的战争赔款，并限制其组建军事的权利。德国人民毫不奇怪地对这在战败之上又加一层侮辱心怀怨恨。他们的怨恨发酵，不久便在民族主义运动中显现出来，其中最显著者便是国家社会主义德国工人党（或称纳粹党）。该党成立于 1919 年，希特勒是其最早的一批成员之一。他很快掌握了党的领导，以“我们与他们”的言辞和强势的领导力吸引追随者。

在成立后的十年里，党的发展并不大。在此期间，希特勒继续按照他的意愿塑造纳粹。对大多数非德国（雅利安）族群的仇恨成为党的核心主题之一，同时对共产主义抱有暴力般的厌恶。然而，该党当时规模不大，只是边缘声音，仅代表少数德国选民。

然而，这种无足轻重并未持续下去。大萧条成为了纳粹崛起的催化剂。全球市场崩溃时，超过两百万德国人失业。失业的人们纷纷投向那位承诺给他们工作、给他们权力、要“使德国再次伟大”的魅力型领袖。希特勒迅速吸纳了大批追随者。

成千上万的新纳粹党成员使纳粹党得以在许多地方选举中与之抗衡，并在德国议会中控制足够的选票来左右政策制定。从长远看，他们的政治力量将希特勒推上了总理之位。取得该职位后，他进一步推翻德国政府，使自己和其党派确立为德国的无可争议的统治者。

为何这样的人与运动会吸引一个宣称与我们信条相近的教会的注意与崇拜？爱仇敌、与世俗分离、以非抵抗为行事原则，这些与纳粹的信息似乎并不相符。答案如同大多数跌落的教会，最好被描述为逐步发生并在时间中累积。

1929 年，门诺派进入了德国与迅速扩张的纳粹党的视野。1.3 万名俄罗斯门诺派难民蜂拥到莫斯科，寻求从共产政权统治的国家逃出。纳粹利用这一局面，将门诺派作为所谓证据，宣称雅利安人（如门诺派等德裔血统民族）正被世界其他地方不公地对待。国家宣传部门推动这一形象，印发文章、小册子，甚至制作了两部极为流行的电影，将门诺派描绘为血气方刚的德国人，英勇地反抗俄国共产主义者的不公压迫。这些努力为难民带来了全国关注，随后使他们得以进入德国。

许多门诺派作为难民进入德国的同时，也有一些繁荣、已有根基的群体受到了纳粹宣传者相同的爱国改造。不幸的是，这些教会欢迎纳粹的关注，甚至给希特勒写信，感谢他作为“德意志民族的救主”，并宣誓支持他的政府。值得注意的是，希特勒——一位忙于经营新兴世界强权的人——亲自回信致谢这些教会的支持，并表示希望进一步合作，以利于纳粹与门诺派双方。教会在这些看似有利的关系中进一步软弱下来。

一个尤其令人震惊的门诺派政治介入案例出自但泽或其周边地区。但泽及其周围乡村很久以前一直是德意志帝国的一部分，直到第一次世界大战结束时，该地区被从德国分离，实际上成为德国与波兰之间的缓冲区。1939 年，希特勒对欧洲发起的第一步之一就是吞并但泽，纳粹在 1930 年代大部分时间里一直在该地建立党的影响力。该地区的门诺派仅在一代之前还是德国人，他们欢迎自己在未来德国中扮演的新角色，几乎参与了纳粹党各个层面。奥托·安德烈斯成为但泽地区纳粹的第二号人物，而周边教会约六千名信徒中有大量加入了各类纳粹组织。男子常参与冲锋队（SA）和党卫队（SS）等准军事组织，女子和女儿则参加相应的妇女团体。教会被积极的纳粹分子所充斥，甚至接受他们进入教会领导层。曾有一段时间，七个地方教会中有五个由现任党成员领导。

第二次世界大战是门诺派与纳粹整合的最后一步。德国的斯图托夫集中营为众多门诺派企业提供了奴工劳力。门诺派教会组织战争努力，包括招募他们的年轻人服役于德军。在一个尤为扭曲的案件中，一位门诺派医生约翰·克拉森对一百多名残障儿童的死亡负有个人责任。

在这段堕落的阴郁故事中，也许最令人不安的篇章发生在战后。门诺派的领导层在某种程度上认识到了他们堕落的深度，并注意到纽伦堡审判将带来的正义，但他们实际上却将责任从自己肩上耸开。他们向海外的门诺弟兄诉说自己的清白，歪曲他们在纳粹政权中的牵连，使自己看起来像是受害者。美洲的门诺派在许多方面帮助了这些如今成了难民的人，提供了各种援助，并最终使他们中的大多数免于面对可能的监禁或死刑。幸存的德国教会最终解体或移民到美洲。

如果一个最初持有与我们完全相同信仰的群体能堕落到杀害儿童与使用奴工的程度，那么必须提出问题：“我们是否能看清他们的愚昧本来面目？”为什么但泽的教会会接受这样一个事后看来明显不合圣经、不像基督的运动的拉拢？

他们败落的根源出乎意料地简单。德国的门诺派忘记了他们真正的君王是谁。任何正与敌人结盟的属世王国在战争中都不会容忍对敌人的效忠，天国也不例外。他们对属世国度的骄傲、对声望与权力的追求，所有这些都导致了可预见的结局。他们的盐失了味，便被人丢在外面践踏。这是一个关于教会与世界不当缔结不等之约的危险的警示故事。

Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created –Revelation 4:11.

This hymn, often called the “National Anthem of Christendom,” is perhaps one of the greatest of hymns of all time. It was written by Edward Perronet, first appearing in the November 1779 issue of Gospel Magazine. It was edited by Augustus Toplady, who is also the author of another well-known hymn, “Rock of Ages”. The text of this hymn, All Hail the Power of Jesus Name, has been translated into almost every language where Christianity is known. Wherever it is sung, it communicates to the spiritual needs of human hearts. One writer has said, “So long as there are Christians on earth, it will continue to be sung; and after that, in heaven.”

Edward Perronet was born at Sundridge, Kent, England, in 1726. He was a descendant of a distinguished French Huguenot family who had fled to Switzerland and later to England because of the religious persecution in France. Edward’s father, a pastor in the State Church of England, was strongly sympathetic with the evangelical movement spearheaded by the Wesleys and George Whitefield. Edward, too, like his father, became a minister in the Anglican Church but was always critical of its ways. Once he wrote, “I was born and I am likely to die in the tottering communion of the Church of England, but I despise her nonsense.” Soon, however, he broke from the Church and threw himself strenuously into the evangelistic endeavors of the Wesleys during the 1740s and 1750s.

Charles Wesley writes of Edward Perronet’s boldness in preaching. At one time he and Perronet were beset in a house by a mob of rough revilers, whom Perronet opposed courageously, while they abused him and threw dirt on him. It was during this time that the Wesleys and their followers suffered much persecution and even violence from those who disagreed with their ministry. Concerning these experiences, Wesley made the following notation in his diary: “From Rockdale we went to Bolton, and soon found that the Rockdale lions were lambs in comparison with those of Bolton.” Edward Perronet was thrown down and rolled in mud and mire. Stones were hurled and windows broken.

Another interesting account is given regarding the relationship between the Wesleys and Perronet. John Wesley wanted to hear Perronet preach, and he, being 18 years younger than John had always refused to preach in the older churchman’s presence. So, one day Wesley seeing Edward in the congregation announced that he would preach at the next service. Desiring to avoid a public conflict with Wesley, Perronet mounted the pulpit the next morning, but quickly explained that he had never consented to preach. “However,” he added, “I shall deliver the greatest sermon that has ever been preached on earth.” He then read the Sermon on the Mount and sat down without comment.

After eight years of co-operation with the Wesleys, Perronet’s strong-mindedness and free spirit caused a division between them, as he disagreed with some of their regulations. They continued, however, to esteem and love each other.

The last years of Perronet were spent at Canterbury, where he was pastor of an independent church, and where he died in 1792, at the age of sixty-six. His last words have also become a classic: “Glory to God in the height of His divinity! Glory to God in the depth of His humanity! Glory to God in His all-sufficiency! Into His hands I commend my spirit.”

Though Perronet wrote many other hymns and forms of poetry, none of them, have attained fame except the immortal “All Hail the Power of Jesus Name.” The success of this text has, no doubt, been furthered by three fine tunes. “Coronation,” composed by Oliver Holden, a Massachusetts carpenter, self-taught musician, and respected singing-school teacher, is most widely used in America. “Miles Lane” composed by William Shrubsole, Perronet’s personal friend, is the most popular in Great Britain. While the festive “Diadem” tune, composed in 1838 for this text by James Ellor, an English layman, is frequently used as a choir number. This hymn was originally written having the title, “On the Resurrection,” and there were eight stanzas, as follows:

All hail the power of Jesus’ name,
Let angels prostrate fall
Bring forth the royal diadem,
To crown Him Lord of all!

Let high born seraphs tune the lyre,
And, as they tune it, fall
Before His face who tunes their choir,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Crown Him, ye morning stars of light,
Who fixed this floating ball,
Now hail the Strength of Israel’s might,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Crown Him, ye martyrs of your God,
Who from His altar call;
Extol the stem of Jesse’s rod,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Ye seed of Israel’s chosen race,
Ye ransomed of the fall,
Hail Him who saves you by His grace
And crown Him Lord of all!

Hail Him, ye heirs of David’s line,
Whom David Lord did call.
The God incarnate, Man divine,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Sinners, whose love can ne’er forget
The wormwood and the gall,
Go spread your trophies at His feet,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Let every tribe and every tongue
That bound creation’s call
Now shout in universal song,
The crowned Lord of all!

As it now stands in our hymnbooks, the hymn is shortened and changed, and one stanza has been added by the famous hymn collector, Rev. John Rippon, in 1787.

Oh, that with yonder sacred throng
We at His feet may fall;
We’ll join the everlasting song,
And crown Him Lord of all.

As we wrap up this amazing story of the life of Edward Perronet and the others who have had their part in bringing this immortal hymn to us, let’s take a look in closing at the effect this hymn has had on heathens who knew nothing about Jesus. The most famous story connected with Perronet’s great hymn is told of the missionary to India, Rev. E.P. Scott. One day he saw on the street a man of so strange an appearance that he inquired about him and learned that he belonged to a wild mountain tribe among whom Christ had never been preached. Mr. Scott prayed over the matter and decided to visit that tribe. As soon as he reached their mountain home, he fell in among a savage band of murderous tribesmen who were on a war expedition, and who were closing in on him with their spears. They seized him and pointed their spears at his heart. At once the missionary drew out the violin that he always carried with him and began to play and sing in the native language, “All hail the power of Jesus’ name!” He closed his eyes, expecting death at any minute. When he reached the fourth stanza, and nothing had happened, he opened his eyes, and was amazed to see that the spears had fallen from the hands of the savages, and big tears were in their eyes! They invited Mr. Scott to their homes, and he spent the remaining years of his life preaching and ministering God’s love and redemption to these people. God in His providence used a simple hymn as a means of introducing the gospel to a group of needy pagans.

Du er verdig, Herre, til å få ære, ære og makt; for du skapte alle ting, og ved din vilje er de og ble de skapt – Åpenbaringen 4:11.

Denne salmen, ofte kalt «Kristendommens nasjonalsang», er kanskje en av de største salmene gjennom tidene. Den ble skrevet av Edward Perronet og sto først i Gospel Magazine i november 1779. Den ble redigert av Augustus Toplady, som også er forfatteren av en annen velkjent salme, «Rock of Ages». Teksten til denne salmen, All Hail the Power of Jesus Name, er blitt oversatt til nesten alle språk hvor kristendommen er kjent. Hvor enn den synges, treffer den menneskehjertets åndelige behov. En forfatter har sagt: «Så lenge det finnes kristne på jorden, vil den fortsette å bli sunget; og etter det, i himmelen.»

Edward Perronet ble født i Sundridge, Kent, England, i 1726. Han stammet fra en fremtredende fransk hugenottfamilie som hadde flyktet til Sveits og senere til England på grunn av den religiøse forfølgelsen i Frankrike. Edwards far, en prest i den engelske statskirken, hadde sterk sympati for den evangeliske bevegelsen ledet av Wesley-brødrene og George Whitefield. Edward ble, lik sin far, også prest i den anglikanske kirken, men var alltid kritisk til dens væremåte. En gang skrev han: «Jeg ble født og jeg kommer trolig til å dø i den vaklende kommunionen i den engelske kirke, men jeg forakter hennes tåpeligheter.» Snart brøt han imidlertid med kirken og engasjerte seg energisk i Wesley-brødrenes evangeliske arbeid på 1740- og 1750-tallet.

Charles Wesley skriver om Edward Perronets frimodighet i forkynnelsen. En gang ble han og Perronet beleiret i et hus av en mobb med grove skjennere, som Perronet møtte med mot mens de fornærmet ham og kastet jord på ham. Det var i denne tiden at Wesley-brødrene og deres tilhengere ble utsatt for mye forfølgelse og til og med vold fra dem som var uenige i deres tjeneste. Om disse erfaringene noterte Wesley i sin dagbok: «Fra Rockdale dro vi til Bolton, og snart fant vi at Rockdale-løvene var lammer sammenlignet med dem i Bolton.» Edward Perronet ble kastet ned og rullet i søle og gjørme. Steiner ble kastet og vinduer knust.

En annen interessant beretning gjelder forholdet mellom Wesley-brødrene og Perronet. John Wesley ønsket å høre Perronet forkynne, og Perronet, som var 18 år yngre enn John, hadde alltid nektet å forkynne i den eldre kirkemannens nærvær. Så en dag, da Wesley så Edward i menigheten, annonserte han at han ville preke ved neste samling. For å unngå en offentlig konflikt med Wesley gikk Perronet opp i prekestolen neste morgen, men forklarte raskt at han aldri hadde samtykket til å preke. «Likevel,» la han til, «vil jeg holde den største prekenen som noen gang er holdt på jorden.» Han leste så Bergprekenen og satte seg ned uten kommentar.

Etter åtte år med samarbeid med Wesley-brødrene førte Perronets stahet og frie ånd til en splittelse mellom dem, ettersom han var uenig i noen av deres regler. De fortsatte imidlertid å holde av hverandre og elske hverandre.

De siste årene av Perronets liv ble tilbrakt i Canterbury, hvor han var pastor for en uavhengig menighet, og hvor han døde i 1792, i en alder av sekstiseks år. Hans siste ord har også blitt klassiske: «Ære være Gud i høyden for Hans guddommelighet! Ære være Gud i dybden for Hans menneskelighet! Ære være Gud i Hans alt-tilstrekkelighet! I Hans hender overgir jeg min ånd.»

Selv om Perronet skrev mange andre salmer og diktformer, har ingen av dem oppnådd berømmelse bortsett fra den udødelige «All Hail the Power of Jesus Name». Tekstens suksess har utvilsomt blitt fremmet av tre gode melodier. «Coronation», komponert av Oliver Holden, en snekker fra Massachusetts, selvlært musiker og respektert sangskolelærer, er mest brukt i Amerika. «Miles Lane», komponert av William Shrubsole, Perronets personlige venn, er mest populær i Storbritannia. Mens den festlige «Diadem»-melodien, komponert i 1838 til denne teksten av James Ellor, en engelsk lekperson, ofte brukes som korstykke. Denne salmen ble opprinnelig skrevet med tittelen «On the Resurrection», og den hadde åtte vers, som følger:

All hail the power of Jesus’ name,
Let angels prostrate fall
Bring forth the royal diadem,
To crown Him Lord of all!

Let high born seraphs tune the lyre,
And, as they tune it, fall
Before His face who tunes their choir,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Crown Him, ye morning stars of light,
Who fixed this floating ball,
Now hail the Strength of Israel’s might,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Crown Him, ye martyrs of your God,
Who from His altar call;
Extol the stem of Jesse’s rod,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Ye seed of Israel’s chosen race,
Ye ransomed of the fall,
Hail Him who saves you by His grace
And crown Him Lord of all!

Hail Him, ye heirs of David’s line,
Whom David Lord did call.
The God incarnate, Man divine,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Sinners, whose love can ne’er forget
The wormwood and the gall,
Go spread your trophies at His feet,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Let every tribe and every tongue
That bound creation’s call
Now shout in universal song,
The crowned Lord of all!

Som den nå står i våre salmebøker, er salmen forkortet og endret, og ett vers ble lagt til av den berømte salmesamleren, prest John Rippon, i 1787.

Oh, that with yonder sacred throng
We at His feet may fall;
We’ll join the everlasting song,
And crown Him Lord of all.

Når vi avrunder denne bemerkelsesverdige beretningen om livet til Edward Perronet og de andre som har hatt sin del i å bringe denne udødelige salmen til oss, la oss til slutt se på hvilken virkning denne salmen har hatt på hedninger som ikke kjente til Jesus. Den mest berømte historien knyttet til Perronets store salme fortelles om misjonæren til India, Rev. E. P. Scott. En dag så han i gaten en mann med så merkelig utseende at han spurte om ham og fikk vite at han tilhørte en vill fjellstamme hvor Kristus aldri var blitt forkynt. Mr. Scott ba over saken og besluttet å besøke stammen. Så snart han nådde deres fjellhjem, falt han blant en vill bande av mordiske stammemenn som var på krigstokt, og som nærmet seg ham med spyd. De grep ham og pekte spyd mot hans hjerte. Med en gang tok misjonæren fram fiolinen han alltid bar med seg og begynte å spille og synge på morsmålet: «All hail the power of Jesus’ name!» Han lukket øynene, forventet å dø hvert øyeblikk. Da han nådde fjerde vers, og ingenting hadde skjedd, åpnet han øynene og ble forbauset over å se at spydene hadde falt fra de villmennenes hender, og store tårer fylte øynene deres! De inviterte Mr. Scott til hjemmene sine, og han tilbrakte de gjenværende årene av sitt liv med å forkynne og tjene Guds kjærlighet og forløsning for disse menneskene. Gud brukte i sin forsyn en enkel salme som et middel til å introdusere evangeliet for en gruppe trengende hedninger.

Greetings to each one in the worthy name of Jesus Christ, our Saviour, and our Redeemer.

This magazine issue may seem to be arriving more quickly on the heels of the last one. True. We are continuing to tighten up our schedule as we work towards getting each quarterly issue out in a more timely manner. Our ultimate goal is to have them arrive in your mailboxes in the months of March, June, September, and December of each year. Pray for us as we continue moving towards that schedule.

From time to time, we receive feedback—suggestions, concerns, and encouragement. We value this feedback. It is filed away and used by the board as we continually evaluate ways to make our magazine better. One final thought on this matter… when we receive feedback of encouragement regarding a specific article, it is helpful for us, and it is encouraging for our authors as we pass that along to them. We welcome your ongoing feedback.

As previously mentioned, we are including several new categories in this issue. One on Church History that is being written by two young brothers from our church. And one on Hymn Histories being written by one of our board members, a middle-aged married man, who is also from our church.

In “Moses in Midian”, we take a walk in Moses’ footsteps during the mid-section of his life. He was uprooted from his comfortable lifestyle in Egypt as an adopted son of royalty and was then sent by God into the desert to learn some much-needed lessons in further preparation towards becoming God’s servant. As we take a look at the life of Jonah, we glean glimpses of “The God Who Will Not Let Go”. Often a struggling believer loses sight of the Truth of God because they believe the lie that no one cares, yet the truth of the matter is this—the God of the Bible doesn’t just drop us, or turn His back on us, the instant that we take a wrong turn or a misstep. Let’s allow this article to help us to become rooted and grounded in the biblical Truth of Abba Father—a Father who cares for His children. We also have the second article in a continuing series on discipleship, as well as an article written by a middle-aged, spiritually-mature sister who shares her encouragement for sisters to evaluate what God thinks of their attire.

Church History and Should A Christian Vote

Finally, let’s consider the two short articles on church history. One of our goals for this issue is burdened with the awareness that the country in which we live (the U.S.) is approaching mid-term elections in November of this year and that there will be a strong push for many conservative Anabaptists to become involved in the voting process to ensure a proper outcome for the good of their perceived cause or goals.

In the natural world our “old man” has the tendency to think that we must “do something” if we expect things to go in a “right” direction. The spiritual Truth is this: The king’s heart is in the hand of the LORD, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will –Proverbs 21:1. If we think that, as believers, we will have a part in electing the “right” person in an election if we personally vote, let’s stop to consider what God Himself told Nebuchadnezzar. …That the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will –Daniel 4:31-32.

Throughout the history of the Anabaptist people there have been varied opinions on this matter, however, it is our wish to lift up the perspective that Jesus said …My kingdom is not of this world: if my kingdom were of this world, then would my servants fight … but now is my kingdom not from hence –John 18:36. When we understand and develop a personal world view that is founded on the two-kingdom principle, we realize that we must function as …strangers and pilgrims on the earth. [While we] …declare plainly that [we] seek a country …a better country, that is, an heavenly: wherefore God is not ashamed to be called [our] God: for he hath prepared for [us] a city –Hebrews 11:13-16. In all things involving political involvement, it is our encouragement that New Testament believers should obey the command to …come out from among them, and be ye separate… –2 Corinthians 6:17.

Let’s always cultivate a right attitude in our hearts so that our talk and actions reflect God’s view on the matter when He through the Apostle Paul tells us to: Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God … For he is the minister of God to thee… –Romans 13:1-4.

It is in consideration of these thoughts that we wrote the two articles detailing very different times in the history of the church and what it was like for Christians to relate to the government of their day. Let us seriously ponder whether we can do more good by getting involved in politics, especially in the voting process. Or whether God wants us to pray for our elected officials, to view them as His servants, and to speak about them with respect. Ultimately, we must trust God to bring about His will for the winding down of the “clock of time” as time speeds onward towards the end of time. God will do this through hardening the hearts of ungodly men in positions of power, just like Pharaoh of old, to accomplish His sovereign will for the world.

So, what is the solution when we struggle within our hearts about the direction of our country and its growing instability or when we experience so much pressure from our peers or the society around us to get involved to make a difference? The Apostle Paul gives us very clear direction when he says, I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men; For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty. 1 Timothy 2:1-2. The Christian’s secret power of influence lies in the power of prayer that is produced in the privacy of his or her closet. However, for this prayer to have power it must be produced out of a heart of faith—And Jesus said unto them … verily I say unto you, If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you –Matthew 17:20. Let us always remember that …The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much –James 5:16.

Until the next time, may God be with each one and grant you grace and peace as you walk faithfully according to His Word. Let us pray for each other as we go through the trying times in our world today.

Saludos a cada uno en el digno nombre de Jesucristo, nuestro Salvador y nuestro Redentor.

Esta edición de la revista puede parecer que llega más rápidamente tras la anterior. Es cierto. Seguimos ajustando nuestro calendario mientras trabajamos para publicar cada número trimestral de manera más oportuna. Nuestra meta final es que lleguen a sus buzones en los meses de marzo, junio, septiembre y diciembre de cada año. Oren por nosotros mientras seguimos avanzando hacia ese calendario.

De vez en cuando recibimos comentarios: sugerencias, inquietudes y estímulos. Valoramos estos comentarios. Se archivan y el consejo los utiliza mientras evaluamos continuamente maneras de mejorar la revista. Un último pensamiento sobre este asunto… cuando recibimos comentarios de ánimo respecto a un artículo específico, nos resulta útil y también es alentador para nuestros autores cuando se los transmitimos. Apreciamos sus comentarios continuos.

Como se mencionó anteriormente, estamos incluyendo varias categorías nuevas en este número. Una sobre Historia de la Iglesia que está siendo escrita por dos jóvenes hermanos de nuestra iglesia. Y otra sobre Historias de Himnos escrita por uno de los miembros de nuestro consejo, un hombre casado de mediana edad, que también es de nuestra iglesia.

En «Moisés en Madián», caminamos tras las huellas de Moisés durante la sección media de su vida. Fue arrancado de su estilo de vida cómodo en Egipto como hijo adoptivo de la realeza y luego enviado por Dios al desierto para aprender unas lecciones muy necesarias en preparación adicional para llegar a ser siervo de Dios. Al contemplar la vida de Jonás, vislumbramos a “El Dios que no suelta”. Con frecuencia un creyente en lucha pierde de vista la Verdad de Dios porque cree la mentira de que a nadie le importa; sin embargo, la verdad es esta: el Dios de la Biblia no nos abandona ni nos da la espalda en el instante en que tomamos un rumbo equivocado o damos un paso en falso. Permitamos que este artículo nos ayude a enraizarnos y afirmarnos en la Verdad bíblica del Abba Padre: un Padre que cuida de sus hijos. También tenemos el segundo artículo de una serie continua sobre el discipulado, así como un artículo escrito por una hermana de mediana edad y madura espiritualmente, que comparte su estímulo para que las hermanas evalúen lo que Dios piensa sobre su vestimenta.

Historia de la Iglesia y ¿Debería un cristiano votar?

Finalmente, consideremos los dos artículos breves sobre historia de la iglesia. Una de nuestras metas para este número está cargada con la conciencia de que el país en el que vivimos (EE. UU.) se aproxima a las elecciones de medio término en noviembre de este año y que habrá un fuerte impulso para que muchos anabaptistas conservadores se involucren en el proceso de votación para asegurar un resultado apropiado para el bien de su causa o de sus metas percibidas.

En el mundo natural nuestro “hombre viejo” tiene la tendencia a pensar que debemos “hacer algo” si esperamos que las cosas vayan en la dirección “correcta”. La verdad espiritual es esta: El corazón del rey está en la mano del SEÑOR, como los torrentes de las aguas; él lo inclina a donde quiere —Proverbios 21:1. Si pensamos que, como creyentes, tendremos parte en elegir a la persona “correcta” en una elección si votamos personalmente, detengámonos a considerar lo que Dios mismo le dijo a Nabucodonosor. …Que el Altísimo reina en el reino de los hombres, y lo da a quien él quiere —Daniel 4:31-32.

A lo largo de la historia del pueblo anabaptista ha habido opiniones variadas sobre este asunto; sin embargo, deseamos presentar la perspectiva de que Jesús dijo …Mi reino no es de este mundo; si mi reino fuera de este mundo, mis siervos pelearían… pero ahora mi reino no es de aquí —Juan 18:36. Cuando entendemos y desarrollamos una cosmovisión personal fundada en el principio de los dos reinos, nos damos cuenta de que debemos comportarnos como …extranjeros y peregrinos en la tierra. [Mientras] …declaramos públicamente que buscamos una patria… una mejor patria, es decir, celestial; por lo cual Dios no se avergüenza de ser llamado su Dios: porque les ha preparado una ciudad —Hebreos 11:13-16. En todo lo relacionado con la participación política, nuestro aliento es que los creyentes del Nuevo Testamento obedezcan el mandato de …salid de entre ellos, y apartaos… —2 Corintios 6:17.

Siempre cultivemos una actitud correcta en nuestros corazones para que nuestras palabras y acciones reflejen la perspectiva de Dios sobre el asunto cuando Él, por medio del apóstol Pablo, nos dice: Sométase toda persona a las autoridades superiores; porque no hay autoridad sino de parte de Dios, y las que hay, por Dios han sido establecidas… Porque el magistrado no es temor para las buenas obras, sino para las malas. ¿Quieres, pues, no temer la autoridad? Haz lo bueno, y tendrás alabanza de ella; porque es ministro de Dios para tu bien… —Romanos 13:1-4.

Es en consideración de estos pensamientos que escribimos los dos artículos que detallan épocas muy diferentes en la historia de la iglesia y cómo fue la relación de los cristianos con el gobierno de su tiempo. Meditemos seriamente si podemos hacer más bien involucrándonos en la política, especialmente en el proceso de votación. O si Dios quiere que oremos por nuestros funcionarios electos, que los veamos como sus siervos y que hablemos de ellos con respeto. En última instancia, debemos confiar en que Dios traerá a cabo su voluntad para el transcurso del “reloj del tiempo” conforme el tiempo avanza hacia el fin. Dios hará esto endureciendo los corazones de hombres impíos en posiciones de poder, tal como lo hizo con el Faraón de antaño, para cumplir su soberana voluntad para el mundo.

Entonces, ¿cuál es la solución cuando luchamos en nuestro interior por la dirección de nuestro país y su creciente inestabilidad o cuando sentimos tanta presión de nuestros pares o de la sociedad para involucrarnos y hacer la diferencia? El apóstol Pablo nos da una dirección muy clara cuando dice: Exhorto, pues, ante todo, que se hagan peticiones, oraciones, intercesiones y acciones de gracias, por todos los hombres; por los reyes y por todos los que están en eminencia, para que vivamos quieta y reposadamente en toda piedad y honestidad. —1 Timoteo 2:1-2. El poder secreto de influencia del cristiano yace en el poder de la oración que se produce en la privacidad de su aposento. Sin embargo, para que esta oración tenga poder debe nacer de un corazón de fe —Y Jesús les dijo… De cierto os digo, si tenéis fe como un grano de mostaza, diréis a este monte: Pásate de aquí allá, y se pasará; y nada os será imposible —Mateo 17:20. Recordemos siempre que …la oración eficaz y ferviente del justo puede mucho —Santiago 5:16.

Hasta la próxima, que Dios esté con cada uno y les conceda gracia y paz mientras caminan fielmente conforme a su Palabra. Oremos los unos por los otros mientras atravesamos los tiempos difíciles en nuestro mundo hoy.
