“Dr. Waldron,” disse la signora seduta di fronte a me. “Ultimamente sto lottando molto.”

“Dimmi cosa sta succedendo,” dissi.

“Non so come spiegarlo,” esitò… “Mi sento semplicemente stanca la maggior parte del tempo. Non riesco più a concentrarmi e non provo più piacere per la maggior parte delle cose che prima mi piacevano. Supero la giornata, ma non molto di più. Pensi che possa essere un problema alla tiroide o una carenza di qualche minerale o vitamina?”

“Potrebbe esserlo,” le dissi. “Possiamo sicuramente controllare queste cose, ma penso che ci sia qualcos’altro in gioco qui.”

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

Sono un medico di famiglia e probabilmente il trenta percento delle persone che vengono nel mio studio per vedermi presentano sintomi di depressione. Questo non significa che siano tutte in terapia farmacologica o che sentano di aver bisogno di aiuto specializzato, ma indica che questi sintomi sono diffusi nel nostro mondo.

Anche nelle cerchie cristiane, i sondaggi indicano che circa il 15 percento dei cristiani dichiara di essere stato diagnosticato con depressione in qualche momento della propria vita. Questo dato è del 25 percento inferiore rispetto alla società nel suo complesso, ma è comunque più alto di quanto vorremmo credere.

All’inizio, Dio creò il mondo e Adamo ed Eva. E Dio vide tutte le cose che aveva fatte, ed esse erano molto buone… –Genesi 1:31. Prima della Caduta, tutto era perfetto.

Non credo che sappiamo completamente cosa significasse questo. Ovviamente non esistevano malattie fisiche o afflizioni né per gli esseri umani né per la flora e la fauna dell’Eden. Più di questo, Adamo ed Eva non soffrivano di ansia o depressione. I loro ormoni non si sbilanciavano, non si stressavano (anche se in un giardino perfetto poteva comunque esserci qualche tensione), e non si sarebbero mai arrabbiati o turbati in alcun momento.

Tutto cambiò quando Adamo ed Eva peccarono. Lo vediamo nella tensione tra loro dopo che mangiarono il frutto, con Adamo che incolpa Eva ed Eva che incolpa il serpente. E l’uomo disse: La donna che tu mi hai dato per essere con me, ella mi ha dato dell’albero, ed io ne ho mangiato. E il SIGNORE Dio disse alla donna: Che cosa hai fatto? E la donna rispose: Il serpente mi ha ingannata, ed io ne ho mangiato –Genesi 3:12-13.

Nutrire una famiglia divenne improvvisamente un lavoro duro. Virus e batteri divennero patogeni e, a un certo punto, nelle prime famiglie, le persone avrebbero cominciato a lottare con problemi di salute emotiva e mentale.

Alla donna disse: Moltiplicherò grandemente il tuo dolore e il tuo concepimento; con dolore partorirai i figli; e il tuo desiderio sarà per tuo marito, ed egli dominerà su di te. E ad Adamo disse: Poiché hai ascoltato la voce di tua moglie e hai mangiato dell’albero di cui ti avevo comandato, dicendo: Non ne mangerai; maledetta sia la terra per causa tua; con dolore ne mangerai tutti i giorni della tua vita; spine e cardi ti produrrà; e mangerai l’erba del campo; col sudore del tuo volto mangerai il pane, fino a che tu ritorni alla terra; poiché da essa sei stato tratto: polvere sei e in polvere ritornerai –Genesi 3:16-19.

Vorrei esplorare che cosa sia la depressione secondo la definizione medica, alcune delle sue cause e poi discutere come possiamo affrontarla, sia nelle nostre vite sia nella vita di amici e familiari.

Diagnosticare la depressione

Come accennato prima, molte persone presentano alcuni sintomi di depressione. Possono sentirsi più affaticate, piangere facilmente o avere altri sintomi non abituali per loro. La maggior parte di queste persone non soffre però di una vera depressione clinica.

La maggior parte delle persone non presenta tutti questi sintomi, ma quando essi sono continuamente presenti senza attenuarsi per due settimane o più, specialmente se sono abbastanza intensi da ostacolare le responsabilità quotidiane normali o la capacità di ottenere un riposo adeguato, allora è il momento di intervenire.

È importante ricordare che esiste un ampio continuum riguardo alla depressione. Alcune persone hanno scoraggiamento lieve, altre provano profondo senso di tristezza, e alcune hanno una depressione di tale entità da essere a rischio di nuocere a sé stesse o agli altri.

Cause della depressione

Ci sono diversi esempi di persone nella Bibbia che sembrano aver mostrato sintomi compatibili con la depressione. Due di questi risaltano alla mia mente.

La prima è Noemi. Sappiamo che andò con suo marito e i suoi due figli a Moab a causa di una carestia che colpiva il sud d’Israele. Vi rimase per dieci anni e durante quel periodo suo marito e entrambi i suoi figli morirono.

Il libro di Rut ci racconta che quando tornò a Betlemme disse alla gente: …Non chiamatemi Noemi [dolce], chiamatemi Mara [amara]: perché l’Onnipotente mi ha fatto molto male. Io uscii piena, ma il SIGNORE mi ha ricondotta a casa vuota: perché dunque mi chiamate Noemi, vedendo che il SIGNORE ha testimoniato contro di me e l’Onnipotente mi ha afflitto? –Rut 1:20-21.

Non c’è modo di intervistare Noemi per scoprire tutto ciò che provava, ma questo sembra essere più che semplice dolore. Aveva perso tutte le cose a cui teneva e, a lei, sembrava che persino Dio si fosse rivoltato contro di lei.

Leggendo la storia di Rut, vediamo che le cose migliorarono per lei nel corso del libro—prevalentemente attraverso il ministero della nuora Rut, ma anche per il graduale ristabilirsi nella sua vita di cose di valore da parte di Dio, e per l’incoraggiamento degli altri nella bontà del Signore. Le donne dissero a Noemi: Benedetto sia il SIGNORE, il quale oggi non ti ha lasciata senza un parente, perché il suo nome sia famoso in Israele. E sarà per te un restauratore della tua vita, un nutrice della tua vecchiaia: perché la tua nuora, che ti ama e che è per te più di sette figli, gli ha dato alla luce un figlio. Allora Noemi prese il bambino e lo pose sul suo petto e ne fu nutrice –Rut 4:14-16.

Un altro che mi viene in mente è il profeta Geremia. Geremia fu chiamato quando era un giovane e svolse una carriera molto lunga parlando la Parola di Dio a una serie di re e ad altre persone che semplicemente non erano interessate a ciò che aveva da dire.

La vita di Geremia fu costantemente minacciata. In un’occasione fu gettato in una prigione piena di fango e fu salvato solo all’ultimo momento. Gerusalemme fu assediata tre volte diverse prima che i Babilonesi la radessero al suolo. Durante i suoi decenni di ministero, Geremia disse al popolo ciò che Dio chiedeva e il popolo lo ignorava costantemente.

Forse non sorprende che Geremia sia oggi conosciuto come il profeta piangente. Egli disse: Maledetta sia il giorno in cui nacqui: non sia benedetto il giorno in cui mia madre mi partorì. Maledetto sia l'uomo che annunziò a mio padre: È nato un figlio per te, rendendolo molto lieto. E sia quell'uomo come le città che il SIGNORE ha percosse, e non si è pentito: e che ascolti il grido al mattino e l'urlo a mezzogiorno … Perché uscii dal seno per vedere fatica e dolore, che i miei giorni siano consumati con vergogna? –Geremia 20:14-18.

È importante notare che in entrambi questi esempi biblici il peccato non è rivelato come il problema (o la ragione) che spinse queste persone nella depressione. Per Noemi fu probabilmente una miscela di isolamento dalla sua patria e della perdita di persone a lei care. Per Geremia fu lo stress costante di cercare di servire Dio in una nazione che non si preoccupava di Dio.

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

La depressione è sempre multifattoriale. Cioè, di solito c’è una miscela di fattori interni ed esterni che logorano una persona.

Entrano in gioco componenti genetiche e ormonali. Non c’è dubbio che alcuni individui e alcune famiglie siano più inclini alla depressione di altri. Molti medici e ricercatori pensano che cambiamenti nei geni che trasportano il neurotrasmettitore serotonina attraverso il cervello possano rendere alcune persone più suscettibili alla depressione rispetto ad altre.

Queste differenze nel patrimonio genetico possono aiutarci a capire perché alcune persone richiedono pochissimo stress per essere abbattute, mentre altre sembrano molto resilienti. Poiché non possiamo cambiare il nostro patrimonio genetico, non ha senso compiacersi se abbiamo una personalità più ottimista di qualcun altro. E, se riconosciamo di avere una maggiore tendenza alla depressione, non dobbiamo scoraggiarci per questo fatto. Se Dio ci ha creati in modo tale da tendere ad essere malinconici piuttosto che naturalmente allegri, dobbiamo usare saggezza nel fare ciò che possiamo per gestire quanti più fattori esterni possibile per minimizzare il rischio di una depressione debilitante (estrema).

Gli stress esterni sono spesso la causa scatenante di questi sentimenti (discouragement). Può trattarsi della morte di un amico o familiare stretto, oppure di una disgrazia finanziaria. È importante ricordare che anche eventi positivi possono produrre grandi quantità di stress. Le madri con neonati spesso funzionano con pochissimo sonno, mentre stanno anche vivendo grandi cambiamenti fisici nei loro corpi.

Alcune persone possono avere scarse abilità di coping. Purtroppo molti ricorrono a droghe di strada o ad alcool per cercare di soffocare i sentimenti che altrimenti non riescono a controllare.

Infine, peccato e senso di colpa possono innescare la depressione o peggiorarla. Vediamo questo presente nella vita di Davide e di Saul. (Vedi Salmi, capitolo 32) Questo non vuol dire che tutta la depressione sia il risultato del peccato—ben lungi—ma il peccato va affrontato e confessato, per poter andare avanti.

Forse come nota a margine, menzionerò che per esperienza, le persone profondamente depresse spesso lottano con un senso di colpa atroce. Non sanno nemmeno quale peccato possano aver commesso; sono solo sicure che Dio è arrabbiato con loro e che devono aver fatto qualcosa di sbagliato. Curare la depressione aiuterà con le questioni di certezza della salvezza con cui queste persone tendono a lottare.

Questo ci lascia con la domanda su come aiutare qualcuno che sta vivendo questo tipo di pensiero.

Ascolta

Ascoltare è uno strumento potente per aiutare gli altri. Ascolta attivamente e senza interrompere i pensieri negativi.

Potresti vedere che non tutto è tragico e che c’è molto di positivo nel mondo. Il fatto che loro non riescano a vedere queste cose ha più a che fare con il loro stato mentale che con quanto le cose siano realmente terribili. Una persona che lotta con la depressione può sapere che ci sono persone in condizioni peggiori nel mondo, ma non serve molto indicarglielo.

Incoraggia

L’incoraggiamento può essere semplicemente dire cose buone che vedi nella vita della persona che lotta. Questo è qualcosa di cui tutti noi abbiamo bisogno di più.

Più di questo, dobbiamo incoraggiare le persone a fare cose che siano salutari per loro stesse. Devono uscire di casa, provare a fare esercizio e tentare di mangiare in modo sano. Possiamo aiutarle a migliorare in tutte queste aree. (Vedi Galati 6:2)

Prega

…La fervente preghiera del giusto ha molta efficacia –Giacomo 5:16.

Queste persone hanno bisogno che qualcuno preghi con loro. Hanno bisogno che qualcuno preghi per loro. Gesù ci chiede di pregare in segreto, ma è anche molto incoraggiante per chi lotta sentirsi pregare. Questo li aiuta a sapere che ci sono molte persone che li sostengono con la preghiera.

Sii disposto a essere l’iniziatore

Le persone con depressione hanno livelli di energia molto bassi. Inoltre, non si vedono come aventi valore, almeno abbastanza perché qualcun altro voglia passare del tempo con loro. Non chiameranno o manderanno messaggi e certamente non organizzeranno un pranzo o un momento di preghiera.

Anche se desiderano tutte queste cose, è davvero difficile per loro fare il primo passo per cercare gli altri. Tocca quindi a noi essere disposti a fare quelle cose.

Non saltare a conclusioni

Conosciamo la storia degli amici di Giobbe. Vennero da lui dopo che la calamità lo aveva colpito e rimasero seduti in silenzio per diversi giorni, sotto shock vedendo la devastazione che gli era capitata. Quando finalmente cominciarono a parlare, lo giudicarono per il terribile peccato che presuppondevano avesse commesso.

Non è sbagliato chiedere del peccato, ma ci sono molte occasioni in cui la depressione non è legata al peccato. Concentrarsi prematuramente sul peccato, o presumerne l’esistenza, creerà semplicemente spaccature che renderanno meno probabile riuscire ad aiutare una persona a trovare guarigione.

E se sei tu la persona che lotta con la depressione? Come dovresti affrontarla e cosa può aiutare?

Affronta i problemi precocemente

Tutti abbiamo momenti in cui siamo stressati e davvero scoraggiati. Nel campo medico usiamo termini come “burnout” e “fatica da compassione” quando le persone stanno andando nella direzione sbagliata. Queste difficoltà si manifestano quando diventiamo irritabili con chi ci sta intorno, quando siamo stanchi la maggior parte del tempo o quando ci sentiamo scoraggiati perlopiù. Quando vediamo che questi sintomi stanno emergendo, è il momento di fare qualcosa per evitare che peggiorino.

Forse un primo passo è semplicemente conoscere i propri limiti. Ci sono momenti in cui dobbiamo dire no a progetti di lavoro o persino ad attività della chiesa perché non ci lasciano tempo sufficiente per riposare. Certi periodi dell’anno possono essere peggiori—molte persone faticano di più durante i mesi invernali a causa della minore esposizione alla luce solare.

Ridurre il carico nelle aree possibili è importante quando vediamo di essere su una traiettoria sbagliata.

Non fare confronti

Ognuno è diverso. Identificare persone che sembrano “avere tutto sotto controllo” mentre tu stai lottando non ti aiuta e probabilmente ti farà sentire peggio.

Lottare con il scoraggiamento non significa che tu non sia un cristiano o che Dio abbia finito con te. Significa che sei umano che vive in un mondo caduto. Non vuoi continuare a vivere con uno spirito depresso, ma non dovresti nemmeno credere di essere l’unico ad aver affrontato questo problema. (Vedi 2 Corinzi 10:12)

Esercizio fisico

L’esercizio cardiovascolare è molto importante per aumentare i neurotrasmettitori nel cervello associati alla depressione. Non importa tanto quale tipo di esercizio fai. Quel che conta è che aumenti la frequenza cardiaca del 25-30 percento sopra il tuo ritmo cardiaco basale.

L’esercizio è qualcosa di difficile da fare, anche quando non si è depressi. È particolarmente difficile quando si è affaticati e giù di morale.

Trascorri tempo con incoraggiatori

Le persone hanno bisogno di comunità. Quando affrontiamo sentimenti depressivi, abbiamo davvero bisogno di altri intorno che ci sollevino, pregare con noi e darci incoraggiamento. Nessuno di noi trae beneficio dal passare lunghi periodi da solo. (Vedi Proverbi 27:17)

Affronta il peccato

Il peccato può rendere la preghiera poco efficace. Questo non vuol dire che semplicemente confessare il peccato farà svanire immediatamente la depressione di qualcuno, ma è una parte importante per raggiungere la guarigione. Confessate dunque i vostri peccati gli uni agli altri e pregate gli uni per gli altri, affinché siate guariti… –Giacomo 5:16.

Sii disposto a prendere farmaci

Non tutti hanno bisogno di farmaci. La speranza è che se fai le cose giuste (utili) (alcune delle quali elencate sopra), tu possa evitare che la situazione peggiori al punto da richiedere aiuto medico. Ma ci sono molte situazioni in cui qualcuno ha semplicemente bisogno di iniziare una terapia farmacologica per aiutarlo in vari modi: dormire, calmare una mente stanca che non si ferma, attenuare il dolore emotivo, ecc.

Le persone con depressione sufficientemente grave possono rappresentare un rischio per sé stesse. Possono essere anche completamente incapaci di rispondere a una consulenza o ad altri trattamenti non farmacologici per questi sentimenti. Queste persone hanno davvero bisogno di iniziare una terapia farmacologica con l’obiettivo di passare gradualmente via da questi farmaci in futuro, quando penseranno con sufficiente chiarezza per proseguire sulla strada giusta.

Sfortunatamente, i benefici di questi farmaci sembrano essere di breve durata. L’uso a lungo termine degli antidepressivi non sembra davvero migliorare la qualità della vita per molti pazienti. Uno studio recente ha esaminato pazienti che assumevano antidepressivi e li ha confrontati con quelli che non ne facevano uso, riscontrando livelli simili di qualità della vita correlata alla salute nei due gruppi. In altre parole, confrontando due gruppi di pazienti depressi, uno in terapia farmacologica e l’altro no, dopo un periodo di tempo (circa 6 mesi) non c’erano più differenze osservabili nei loro livelli di depressione. Quindi, mentre questi farmaci possono aiutare a stabilizzare una persona con depressione grave, dopo un certo periodo l’effetto terapeutico del farmaco tende a diminuire. Si spera che a quel punto la persona sia sufficientemente stabile da poter intraprendere una riduzione sicura per sospendere il farmaco.

Con questo in mente, è molto importante fare cose, oltre ai farmaci, per cercare di migliorare la situazione.

Continua, anche quando ti senti meglio

Molte volte, quando qualcuno ha un problema medico, cambia consapevolmente la propria dieta e il proprio stile di vita per migliorare la situazione. Il problema è che quando i sintomi migliorano, la tendenza è tornare alle vecchie abitudini alimentari e comportamentali.

Se hai affrontato la depressione in passato, è importante continuare su un percorso di scelte salutari. Esercitati regolarmente, mangia pasti sani, gestisci il tuo livello di stress (per quanto possibile), non sovraccaricarti di impegni e fai uno sforzo cosciente per incontrarti regolarmente con amici pii per momenti di preghiera e sostegno.

Fai periodicamente un inventario di come stai procedendo. Se stai lottando, individua cosa cambiare per migliorare la situazione.

La depressione è molto comune nella nostra società e nelle nostre chiese. Possiamo avere vittoria su di essa da soli, ma con l’aiuto di Dio e con il sostegno dei fratelli e delle sorelle cristiane, possiamo andare avanti.

Potresti non essere gloriosamente felice tutto il tempo, ma per la grazia di Dio, avrai la gioia del Signore nel tuo cuore, anche nei giorni più stressanti.

And Jesus, walking by the sea of Galilee, saw two brethren, Simon called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers. And he saith unto them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men. And they straightway left their nets, and followed him. And going on from thence, he saw other two brethren, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in a ship with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them. And they immediately left the ship and their father, and followed him –Matthew 4:18-22.

Little did they know where this journey would lead them. They received the call, they responded to the call, and now they were on a journey that would forever change their lives. Little do we know when we choose to follow Jesus where that journey will lead us. That is why it is considered a journey of faith.

One thing is certain, walking with Jesus will lead you into a life of holiness. What exactly do we mean by holiness? Holiness is the full sum of the righteousness of Jesus manifested in our lives by the work of regeneration and the inner renewing of the Holy Ghost.

John the Baptist said of Jesus: I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance: but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire: Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire –Matthew 3:11-12.

This speaks of the baptism of the Holy Ghost and fire, and of the thorough purging that Jesus would bring. Jesus did not come with violence and yet His righteous presence swept through Palestine like a winnowing breeze. Those who rejected Him were blown away and disappeared from the narrative. Those who loved Him were set forth as the chosen ones who became the founders of a new kingdom established on principles not known before.

The principles of this new kingdom are demonstrated in the life of Christ and explained in His teachings. In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus set forth teaching that challenged the most pious Pharisee and disturbed the apathy of the sinner. Jesus’ teachings were such that they could not be lightly ignored for they stirred a deep longing in the human heart for the love and peace that they offered while at the same time exposing the innate selfishness that prevented it.

It was this promise and hope of a new humanity that drew crowds of people after Him. They followed Jesus, some hoping for a miracle, some for bread, but many were drawn to Him by a deep inner longing for deliverance from the stranglehold of sin. Those who truly sought deliverance, found it.

One such disciple was Mary Magdalene. The Scripture gives us only cursory glances of her life. She appears to have been one of several women of whom the Scriptures make mention that followed Jesus. Doctor Luke tells us that Jesus healed her of evil spirits and infirmities. Apparently, she was not only possessed of evil spirits, but also physically infirmed.

And it came to pass afterward, that he went throughout every city and village, preaching and shewing the glad tidings of the kingdom of God: and the twelve were with him, And certain women, which had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities, Mary called Magdalene, out of whom went seven devils, And Joanna the wife of Chuza Herod's steward, and Susanna, and many others, which ministered unto him of their substance –Luke 8:1-3.

Mary became a faithful follower of Jesus. Her presence is especially noted in the Scriptures after the death of Christ. She was first to the sepulcher early on the resurrection morning and she lingered there when the others had gone away. Her diligent pursuit of Christ was rewarded when Jesus appeared first to her.

Jesus saith unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? whom seekest thou? She, supposing him to be the gardener, saith unto him, Sir, if thou have borne him hence, tell me where thou hast laid him, and I will take him away. Jesus saith unto her, Mary. She turned herself, and saith unto him, Rabboni; which is to say, Master –John 20:15-16.

Mary knew Jesus the moment He spoke her name. This intimacy was born of a passion for Christ that was the fruit of her deliverance. Mary’s love for Jesus was the result of having been delivered from seven devils.

Jesus’ primary mission in coming to earth was to deliver us from the power of sin. In Luke 5, Doctor Luke records an account of a man who was paralyzed. He could not walk. His friends brought him for healing, but they could not reach Jesus because of the crowd. So, they went up onto the roof and removed enough of roof tiles to let their friend through and lowered him into the presence of Jesus. How ingenious! How desperate they were to help their friend to find healing.

And when he saw their faith, he said unto him, Man, thy sins are forgiven thee –Luke 5:20. They sought healing, but Jesus saw the deeper need of this man’s soul, so He offered forgiveness. This, of course, raised the ire of the Pharisees who …began to reason, saying, Who is this which speaketh blasphemies? Who can forgive sins, but God alone? –Luke 5:21. They were right, only God can forgive sins, but what they did not want to believe was that Jesus was God’s Son and that thus He had did have the power to forgive sins. So, Jesus went on to say: …What reason ye in your hearts? Whether is easier, to say, Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Rise up and walk? But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power upon earth to forgive sins, (he said unto the sick of the palsy,) I say unto thee, Arise, and take up thy couch, and go into thine house –Luke 5:22-24.

To follow Jesus is to leave your sins. We would be greatly mistaken to suggest that holiness is a product of human effort. Our journey to holiness must be a journey to Calvary. Many “holy men” and “holy women” down through the ages have sought to live a holy life in their own strength. What always happens is that we settle for a form of godliness that falls short of Christ’s righteousness. We settle for a religion that is doable.

The apostle Paul, when writing about his Jewish brethren said: For they being ignorant of God's righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God –Romans 10:3.

This “righteousness of God” is an inner righteousness of the heart that can only come about through the work of regeneration and the renewing of the Holy Ghost. It is for this reason that our journey with Jesus must lead us to Calvary for it is there that we behold our dying Lord—bleeding, dying for our sins—for my sins—for your sins.

The blood of Jesus is the only means to the “righteousness of God”. The “righteousness of God” is imputed through forgiveness, and it is the fruit of our lives after being empowered through the Holy Spirit. Either way, the “righteousness of God” is attributed to the work of Christ on the cross. There is no other means to holiness.

In Mathew 22, Jesus told the story of a king who planned a wedding for his son. When the invited guests (the Jewish people) refused his invitation, the invitation then went out to all those who had not been invited, and the wedding was furnished with guests.

When the king came in to observe the wedding, he was pleased with what he saw until he spotted a man who was not wearing a wedding garment. (A wedding garment was a white linen garment that was provided by the master of the feast.)

I quote Adam Clark: “Among the Orientals, long white robes were worn at public festivals; and those who appeared on such occasions with any other garments were esteemed, not only highly culpable, but worthy of punishment. The person who invited the guests prepared such a garment for each, for the time being; and with which he was furnished on his application to the ruler of the feast. It was this which made the conduct of the person mentioned in the text inexcusable; he might have had a proper marriage garment, if he had applied for it”.

“Not wearing a wedding garment” was to insult the master of the feast, who provided everything, (including the wedding garment) so that all the guests would be equally suited for the occasion. No one needs to be excluded for lack of proper clothing or any other amenity. The king provided the invitation and all necessary amenities, and the guest need only to accept the invitation and receive the gracious provision of the king.

What a beautiful analogy of the Kingdom of Heaven. The King has invited us to His heavenly feast. He wants us to come and enjoy the feast with Him. He wants us to come no matter who we are or where we come from—some from the gutters of sin, some from the depth of ignorance, and some from the temples of self-righteousness. All are invited to come on equal terms—All must accept the invitation, and all must wear the wedding garment.

We are not told the exact condition of this man who refused the wedding garment, but a general understanding of human nature would indicate that he was probably a well-dressed gentleman. Those who came shabbily dressed would have welcomed the wedding garment to disguise their true condition. Most likely this man wanted to display his finery. He did not feel inclined to cover his fine clothing with a simple white cloak.

This is the condition of all who trust in their own righteousness. The best that we can bring to God falls short of the righteousness that God requires. Isaiah wrote: But we are all as an unclean thing, and all our righteousnesses are as filthy rags; and we all do fade as a leaf; and our iniquities, like the wind, have taken us away –Isaiah 64:6.

In this desperate situation we find ourselves in need of a redeemer. God has provided us with a Redeemer in His Son, Jesus. In whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of his grace –Ephesians 1:7. God has invited us to His feast, and He has provided us with everything that is needed that we can be made righteous.

One attribute of a person who has been cleansed from sin through the blood of Christ, is worship. Luke tells the story of a woman who “was a sinner” who came to worship Jesus: And, behold, a woman in the city, which was a sinner, when she knew that Jesus sat at meat in the Pharisee's house, brought an alabaster box of ointment, And stood at his feet behind him weeping, and began to wash his feet with tears, and did wipe them with the hairs of her head, and kissed his feet, and anointed them with the ointment. Now when the Pharisee which had bidden him saw it, he spake within himself, saying, This man, if he were a prophet, would have known who and what manner of woman this is that toucheth him: for she is a sinner –Luke 7:37-39.

We do not know her name, only that she “was a sinner”. That was her reputation—she was ‘not good’. But she apparently had had a previous encounter with Jesus. She came to Simon’s house to offer her sacrifice of thanksgiving. She brought the best that she had. An alabaster box of ointment said to have been worth a year’s wages. She anointed Jesus’ feet and washed them with her tears—tears of repentance, tears of joy, tears of relief.

Simon observed her worship. He despised her in his heart. He considered her offering a great waste. Jesus challenged him. He said to Simon: …Seest thou this woman? I entered into thine house, thou gavest me no water for my feet: but she hath washed my feet with tears, and wiped them with the hairs of her head. Thou gavest me no kiss: but this woman since the time I came in hath not ceased to kiss my feet. My head with oil thou didst not anoint: but this woman hath anointed my feet with ointment. Wherefore I say unto thee, Her sins, which are many, are forgiven; for she loved much: but to whom little is forgiven, the same loveth little –Luke 7:44-47.

He said to the woman …Thy sins are forgiven –Luke 7:48. Forgiveness, and freedom from sin, awaken the heart to worship. When a man or woman is set free from the guilt and bondage of sin, praise flows freely. Simon was a Pharisee who was relying on his own righteousness. Yet Jesus brought him to the awareness that he was greatly lacking in love and worship.

Following Jesus will lead us to holiness of heart and life. Following Jesus brings us face to face with the cause and the cure of the sin problem. The cause of sin is our fallen carnal nature, and our fallen nature is revealed in the light of His holiness. Along with Mary Magdalene and the other disciples, as we journey with Jesus, we become aware of our need and our need cries out for His grace. The cure for our sin is Jesus—…thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins –Matthew 1:21.

In Augustus Toplady’s famous hymn, Rock of Ages we find this line–

Be of sin the double cure; save me from its guilt (through forgiveness) and power (through sanctification).

En Jezus, wandelende langs de zee van Galilea, zag twee broeders, Simon, die Petrus genoemd wordt, en Andreas zijn broer, die een net in zee uitwierpen; want zij waren vissers. En Hij zei tegen hen: Volgt Mij, en Ik zal u vissers van mensen maken. En zij lieten terstond hun netten en volgden Hem. En van daar gaande zag Hij anderen twee broeders, Jakob, de zoon van Zebedeüs, en Johannes zijn broer, in een boot met Zebedeüs hun vader, die hun netten herstelden; en Hij riep hen. En zij lieten terstond de boot en hun vader achter en volgden Hem –Mattheüs 4:18-22.

Weinigen wisten waar deze reis hen heen zou leiden. Zij ontvingen de roeping, zij reageerden op de roeping, en nu waren zij op een reis die hun leven voor altijd zou veranderen. Weinig weten wij waarheen die reis ons zal brengen wanneer wij ervoor kiezen Jezus te volgen. Daarom wordt het beschouwd als een reis des geloofs.

Één ding staat vast: wandelen met Jezus zal je leiden tot een leven van heiligheid. Wat bedoelen we precies met heiligheid? Heiligheid is de volledige som van de gerechtigheid van Jezus, gemanifesteerd in ons leven door het werk van wedergeboorte en de innerlijke vernieuwing door de Heilige Geest.

Johannes de Doper zei van Jezus: Ik doop u inderdaad met water ten teken van bekering; maar Hij die na mij komt, is machtiger dan ik, van wie ik niet waardig ben de rijgsels van Zijn schoenen te dragen; Hij zal u dopen met de Heilige Geest en met vuur; Zijn wan is in Zijn hand, en Hij zal Zijn dorsvloer grondig zuiveren en Zijn tarwe bijeenbrengen in de schuur; maar Hij zal de kaf met onblusbaar vuur verbranden –Mattheüs 3:11-12.

Dit spreekt van de doop met de Heilige Geest en met vuur, en van de grondige reiniging die Jezus zou brengen. Jezus kwam niet met geweld, en toch trok Zijn rechtvaardige aanwezigheid als een dorswind door Palestina. Degenen die Hem verwierven, werden weggeblazen en verdwenen uit het verhaal. Degenen die Hem liefhadden, werden naar voren gesteld als de uitverkorenen die de stichters werden van een nieuw koninkrijk dat op principes berustte die eerder niet bekend waren.

De principes van dit nieuwe koninkrijk worden gedemonstreerd in het leven van Christus en uitgelegd in Zijn leer. In de Bergrede stelde Jezus leringen voor die de vroomste Farizeeër uitdaagden en de apathie van de zondaar verontrustten. Jezus’ onderwijs was zodanig dat het niet licht kon worden genegeerd, want het wekte een diepe hunkering in het menselijk hart naar de liefde en vrede die het bood, terwijl het tegelijkertijd de aangeboren eigenliefde blootlegde die dat verhinderde.

Het was deze belofte en hoop op een nieuw mensdom die menigten mensen naar Hem toe trok. Zij volgden Jezus, sommigen hopend op een wonder, sommigen op brood, maar velen werden door Hem aangetrokken door een diepe innerlijke hunkering naar bevrijding van de verstikkende greep van de zonde. Degenen die werkelijk bevrijding zochten, vonden die.

Een van die discipelen was Maria Magdalena. De Schrift geeft ons slechts vluchtige aanwijzingen over haar leven. Zij lijkt een van meerdere vrouwen te zijn van wie de Schriften melding maken die Jezus volgden. Artsen-Lukas vertelt ons dat Jezus haar genas van boze geesten en ziekten. Blijkbaar was zij niet alleen bezeten door boze geesten, maar ook lichamelijk ziek.

En het geschiedde daarna dat Hij door alle steden en dorpen ging, predikende en verkondigende de blijde boodschap van het koninkrijk van God; en de twaalf waren met Hem, en enkele vrouwen die van boze geesten en ziekten waren genezen, Maria, genoemd Magdalena, waaruit zeven demonen waren uitgegaan, en Johanna, de vrouw van Choesa, die Herodes' beheerder was, en Suzanna, en vele anderen, die voor Hem uit hun middelen dienden –Lukas 8:1-3.

Maria werd een trouwe volgelinge van Jezus. Haar aanwezigheid wordt in het bijzonder genoemd in de Schriften na de dood van Christus. Zij was de eerste bij het graf vroeg op de paasochtend en bleef daar hangen toen de anderen waren weggegaan. Haar ijverige navolging van Christus werd beloond toen Jezus haar als eerste verscheen.

Jezus zei tegen haar: Vrouw, waarom huil je? Wie zoek je? Zij, terwijl zij Hem voor de tuinman aanzien, zei tegen Hem: Heer, als U Hem weggehaald hebt, vertel mij waar U Hem gelegd hebt, en ik zal Hem wegnemen. Jezus zei tegen haar: Maria. Zij keerde zich om en zei tegen Hem: Rabboni; dat is, Meester –Johannes 20:15-16.

Maria kende Jezus op het ogenblik dat Hij haar naam sprak. Deze intimiteit was geboren uit een passie voor Christus die de vrucht was van haar bevrijding. Maria’s liefde voor Jezus was het resultaat van haar bevrijding van zeven demonen.

Jezus’ voornaamste missie in het komen naar de aarde was ons te bevrijden van de macht der zonde. In Lukas 5 geeft Artsen-Lukas een verslag van een man die verlamd was. Hij kon niet lopen. Zijn vrienden brachten hem om genezing, maar zij konden Jezus niet bereiken vanwege de menigte. Dus gingen zij op het dak en verwijderden genoeg dakpannen om hun vriend door te laten en lieten hem beneden in de tegenwoordigheid van Jezus zakken. Hoe vindingrijk! Hoe wanhopig waren zij om hun vriend te helpen genezing te vinden.

En toen Hij hun geloof zag, zei Hij tegen hem: Mens, uw zonden zijn u vergeven –Lukas 5:20. Zij zochten genezing, maar Jezus zag de diepere behoefte van deze ziel, dus Hij bood vergeving aan. Dit riep natuurlijk de woede op van de Farizeeën die …begonnen te redeneren en zeiden: Wie is deze die godslasteringen spreekt? Wie kan zonden vergeven dan God alleen? –Lukas 5:21. Zij hadden gelijk: alleen God kan zonden vergeven, maar wat zij niet wilden geloven was dat Jezus de Zoon van God was en dat Hij daardoor wél de macht had zonden te vergeven. Dus vervolgde Jezus en zei: Wat bent u nu in uw hart aan het bedenken? Wat is gemakkelijker te zeggen: Uw zonden zijn u vergeven; of te zeggen: Sta op en wandel? Maar opdat u zou weten dat de Zoon des mensen macht heeft op aarde zonden te vergeven, (hij zei tegen de verlamde,) Ik zeg u: Sta op, neem uw bed op en ga naar uw huis –Lukas 5:22-24.

Jezus volgen is je zonden achterlaten. Wij zouden ons ernstig vergissen als wij suggereren dat heiligheid een product is van menselijke inspanning. Onze reis naar heiligheid moet een reis naar Calvarië zijn. Veel "heilige mannen" en "heilige vrouwen" door de eeuwen heen hebben geprobeerd een heilig leven te leiden in hun eigen kracht. Wat er altijd gebeurt, is dat we het doen met een vorm van godsvrucht die tekortschiet tegenover Christus’ gerechtigheid. We nemen genoegen met een religie die te doen is.

De apostel Paulus zei toen hij over zijn Joodse broeders schreef: Want zij, die de gerechtigheid van God niet kenden en hun eigen gerechtigheid probeerden te stichten, hebben zich niet onderworpen aan de gerechtigheid van God –Romeinen 10:3.

Deze "gerechtigheid van God" is een innerlijke gerechtigheid van het hart die slechts kan voortkomen door het werk van wedergeboorte en de vernieuwing door de Heilige Geest. Het is om deze reden dat onze weg met Jezus ons naar Calvarië moet leiden, want daar aanschouwen wij onze stervende Heer—bloedend, stervend voor onze zonden—for mijn zonden—for jouw zonden.

Het bloed van Jezus is het enige middel tot de "gerechtigheid van God". De "gerechtigheid van God" wordt toegerekend door vergeving, en het is de vrucht van ons leven nadat wij door de Heilige Geest zijn bekrachtigd. Hoe dan ook, de "gerechtigheid van God" is toe te schrijven aan het werk van Christus aan het kruis. Er is geen ander middel tot heiligheid.

In Mattheüs 22 vertelde Jezus het verhaal van een koning die een bruiloft voor zijn zoon voorbereidde. Toen de uitgenodigde gasten (het Joodse volk) zijn uitnodiging weigerden, werd de uitnodiging uitgestuurd naar allen die niet uitgenodigd waren, en de bruiloft werd gevuld met gasten.

Toen de koning binnenkwam om de bruiloft te bekijken, was hij tevreden met wat hij zag totdat hij een man zag die geen bruiloftskleed droeg. (Een bruiloftskleed was een wit linnen kleed dat door de heer des geschenks werd verstrekt.)

Ik citeer Adam Clark: "Onder de Oosterse mensen droegen men lange witte gewaden bij openbare feesten; en degenen die bij zulke gelegenheden andere kleding droegen, werden niet alleen als zeer schuldig geacht, maar waardig tot straf. Degene die de gasten uitnodigde, bereidde zo’n kleed voor ieder, voor die tijd; en waarmee hij hem bij zijn verzoek aan de bestuurder van het feest uitrustte. Het was dit wat het gedrag van de in de tekst genoemde persoon onvergeeflijk maakte; hij had een geschikter huwelijkskleed kunnen hebben, als hij erom had gevraagd."

"Het niet dragen van een bruiloftskleed" was een belediging van de heer des feestmalen, die alles verschafte, (inclusief het bruiloftskleed) zodat alle gasten gelijk passend zouden zijn voor de gelegenheid. Niemand hoefde uitgesloten te worden wegens gebrek aan geschikte kleding of enige andere voorziening. De koning gaf de uitnodiging en alle noodzakelijke voorzieningen, en de gast hoefde alleen de uitnodiging te aanvaarden en de genadige voorziening van de koning te ontvangen.

Wat een prachtige vergelijking van het Koninkrijk der Hemelen. De Koning heeft ons uitgenodigd tot Zijn hemels feest. Hij wil dat wij komen en het feest met Hem genieten. Hij wil dat wij komen, ongeacht wie wij zijn of waar wij vandaan komen—sommigen uit de goot van zonde, sommigen uit de diepten van onwetendheid, en sommigen uit de tempels van eigengerechtigheid. Allen zijn uitgenodigd om op gelijke voorwaarden te komen—Allen moeten de uitnodiging aannemen, en allen moeten het bruiloftskleed dragen.

Wij krijgen niet te horen wat de precieze toestand van deze man was die het bruiloftskleed weigerde te dragen, maar een algemeen begrip van de menselijke natuur zou aangeven dat hij waarschijnlijk een goed geklede heer was. Degenen die sjofel gekleed kwamen, zouden het bruiloftskleed hebben verwelkomd om hun ware toestand te verbergen. Hoogstwaarschijnlijk wilde deze man zijn pracht tonen. Hij voelde zich niet geneigd zijn fraaie kleding te bedekken met een eenvoudig wit kleed.

Dit is de toestand van allen die op hun eigen gerechtigheid vertrouwen. Het beste wat wij God kunnen brengen schiet tekort van de gerechtigheid die God verlangt. Jesaja schreef: Maar wij allen zijn als een verontreinigd ding, en al onze gerechtigheden zijn als een bevlekte doek; en wij verdorren alle als een blad; en onze ongerechtigheden hebben ons weggenomen als de wind –Jesaja 64:6.

In deze hopeloze toestand bevinden wij ons in behoefte aan een Redder. God heeft ons voorzien van een Redder in Zijn Zoon, Jezus. In wie wij de verlossing hebben door Zijn bloed, namelijk de vergeving der zonden, naar de rijkdom Zijner genade –Efeziërs 1:7. God heeft ons uitgenodigd tot Zijn feest, en Hij heeft ons alles voorzien wat nodig is om rechtvaardig te worden gemaakt.

Een kenmerk van een persoon die van zonde is gereinigd door het bloed van Christus, is aanbidding. Lukas vertelt het verhaal van een vrouw die "een zondares" was en kwam om Jezus te aanbidden: En zie, er was in de stad een vrouw die een zondares was; en toen zij wist dat Jezus aanliggend in het huis van een Farizeeër zat, bracht zij een alabaster doos met zalf, en stond achter Hem bij Zijn voeten en weende, en begon Zijn voeten te wassen met haar tranen en droogde ze met de haren van haar hoofd, en kuste Zijn voeten en zalfde ze met de zalf. Nu toen de Farizeeër die Hem had uitgenodigd dit zag, zei hij bij zichzelf: Als deze man een profeet ware, zou Hij weten wie en welk een vrouw deze is die Hem aanraakt; want zij is een zondares –Lukas 7:37-39.

Wij kennen haar naam niet, alleen dat zij "een zondares" was. Dat was haar reputatie—zij was 'niet goed'. Maar zij had blijkbaar een eerdere ontmoeting met Jezus gehad. Zij kwam in Simons huis om haar dankofferde te brengen. Zij bracht het beste dat zij had. Een alabaster doos met zalf, naar verluidt waard een jaarsalaris. Zij zalfde Jezus’ voeten en waste ze met haar tranen—tranen van bekering, tranen van blijdschap, tranen van verlichting.

Simon zag haar aanbidding. Hij verachtte haar in zijn hart. Hij achtte haar offer een grote verspilling. Jezus gaf hem daarop te kennen. Hij zei tegen Simon: Zie je deze vrouw? Ik ben uw huis binnengekomen, gij hebt mij geen water gegeven voor mijn voeten; maar zij heeft mijn voeten gewassen met tranen en heeft ze afgeveegd met de haren van haar hoofd. Gij hebt mij geen kus gegeven; maar deze vrouw heeft, vanaf het ogenblik dat ik binnenkwam, niet opgehouden mijn voeten te kussen. Gij hebt mijn hoofd niet met olie gezalfd; maar deze vrouw heeft mijn voeten gezalfd met zalf. Daarom zeg ik u: Haar zonden, die talrijk zijn, zijn vergeven; want zij heeft veel liefgehad; maar aan wie weinig vergeven wordt, die heeft weinig liefgehad –Lukas 7:44-47.

Hij zei tot de vrouw: Uw zonden zijn u vergeven –Lukas 7:48. Vergeving en vrijspraak van zonde wekken het hart tot aanbidding. Wanneer een man of vrouw vrijgemaakt wordt van de schuld en de slavernij der zonde, vloeit lofprijs vrijelijk voort. Simon was een Farizeeër die op zijn eigen gerechtigheid vertrouwde. Toch bracht Jezus hem tot het besef dat hij zeer gebrek had aan liefde en aanbidding.

Jezus volgen zal ons leiden tot heiligheid van hart en leven. Jezus volgen brengt ons oog in oog met de oorzaak en het geneesmiddel van het zondeprobleem. De oorzaak van de zonde is onze gevallen aard, en onze gevallen aard wordt geopenbaard in het licht van Zijn heiligheid. Samen met Maria Magdalena en de andere discipelen worden wij, terwijl wij met Jezus reizen, bewust van onze behoefte en onze behoefte roept om Zijn genade. Het geneesmiddel voor onze zonde is Jezus—…gij zult Zijn naam noemen Jezus; want Hij zal Zijn volk behouden van hun zonden –Mattheüs 1:21.

In Augustus Toplady’s beroemde hymne, Rock of Ages, vinden wij deze regel–

Wees van de zonde de dubbele genezing; red mij van haar schuld (door vergeving) en haar macht (door heiliging).

The angel of the LORD encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them –Psalm 34:7.

“Tell us a story, Grandma,” begged two eager children as they crowded around her rocking chair.

“My, my, you children like to hear stories, don’t you?” replied Grandma, with a twinkle in her eye. “All right, I’ll tell you about a time when I was about eight years old, and my sister Lori was nine.

We lived on an old farm, back a short lane along a dirt road. One morning, Mother called us in from our play and said she was out of sugar. She asked us to walk to Mrs. Brightbill to see if she had any sugar to spare. You see, we didn’t have telephones when I was a little girl, so she couldn’t call the neighbor and ask her. Neighbors often shared back and forth because we didn’t go shopping at the store very often either. So, mother gave us a container, and we started out on our long walk as Mother called after us and reminded us not to loiter along the way.”

“How far was it to the Brightbills?” asked Sharon.

“Oh, it was about half a mile to our closest neighbor, the Rhine’s place, and then about another quarter of a mile to the Brightbills,” replied Grandma.

“Oh, that’s far. Mother won’t let us walk on the road at all,” added Micah.

“I’m sure you are right,” agreed Grandma. “And I hope you never walk on the road without your parents’ permission. But things were much different when I was a little girl. We also walked every day to school, which was quite a bit further than the Brightbill farm. So, the little errand we were doing on this morning for Mother seemed like fun. There was only one problem though. The Rhine family had an old man living in their summer house. His name was Pierce, and he had a very fierce dog; at least he acted very fierce! He was kept behind a high wire fence connected to an old shed.

Every day when we walked to school, that dog frightened us terribly with his fierce barking and growling. But Mother always reminded us to pray and remember the Bible verse which says: What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee –Psalm 56:3. Still, we hurried by as fast as our legs could take us.

Lori and I started out happily on our errand for Mother. We skipped along, watching the dust swirl beneath our feet on that warm summer morning. Everything seemed unusually quiet and still as we passed through the gully, over the rippling creek, and up the steep hill right before Neighbor Rhine’s place. There before us was the old shed, and on the other side was the high fence which kept in Pierce’s mean dog. My heart began to thump rapidly. ‘Maybe that bad dog hadn’t seen us yet,’ I thought gratefully as I whispered once more to myself, ‘I will trust and not be afraid.’

Suddenly, the air was shattered by the ferocious barking of that mean dog as he sprang around the corner of the old shed! Lori and I froze in our tracks! As that angry dog raced toward us, Lori screamed. The next moment, I realized she had fallen down and was sitting in the middle of the dirt road, with her hands behind her on the hard packed gravel, feet and legs in the air, kicking and kicking, spinning around and around as that angry dog circled her, jumping in at her and nipping at her feet and legs! I was so scared. I just stood frozen to the spot. I don’t remember if I screamed, or if I prayed. But suddenly there was a shout! It was Pierce, with a whip in his hand. He came running around the shed and out on the road. He whipped and whipped that dog and finally got him away from Lori and back inside the fence where he belonged, as Lori and I stood there, trembling, and crying with relief.”

“Wow!” exclaimed Sharon. “That was really scary, wasn’t it?”

“Did Pierce need to get rid of his dog?” asked Micah.

“Yes, Sharon, it was very scary,” answered Grandma. “And no, Micah, Pierce did not get rid of his dog. We children needed to keep trusting the good Lord to keep us safe every day.”

“I don’t remember what happened after Pierce got the dog away that day, or if we ever got Mother’s sugar, but I will never forget what happened that day.

It was a miracle that Lori and I were not injured. There is a verse in Psalms which says: Save me from the lion’s mouth… –Psalm 22:21. How thankful we were to be delivered from the dog’s mouth! I like to think that the Lord’s angel had his sword drawn in front of that dog’s mouth every time he leaped at my dear sister.”

malaikat TUHAN berkemah di sekeliling orang-orang yang takut akan Dia, dan melepaskan mereka –Mazmur 34:7.

“Ceritakan sebuah cerita, Nenek,” pinta dua anak yang bersemangat sambil berkumpul di sekitar kursi goyangnya.

“Ya ampun, kalian anak-anak senang mendengar cerita, bukan?” jawab Nenek, dengan kilau di matanya. “Baiklah, aku akan ceritakan tentang suatu waktu ketika aku kira-kira berumur delapan tahun, dan saudara perempuanku Lori berumur sembilan.

Kami tinggal di sebuah peternakan tua, di ujung jalan kecil di sepanjang jalan tanah. Suatu pagi, Ibu memanggil kami dari bermain dan berkata bahwa ia kehabisan gula. Ia meminta kami berjalan ke rumah Nyonya Brightbill untuk melihat apakah dia punya gula yang bisa dipinjamkan. Lihat, kami tidak punya telepon ketika aku masih kecil, jadi ia tidak bisa menelepon tetangga dan bertanya. Tetangga sering saling berbagi karena kami juga tidak sering berbelanja di toko. Jadi, ibu memberi kami sebuah wadah, dan kami memulai jalan panjang kami sementara Ibu memanggil dari belakang dan mengingatkan kami untuk tidak nongkrong di sepanjang jalan.”

“Seberapa jauh ke rumah keluarga Brightbill?” tanya Sharon.

“Oh, sekitar setengah mil ke tetangga terdekat kami, tempat keluarga Rhine, dan kemudian sekitar seperempat mil lagi ke rumah Brightbill,” jawab Nenek.

“Oh, itu jauh. Ibu tidak mengizinkan kami berjalan di jalan sama sekali,” tambah Micah.

“Aku yakin kalian benar,” setuju Nenek. “Dan aku harap kalian tidak pernah berjalan di jalan tanpa izin orang tua kalian. Tetapi keadaan sangat berbeda ketika aku masih kecil. Kami juga berjalan setiap hari ke sekolah, yang jauhnya jauh lebih daripada peternakan Brightbill. Jadi, tugas kecil yang kami lakukan pagi itu untuk Ibu terasa menyenangkan. Hanya ada satu masalah. Keluarga Rhine punya seorang pria tua yang tinggal di rumah musim panas mereka. Namanya Pierce, dan dia mempunyai seekor anjing yang sangat galak; setidaknya kelihatannya sangat galak! Anjing itu dikurung di balik pagar kawat tinggi yang terhubung ke sebuah gudang tua.

Setiap hari ketika kami berjalan ke sekolah, anjing itu sangat menakutkan kami dengan gonggongannya yang galak dan geramnya. Tetapi Ibu selalu mengingatkan kami untuk berdoa dan mengingat ayat Alkitab yang berkata: Pada waktu aku takut, aku akan percaya kepada-Mu –Mazmur 56:3. Namun, kami tetap bergegas melewatinya secepat kaki kami bisa melangkah.

Lori dan aku memulai tugas kami dengan gembira untuk Ibu. Kami melompat-lompat, menyaksikan debu berputar di bawah kaki kami pada pagi musim panas yang hangat itu. Segalanya tampak sangat sunyi dan tenang ketika kami melewati jurang, menyeberangi sungai kecil yang beriak, dan menaiki bukit curam tepat sebelum rumah tetangga Rhine. Di sana di depan kami ada gudang tua, dan di seberangnya pagar tinggi yang menahan anjing galak milik Pierce. Jantungku mulai berdetak cepat. ‘Mungkin anjing buruk itu belum melihat kita,’ pikirku dengan syukur sambil berbisik sekali lagi pada diriku sendiri, ‘Aku akan percaya dan tidak takut.’

Tiba-tiba, udara pecah oleh gonggongan ganas anjing itu ketika ia melompat mengitari sudut gudang! Lori dan aku membeku di tempat! Ketika anjing marah itu berlari ke arah kami, Lori menjerit. Saat berikutnya, aku menyadari ia telah jatuh dan duduk di tengah jalan tanah, dengan tangan di belakangnya di kerikil padat yang keras, kaki dan kakinya di udara, menendang-nendang, berputar-putar sementara anjing marah itu mengelilinginya, menyerang dan menggigit pada kaki dan betisnya! Aku sangat takut. Aku hanya berdiri membeku. Aku tidak ingat apakah aku berteriak, atau apakah aku berdoa. Tetapi tiba-tiba terdengar teriakan! Itu Pierce, dengan cambuk di tangannya. Dia berlari mengelilingi gudang dan keluar ke jalan. Dia mencambuk dan mencambuk anjing itu dan akhirnya menjauhkan anjing itu dari Lori dan kembali memasukkannya ke dalam pagar tempatnya semestinya, sementara Lori dan aku berdiri di sana, gemetar, dan menangis karena lega.”

“Wah!” seru Sharon. “Itu benar-benar menakutkan, ya?”

“Apakah Pierce harus menyingkirkan anjingnya?” tanya Micah.

“Ya, Sharon, itu sangat menakutkan,” jawab Nenek. “Dan tidak, Micah, Pierce tidak menyingkirkan anjingnya. Kami anak-anak harus terus percaya kepada Tuhan yang baik untuk menjaga kami tetap aman setiap hari.”

“Aku tidak ingat apa yang terjadi setelah Pierce menjauhkan anjing hari itu, atau apakah kami pernah mendapatkan gula Ibu, tetapi aku tidak akan pernah melupakan apa yang terjadi hari itu.

Itu adalah mukjizat bahwa Lori dan aku tidak terluka. Ada sebuah ayat dalam Mazmur yang berkata: Lindungilah aku dari mulut singa… –Mazmur 22:21. Betapa bersyukurnya kami diselamatkan dari mulut anjing itu! Aku suka membayangkan bahwa malaikat Tuhan menajamkan pedangnya di depan mulut anjing itu setiap kali ia melompat ke arah saudara perempuanku yang tercinta.”

Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted?… –Matthew 5:13.

One might wonder as to why the Anabaptists, the early church fathers, church history writers, and especially the progenitor (originator or author) of our beliefs, Christ Himself, effected such a vehement and absolute approach to a separated church and state. Why did they unanimously preach, write, and otherwise caution against political involvement of any kind by Christians? Perhaps this is best answered by looking at the results of Christians ignoring these sincere warnings, casting off their Godly allegiance, and pledging themselves to a flawed and ultimately futile earthly kingdom.

The Mennonites of Germany are a particularly intriguing and cautionary episode of Christian and Anabaptist histories—not only because of their relative proximity to our time—but also because of their almost wholesale devotion to a worldly leader and agenda. What led them to such an un-Christ-like position? A true understanding of their story must begin, naturally, with their beginnings.

The Mennonites of 20th century Germany were descended from the first Anabaptist groups, but unlike our ancestors, they stayed in the Old World instead of emigrating to the New World. There, a number of factors led them to a unique position within world events, a position that would test their mettle on a global stage.

The beginnings of the 20th century brought about the first World War, which ended with the defeat of Germany and its allies. The resulting peace treaties were structured to humiliate and crush Germany, saddling it with an almost unpayable war debt, and restricting its rights to build a military. The German people, unsurprisingly, resented this insult being added to the injury of having lost the War. Their resentment festered, and soon manifested itself in nationalistic movements, the most notable of which was the National Socialist German Workers Party (or the Nazi Party). The party was founded in 1919, and Hitler was amongst its first members. He quickly assumed party leadership, attracting followers with his “us vs. them” rhetoric and strong leadership.

Party growth was small in the decade following its founding. During this time, Hitler continued to shape the Nazis according to his wishes. Hatred for most non-German (Aryan) groups became a central party theme, along with a violent distaste for communism. However, the party was not large enough to be anything but a fringe voice, representing only a small portion of German voters.

Insignificance did not last, however. The Great Depression brought the catalyst for the Nazi’s rise to power. When the global market crashed, over 2 million Germans lost their jobs. Unemployed, they rallied around the charismatic leadership that promised to give them jobs, give them power, to “Make Germany great again”. Moving quickly, Hitler added legions to his followers.

The thousands of new Nazi Party members enabled the Nazi Party to seriously contest many local elections, and in Germany’s Parliament, they were able to control enough votes to sway policy making. In the long run, their political might handed Hitler the office of prime minister. Having secured that position, he went on to overthrow the German government, establishing himself and his party as the undisputed rulers of Germany.

Why did such a man, and such a movement, attract the attention and adoration of a church that professed much of what we do? Loving our enemies, separation from the world, and nonresistance did not seem to combine with the message of the Nazis. The answer, like most backsliding churches, is best portrayed as happening in small steps and over time.

In 1929, the Mennonites came under the eye of Germany and its rapidly expanding Nazi Party. 13,000 Russian Mennonite refugees descended on Moscow, seeking an exit from the Communist-run country. The Nazis seized the situation, using the Mennonites as supposed evidence that Aryans (peoples of German lineage, such as the Mennonites) were being unjustly used by the rest of the world. This image was pushed by state propaganda departments, who circulated writings, pamphlets, and even two immensely popular movies, depicting the Mennonites as strong, red-blooded Germans valiantly striving against the unjust oppression of the Russian Communists. These efforts afforded the refugees national attention, which subsequently led to them being admitted into Germany.

While many Mennonites entered Germany, as refugees and otherwise, there were also thriving, established communities that were given the same patriotic make-over by the Nazi propogandists. Unfortunately, these churches welcomed the Nazi attention, going so far as to send Hitler a letter thanking him for being the “savior of the German peoples” and pledging their support to his government. It is of note that Hitler, a man quite busy running an emerging world power, personally responded to this letter with a memo thanking the churches for their support and expressing a desire for further cooperation to the benefit of both the Nazis and the Mennonites. The church further weakened under these seemingly beneficial relations.

A particularly shocking case of Mennonite political involvement came from the churches in or around Danzig. Danzig and the surrounding countryside had long been a part of the German Empire, until the end of World War I, when the region was separated from Germany, essentially becoming a buffer zone between Germany and Poland. In 1939, Hitler would make one of his first moves on Europe by annexing Danzig, where the Nazis had been building party influence for most of the 1930’s. The Mennonites of the area, having been German only a generation before, welcomed their new part in the Germany of the future, becoming involved in almost every level of the Nazi Party. Otto Andres became the second-highest ranked Nazi of the Danzig area, and scores of the 6,000 believers in the surrounding congregations joined various Nazi organizations. The men often took part in the paramilitary SA and SS, while their wives and daughters took part in corresponding women’s groups. Churches became saturated with active Nazis, even going so far as to accept them into church leadership. At one point, five of the seven local churches were led by active party members.

World War II was the final step in the Mennonites’ integration with the Nazis. The German concentration camp of Stutthof supplied slave labor to numerous Mennonite businesses. Mennonite churches organized war efforts, including recruiting their young men to serve in the German army. In a particularly twisted case, a Mennonite doctor, Johan Klassen, was personally responsible for the deaths of more than one hundred disabled children.

Perhaps the most concerning episode in this dismal tale of backsliding comes after the war. Mennonite leadership, recognizing to some extent the terrible depths to which they had fallen, and noting the justice that was to come through the Nuremburg trials, effectively shrugged the blame from off their shoulders. Appealing to their Mennonite brothers across the ocean, they convinced them of their innocence, twisting their involvement in the Nazi regime to make themselves appear the victims. American Mennonites helped these now-refugees in many ways, providing all manner of assistance, and ultimately keeping most of them from facing possible prison time or death sentences. The surviving German churches eventually disintegrated or emigrated to the Americas.

If a group who originally held beliefs identical to our own could stray to the point of child murder and slave labor, then the question must be asked: “Are we seeing their folly for what it was?” Why did the churches of Danzig accept the advances of what, in retrospect, was a clearly un-biblical, un-Christlike movement?

The origin for their downfall was surprisingly simple. The Mennonites of Germany forgot who their true Ruler was. No earthly kingdom at war tolerates an allegiance to the enemy, and neither does the Kingdom of Heaven. The pride in their earthly kingdom, the pursuit of prestige and power, all led to a foreseeable end. Their salt had lost its savor, and they were cast out and trodden underfoot. This is a cautionary tale of the dangers of an unequal yoking of the church with the world.

Dere er jordens salt. Men hvis saltet mister sin kraft, hva skal det da brukes til? … – Matteus 5:13.

Man kan undre seg over hvorfor anabaptistene, de tidlige kirkefedrene, kirkehistorikerne, og særlig opphavsmannen til vår tro, Kristus selv, inntok en så kraftfull og absolutistisk holdning til at kirke og stat skulle være adskilt. Hvorfor forkynte, skrev og advarte de så enstemmig mot enhver form for politisk engasjement fra kristnes side? Kanskje besvares dette best ved å se på konsekvensene av at kristne ignorerte disse oppriktige advarslene, forkastet sin gudsfryktige troskap og sverget troskap til et mangelfullt og i siste instans forgjeves verdslig rike.

Mennonittene i Tyskland er et særlig interessant og formaningseksempel i kristen og anabaptistisk historie — ikke bare på grunn av deres relative nærhet til vår tid — men også på grunn av deres nesten totale hengivenhet til en verdslig leder og en verdslig sak. Hva førte dem til en så lite kristelig posisjon? En sann forståelse av deres historie må naturlig begynne med deres opprinnelse.

Mennonittene i Tyskland på 1900-tallet stammet fra de første anabaptistgruppene, men i motsetning til våre forfedre ble de i den gamle verden i stedet for å emigrere til den nye verden. Der førte flere faktorer dem til en unik posisjon i verdenshendelsene, en posisjon som skulle sette deres prøvelse på en global scene.

Begynnelsen av 1900-tallet førte til første verdenskrig, som endte med Tysklands og dets alliertes nederlag. De påfølgende fredsavtalene var utformet for å ydmyke og knekke Tyskland, ved å pålegge landet en nesten umulig krigsgjeld og begrense dets rett til å bygge opp et forsvar. Det tyske folk følte seg, ikke overraskende, forulempet i tillegg til at de hadde tapt krigen. Deres harme rådde, og snart kom den til uttrykk i nasjonalistiske bevegelser, den mest fremtredende av disse var Nationalsosialistiske tyske arbeiderparti (eller nazistpartiet). Partiet ble grunnlagt i 1919, og Hitler var blant dets første medlemmer. Han overtok raskt ledelsen og tiltrakk seg tilhengere med sin «oss mot dem»-retorikk og sterke lederskap.

Partiets vekst var beskjeden i tiåret etter grunnleggelsen. I denne perioden formet Hitler nazistene etter sin vilje. Hat mot de fleste ikke-tyske (ariske) grupper ble et sentralt partitema, sammen med en voldsom avsky for kommunismen. Partiet var imidlertid ikke stort nok til å være annet enn en randtale, og representerte bare en liten del av de tyske velgerne.

Betydningsløsheten varte ikke. Den store depresjonen utløste nazistenes vei til makten. Da det globale markedet krasjet, mistet over 2 millioner tyskere jobben. Arbeidsløse samlet de seg rundt den karismatiske ledelsen som lovet dem arbeid, makt, å «gjøre Tyskland stort igjen». Hurtig agerte Hitler og la til legioner av tilhengere.

De tusenvis av nye nazimedlemmer gjorde det mulig for partiet å seriøst konkurrere i mange lokale valg, og i Tysklands parlament kunne de kontrollere nok stemmer til å påvirke politikkutformingen. På lang sikt ga deres politiske tyngde Hitler embetet som statsminister. Etter å ha sikret seg denne posisjonen gikk han videre for å velte den tyske regjeringen og etablerte seg selv og partiet som de ubestridte herskerne i Tyskland.

Hvorfor tiltrakk en slik mann, og en slik bevegelse, oppmerksomheten og tilbedelsen fra en kirke som bekjente mye av det samme som vi gjør? Å elske våre fiender, adskillelse fra verden og ikke-motstand sto ikke i overensstemmelse med nazistenes budskap. Svaret, som for de fleste avfallske kirker, fremstår best som noe som skjedde i små skritt og over tid.

I 1929 kom mennonittene under Tysklands og det raskt voksende nazistpartiets søkelys. 13 000 russiske mennonittflyktninger strømmet til Moskva i håp om å komme seg ut av det kommuniststyrte landet. Nazistene grep situasjonen og brukte mennonittene som antatt bevis på at ariere (folk av tysk avstamning, som mennonittene) ble urettferdig behandlet av resten av verden. Dette bildet ble fremmet av statlige propagandadepartementer, som spredte skrifter, brosjyrer og til og med to enormt populære filmer, som skildret mennonittene som sterke, røde- blodige tyskere som tappert strevde mot den urettferdige undertrykkelsen fra de russiske kommunistene. Disse tiltakene ga flyktningene nasjonal oppmerksomhet, noe som førte til at de ble innrømmet i Tyskland.

Mens mange mennonitter kom inn i Tyskland som flyktninger og på andre måter, fantes det også blomstrende, etablerte menigheter som ble gitt samme patriotiske makeover av nazistenes propagandister. Dessverre ønsket disse kirkene nazistenes oppmerksomhet velkommen, så langt at de sendte Hitler et brev hvor de takket ham for å være «det tyske folks frelser» og avla ham sin støtte til hans regjering. Det er verdt å merke seg at Hitler, en mann travelt opptatt med å styre en fremvoksende stormakt, personlig svarte på dette brevet med et notat hvor han takket kirkene for deres støtte og uttrykte ønske om videre samarbeid til gagn for både nazistene og mennonittene. Kirken svekket seg ytterligere under disse tilsynelatende gunstige relasjonene.

Et særlig sjokkerende tilfelle av mennonittisk politisk engasjement kom fra kirkene i eller rundt Danzig. Danzig og det omkringliggende landskapet hadde lenge vært en del av det tyske riket, inntil slutten av første verdenskrig, da regionen ble skilt fra Tyskland og i realiteten ble en buffersone mellom Tyskland og Polen. I 1939 gjorde Hitler et av sine første europeiske fremstøt ved å annektere Danzig, hvor nazistene hadde bygget partiinfluenser gjennom mesteparten av 1930-årene. Mennonittene i området, som bare en generasjon tidligere hadde vært tyskere, ønsket sin nye rolle i fremtidens Tyskland velkommen og ble involvert på nesten alle nivåer i nazistpartiet. Otto Andres ble den nest-høyest rangerte nazisten i Danzig-området, og mange av de 6 000 troende i de omkringliggende menighetene sluttet seg til ulike nazi-organisasjoner. Mennene deltok ofte i de paramilitære SA og SS, mens deres koner og døtre deltok i tilsvarende kvinnegrupper. Kirker ble mettet med aktive nazister, som til og med ble tatt inn i kirkens lederskap. På ett tidspunkt ble fem av de syv lokale kirkene ledet av aktive partimedlemmer.

Andre verdenskrig var det siste skrittet i mennonittenes integrasjon med nazistene. Den tyske konsentrasjonsleiren Stutthof leverte slavearbeid til mange mennonittiske bedrifter. Mennonittiske kirker organiserte krigsinnsats, inkludert verving av sine unge menn til tjeneste i den tyske hæren. I et særlig forvridd tilfelle var en mennonittisk lege, Johan Klassen, personlig ansvarlig for døden til mer enn hundre funksjonshemmede barn.

Kanskje det mest bekymringsfulle av denne dystre fortellingen om frafall skjer etter krigen. Mennonittisk lederskap, som til en viss grad innså hvor dypt de hadde sunket, og som la merke til rettferdigheten som skulle komme gjennom Nürnberg-prosessene, ristet effektivt av seg skylden. Ved å appellere til sine mennonittiske brødre på den andre siden av havet overbeviste de dem om sin uskyld og vridde deres engasjement i naziregimet slik at de framsto som ofre. Amerikanske mennonitter hjalp disse nå-flyktningene på mange måter, ga all slags bistand og hindret til slutt at de fleste av dem møtte mulig fengsling eller dødsdom. De overlevende tyske kirkene brøt etter hvert sammen eller utvandret til Amerika.

Hvis en gruppe som opprinnelig holdt tro identisk med vår kunne vandre så langt bort at de begikk barne-drap og brukte slavearbeid, må spørsmålet stilles: «Ser vi deres villfarelse for hva den var?» Hvorfor godtok kirkene i Danzig fremskrittet fra det som, i ettertid, tydelig var en ubibelsk, ukristelig bevegelse?

Årsaken til deres fall var overraskende enkel. Mennonittene i Tyskland glemte hvem deres sanne Hersker var. Intet jordisk rike i krig tåler troskap til fienden, og det gjør heller ikke himmelriket. Stoltheten over deres jordiske rike, jakten på prestisje og makt, førte alle til en forutsigbar slutt. Deres salt hadde mistet sin kraft, og det ble kastet bort og tråkket under fot. Dette er en formaning om farene ved en ulikt hemmet sammenslåing mellom kirke og verden.
